definition: Not conspicuous or attracting attention; modest in appearance or behaviour.
explanationBg: Който не се набива на очи и не привлича внимание — стои настрана, тихо и скромно.
explanationEn: Staying quiet and not attracting attention; easy not to notice.
exampleEn: The new student was so unobtrusive that half the class didn't notice her for a week.
mnemonicBg: „Ън-ъб-ТРУ-сив“ — представи си мишле, което се промъква покрай стената така тихо, че никой не го забелязва.
bookSentenceEn: Hobbits are an **unobtrusive** but very ancient people, more numerous formerly than they are today; for they love peace and quiet and good tilled earth: a well-ordered and wellfarmed countryside was their favourite haunt.

definition: To prepare and cultivate land for crops by ploughing and harrowing.
explanationBg: Да обработваш земя — да я ореш и разкопаваш, за да я подготвиш за засаждане на култури.
explanationEn: To prepare land for growing crops by ploughing it.
exampleEn: Every spring my grandfather tills the small field behind his house before planting tomatoes.
mnemonicBg: Звучи точно като „тил“: дядо оре нивата приведен, а слънцето му напича тила.
bookSentenceEn: Hobbits are an unobtrusive but very ancient people, more numerous formerly than they are today; for they love peace and quiet and good **tilled** earth: a well-ordered and wellfarmed countryside was their favourite haunt.

definition: A place frequently visited by a particular person or kind of person.
explanationBg: Място, където някой постоянно се навърта и обича да прекарва времето си — нещо като негова лична територия.
explanationEn: A place that someone visits very often and loves to spend time in.
exampleEn: The little café near school is our favourite haunt after exams.
mnemonicBg: Haunt значи и „бродя като призрак“: представи си призрак, който всяка вечер цъфва в любимото си кафене — то е неговото свърталище.
bookSentenceEn: Hobbits are an unobtrusive but very ancient people, more numerous formerly than they are today; for they love peace and quiet and good tilled earth: a well-ordered and wellfarmed countryside was their favourite **haunt**.

definition: A bellows used at a forge to blow air onto a fire and intensify the heat.
explanationBg: Голямо духало в ковачница, с което се вкарва въздух в огъня, за да се разпали още по-силно.
explanationEn: A tool that blows air into a blacksmith's fire to make it hotter.
exampleEn: At the craft museum we took turns pumping the forge-bellows until the coals glowed orange.
mnemonicBg: Bellow ≈ „бълвам“: духалото бълва въздух в ковашкото огнище и пламъците лумват.
bookSentenceEn: They do not and did not understand or like machines more complicated than a **forge-bellows**, a water-mill, or a hand-loom, though they were skilful with tools.

definition: A loom worked by hand rather than mechanically, used for weaving cloth.
explanationBg: Тъкачен стан, който се задвижва само с ръце, без машина — на такива са тъкали платове едно време.
explanationEn: A weaving machine worked by hand instead of by a motor.
exampleEn: In craft class we wove bookmarks on a small hand-loom, and mine came out hilariously crooked.
mnemonicBg: HAND = ръка: представи си баба пред дървения стан — совалката снове напред-назад: лум, лум, ЛУМ!
bookSentenceEn: They do not and did not understand or like machines more complicated than a forge-bellows, a water-mill, or a **hand-loom**, though they were skilful with tools.

definition: Skilful and quick, especially with the hands; neat and dexterous.
explanationBg: Сръчен и бърз, най-вече с ръцете — прави всичко леко, точно и без излишно пипкане.
explanationEn: Quick and skilful, especially with your hands.
exampleEn: With a few deft moves she solved the Rubik's cube in under a minute.
mnemonicBg: Кратка дума като бързо движение: „фът!“ — деФТ ръце правят фокуса за секунда.
bookSentenceEn: They are quick of hearing and sharp-eyed, and though they are inclined to be fat and do not hurry unnecessarily, they are nonetheless nimble and **deft** in their movements.

definition: Acting in a clumsy and careless way, making mistakes.
explanationBg: Който се движи и действа тромаво и небрежно — блъска се, събаря и постоянно обърква нещо.
explanationEn: Acting in a clumsy, careless way and making mistakes.
exampleEn: Our blundering goalkeeper tripped over the ball and let in the easiest goal of the season.
mnemonicBg: БЛЪНдъринг ≈ „блъскам“: представи си някой, който се блъска във всяка маса по пътя си и събаря чашите.
bookSentenceEn: 2 prologue possessed from the ﬁrst the art of disappearing swiftly and silently, when large folk whom they do not wish to meet come **blundering** by; and this art they have developed until to Men it may seem magical.

definition: The quality of being difficult to find, catch, or describe.
explanationBg: Качеството на нещо да е трудно за хващане, намиране или описване — все ти се изплъзва в последния момент.
explanationEn: The quality of being hard to find, catch, or describe.
exampleEn: The elusiveness of the stray cat drove us crazy — every time we got close, it vanished.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „и-ЛУ-сив“ — почти като ИЛЮЗИЯ: посягаш да я докоснеш, а тя се изпарява.
bookSentenceEn: But Hobbits have never, in fact, studied magic of any kind, and their **elusiveness** is due solely to a professional skill that heredity and practice, and a close friendship with the earth, have rendered inimitable by bigger and clumsier races.

definition: So good or unusual as to be impossible to copy; unique.
explanationBg: Толкова добър и единствен по рода си, че никой не може да го имитира или повтори.
explanationEn: So special or good that nobody can copy it.
exampleEn: Everyone tried to copy her inimitable laugh, but nobody came close.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие IMITATE (имитирам) с „не“ отпред: не-имитируем — пробвай да го копираш, няма да стане.
bookSentenceEn: But Hobbits have never, in fact, studied magic of any kind, and their elusiveness is due solely to a professional skill that heredity and practice, and a close friendship with the earth, have rendered **inimitable** by bigger and clumsier races.

definition: Rather fat or of heavy build; also sturdy and resolute.
explanationBg: Едър и набит, със здраво телосложение; казва се и за човек, който е твърд и не се огъва.
explanationEn: Quite heavily built and strong; also firm and brave.
exampleEn: The stout little wrestler surprised everyone by pinning the tallest guy in the tournament.
mnemonicBg: STOut: чичо на СТО кила, як като дъб — събори го, ако можеш.
bookSentenceEn: For they are a little people, smaller than Dwarves: less **stout** and stocky, that is, even when they are not actually much shorter.

definition: To diminish gradually in size, amount, or strength.
explanationBg: Да намаляваш постепенно — малко по малко, докато почти се стопиш.
explanationEn: To become smaller or weaker little by little.
exampleEn: My phone battery dwindled to three percent before the bus finally came.
mnemonicBg: Представи си чертичките на батерията, които гаснат една по една: дуин-дъл… дуин-дъл… 3%.
bookSentenceEn: They seldom now reach three feet; but they have **dwindled**, they say, and in ancient days they were taller.

definition: The undersides of the feet or of footwear that touches the ground.
explanationBg: Долната част на ходилата или на обувките — това, което стъпва по земята.
explanationEn: The bottom parts of your feet or of your shoes.
exampleEn: After the festival my soles ached from dancing all day in flat sneakers.
mnemonicBg: Sole звучи като „сол“: стъпваш бос върху разсипана сол и я усещаш точно със стъпалата.
bookSentenceEn: They dressed in bright colours, being notably fond of yellow and green; but they seldom wore shoes, since their feet had tough leathery **soles** and were clad in a thick curling hair, much like the hair of their heads, which was commonly brown.

definition: Appropriate or suitable in the circumstances; inclined or likely to do something.
explanationBg: Уместен, точно на място за дадената ситуация; също и склонен често да прави нещо.
explanationEn: Suitable for the situation, or likely to do something.
exampleEn: Her nickname for our coach was so apt that the whole team started using it.
mnemonicBg: АПТ като АПТека: точното лекарство за точния момент — apt!
bookSentenceEn: Their faces were as a rule good-natured rather than beautiful, broad, bright-eyed, red-cheeked, with mouths **apt** to laughter, and to eating and drinking.

definition: A thing said or done for amusement; a joke or witty remark.
explanationBg: Шега, закачка или остроумна реплика — нещо казано на майтап, а не на сериозно.
explanationEn: A joke or something said for fun.
exampleEn: He said it in jest, but half the class actually believed school was cancelled.
mnemonicBg: Jest звучи като „жест“: клоунът прави смешен жест и пуска шега.
bookSentenceEn: And laugh they did, and eat, and drink, often and heartily, being fond of simple **jests** at all times, and of six meals a day (when they could get them).

definition: The state of being no longer on friendly terms with someone; alienation.
explanationBg: Когато двама близки се отдалечат и спрат да си говорят — между тях става хладно и чуждо.
explanationEn: When people who were close are no longer friendly with each other.
exampleEn: After years of estrangement, the two sisters finally talked again at a family wedding.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие STRANGE (странен, чужд): близкият човек изведнъж ти става чужд.
bookSentenceEn: It is plain indeed that in spite of later **estrangement** Hobbits are relatives of ours: far nearer to us than Elves, or even than Dwarves.

definition: Relating to the study or tracing of family descent and ancestry.
explanationBg: Свързан с родословието — с проследяването кой от кого произхожда: родители, баби, прадядовци и така назад.
explanationEn: Connected with the history of a family and its ancestors.
exampleEn: For a school project she drew a genealogical chart going back to her great-great-grandparents.
mnemonicBg: ГЕНИ + ЛОГИКА: науката, която подрежда гените на рода в едно голямо семейно дърво.
bookSentenceEn: A love of learning (other than **genealogical** lore) was far from general among them, but there remained still a few in the older families who studied their own books, and even gathered reports of old times and distant lands from Elves, Dwarves, and Men.

definition: Towards the west; in a western direction.
explanationBg: В посока на запад — натам, накъдето залязва слънцето.
explanationEn: Going or facing towards the west.
exampleEn: We cycled westward along the coast so we could watch the sunset.
mnemonicBg: Каубоите от УЕСТърните винаги яздят към залеза — все westward, все на запад.
bookSentenceEn: They moved **westward** early, and roamed over Eriador as far as Weathertop while the others were still in Wilderland.

definition: The part of a roof that meets or overhangs the walls of a building.
explanationBg: Краищата на покрива, които стърчат навън над стените — под тях се скриваш при дъжд.
explanationEn: The edges of a roof that stick out over the walls.
exampleEn: We sheltered under the eaves of the gym until the rain stopped.
mnemonicBg: Оттук идва eavesdrop („подслушвам“) — все едно стоиш под стрехата на съседа и слушаш какво си говорят вътре.
bookSentenceEn: Their earliest tales seem to glimpse a time when they dwelt in the upper vales of Anduin, between the **eaves** of Greenwood the Great and the Misty Mountains.

definition: Full of danger or risk; very dangerous.
explanationBg: Пълен с опасности и рискове — едно невнимание и можеш да пострадаш.
explanationEn: Very dangerous and full of risk.
exampleEn: The hike turned perilous near the peak, where the path was just loose rocks and wind.
mnemonicBg: PERILous ≈ „перила“: перила слагат точно там, където без тях е опасно.
bookSentenceEn: Why they later undertook the hard and **perilous** crossing of the mountains into Eriador is no longer certain.

definition: To live in or at a specified place; to reside.
explanationBg: Да живееш на дадено място, да го обитаваш — по-книжна дума за „живея“.
explanationEn: To live in a place.
exampleEn: An old fisherman dwells in the wooden cabin by the lake all year round.
mnemonicBg: В думата се крие WELL (кладенец): представи си жабче, което си живее на дъното на кладенеца — d-WELL-ва си там.
bookSentenceEn: They passed over the Bridge of Stonebows, that had been built in the days of the power of the North Kingdom, and they took all the land beyond to **dwell** in, between the river and the Far Downs.

definition: The leader of a people, clan, or tribe.
explanationBg: Водачът на племе, род или клан — главният, чиято дума се слуша.
explanationEn: The leader of a tribe or clan.
exampleEn: In our strategy game, the chieftain decides when the whole clan attacks.
mnemonicBg: CHIEF го знаеш — шеф, главатар; добави „-tain“ и става вожд на цяло племе.
bookSentenceEn: While there was still a king they were in name his subjects, but they were, in fact, ruled by their own **chieftains** and meddled not at all with events in the world outside.

definition: Before (archaic or literary).
explanationBg: Старинна дума за „преди“ — ще я срещнеш в стари книги, балади и приказки, не в днешния говор.
explanationEn: An old word that means 'before'.
exampleEn: My grandfather loves old-fashioned phrases like 'Be home ere dark, young lady!'
mnemonicBg: Произнася се „еър“ като air (въздух): преди да се гмурнеш, гълташ въздух — ere = преди.
bookSentenceEn: There was room and to spare for incomers, and **ere** long the Hobbits began to settle in ordered communities.

definition: A tract of open uncultivated upland, typically covered with heather.
explanationBg: Дива, гола пустош по възвишенията — необработвана земя, обрасла с пирен и ниски храсти, често брулена от вятър.
explanationEn: A wild open area of high land with low bushes and no farms.
exampleEn: Our camping group crossed a windy moor where nothing grew taller than our knees.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „мор“: пустош, в която сякаш всичко е измряло — само вятърът свисти из храстите.
bookSentenceEn: Forty leagues it stretched from the Far Downs to the Brandywine Bridge, and ﬁfty from the northern **moors** to the marshes in the south.

definition: An area of low-lying land that is flooded in wet seasons and remains waterlogged.
explanationBg: Ниска земя край вода, която при дъжд се залива и стои постоянно подгизнала — истинско блато, в което затъваш.
explanationEn: Low wet land that floods and stays soggy.
exampleEn: We lost our football in the marsh behind the pitch, and nobody dared go get it.
mnemonicBg: „Марш през блатото!“ — командват ти, а ти жвакаш в калта: марш-марш, marsh!
bookSentenceEn: Forty leagues it stretched from the Far Downs to the Brandywine Bridge, and ﬁfty from the northern moors to the **marshes** in the south.

definition: Careful attention paid to advice or a warning.
explanationBg: Внимание, което обръщаш на съвет или предупреждение — да се вслушаш истински, а не да го пуснеш покрай ушите си.
explanationEn: Careful attention you pay to advice or a warning.
exampleEn: She paid no heed to the 'wet paint' sign and ruined her favourite white hoodie.
mnemonicBg: „Хийд“ звучи като „чуй де!“ — обърни внимание, де!
bookSentenceEn: prologue 7 they **heeded** less and less the world outside where dark things moved, until they came to think that peace and plenty were the rule in Middle-earth and the right of all sensible folk.

definition: A phrase meaning the weather has become less harsh or warmer than before.
explanationBg: Израз, с който казваме, че времето е омекнало — не е вече толкова студено и сурово, колкото беше.
explanationEn: A phrase meaning the weather has become warmer and less harsh.
exampleEn: Now that the weather has grown milder, we finally moved our basketball games back outside.
mnemonicBg: MILD ≈ „мил“: времето е станало по-мило с теб — маха ледения вятър и ти праща слънчице.

definition: Extremely hungry and seeking prey; voracious.
explanationBg: Подивял от глад и хукнал да търси плячка — ненаситен като звяр.
explanationEn: Extremely hungry and hunting for food.
exampleEn: After swim practice we attacked the pizza like a pack of ravening wolves.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е RAVEN (гарван): ято изгладнели гарвани се спуска и помита всичко за секунди.
bookSentenceEn: Even the weathers had grown milder, and the wolves that had once come **ravening** out of the North in bitter white winters were now only a grandfather’s tale.

definition: The floors or surfaces of fireplaces; symbolically, the homes themselves.
explanationBg: Каменните площадки на камините, върху които гори огънят; преносно — самите домове и домашната топлина.
explanationEn: The floors of fireplaces; often a symbol for home.
exampleEn: The mountain lodge had two huge hearths, and we played cards beside them every evening.
mnemonicBg: В HEARTH се крие HEART (сърце): огнището е сърцето на дома.
bookSentenceEn: So, though there was still some store of weapons in the Shire, these were used mostly as trophies, hanging above **hearths** or on walls, or gathered into the museum at Michel Delving.

definition: In Hobbit-speech, anything they have no immediate use for but are unwilling to throw away.
explanationBg: Така хобитите от книгата наричат вещ, която за нищо не им трябва, но не им дава сърце да я изхвърлят.
explanationEn: A thing you never use but cannot make yourself throw away.
exampleEn: My drawer is full of mathoms: broken earphones, old keychains, and a fidget spinner I never spin.
mnemonicBg: Гледаш вещта, казваш „хъм… може да потрябва“ — и матомът се връща в чекмеджето за още десет години.
bookSentenceEn: Their dwellings were apt to become rather crowded with **mathoms**, and many of the presents that passed from hand to hand were of that sort.

definition: In a tireless manner; without growing weary.
explanationBg: Неуморно — без да спираш и без да ти пада енергията, все едно умората не те хваща.
explanationEn: Without ever getting tired.
exampleEn: She practised the same dance move unwearyingly until it looked effortless.
mnemonicBg: UN (не) + WEARY (уморен): като робот-прахосмукачка, която бръмчи ли, бръмчи без почивка.
bookSentenceEn: They were, if it came to it, difﬁcult to daunt or to kill; and they were, perhaps, so **unwearyingly** fond of good things not least because they could, when put to it, do without them, and could survive rough handling by grief, foe, or weather in a way that astonished those…

definition: Brave and persistent (often used humorously or in archaic tone).
explanationBg: Смел и упорит, който не се предава — старовремска дума, днес често казвана с лека усмивка.
explanationEn: Brave and never giving up; an old-fashioned, often playful word.
exampleEn: Our doughty little defender kept chasing every ball even when we were losing five-nil.
mnemonicBg: „Дау-ти“ звучи като „Давай, ти!“ — викаш на смелчагата, а той пак се хвърля напред.
bookSentenceEn: Though slow to quarrel, and for sport killing nothing that lived, they were **doughty** at bay, and at need could still handle arms.

definition: A place of residence; a house or home (formal or literary).
explanationBg: Книжна, малко тържествена дума за дом или жилище — мястото, където живееш.
explanationEn: A formal word for the place where someone lives.
exampleEn: 'Welcome to my humble abode,' he joked, opening the door to his messy room.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „а, боде!“: сядаш върху изскочила пружина на дивана — боде, ама пак е сладко: дом си е.
bookSentenceEn: All Hobbits had originally lived in holes in the ground, or so they believed, and in such dwellings they still felt most at home; but in the course of time they had been obliged to adopt other forms of **abode**.

definition: To form branches or subdivisions; to spread out into branches.
explanationBg: Да се разклоняваш — от едно начало да тръгват все нови и нови клончета и посоки.
explanationEn: To split and spread out like branches.
exampleEn: Our group chat ramified into five smaller chats — one for homework, one for memes, and three for drama.
mnemonicBg: Представи си дърво с РАМЕне, от които израстват клони на всички страни — РАМИ-фай.
bookSentenceEn: But suitable sites for these large and **ramifying** tunnels (or smials as they called them) were not everywhere to be found; and in the ﬂats and the low-lying districts the Hobbits, as they multiplied, began to build above ground.

definition: A hobbit-hole; a burrow-like dwelling dug into a hillside (Tolkien usage).
explanationBg: Дума на Толкин за уютно жилище, изкопано навътре в хълм — като дупка-къща с топли подземни стаи.
explanationEn: A cosy home dug into a hillside, like a burrow with rooms.
exampleEn: If I could dig a smial into the hill behind our house, I'd move my whole gaming setup inside.
mnemonicBg: Пише се почти като SMILE: вратата на дупката в хълма е кръгла и извита като усмивка.
bookSentenceEn: But suitable sites for these large and ramifying tunnels (or **smials** as they called them) were not everywhere to be found; and in the ﬂats and the low-lying districts the Hobbits, as they multiplied, began to build above ground.

definition: A young child’s one-piece outer garment combining shirt and shorts.
explanationBg: Бебешко гащеризонче от едно парче — блузка и панталонки, съшити заедно, за игра и лазене.
explanationEn: A one-piece outfit for a baby or small child.
exampleEn: In the old album there's a photo of my brother in yellow rompers, covered in spaghetti.
mnemonicBg: Бебе марширува из хола: „ром-пом-пом!“ — с ROM-pers, гащеризончето за лудории.

definition: A person whose job is to make and repair carts and wagons.
explanationBg: Майстор, който прави и поправя каруци и талиги — стар занаят от времето преди колите.
explanationEn: A person who makes and repairs carts and wagons.
exampleEn: At the open-air museum a cartwright showed us how wooden cart wheels are fitted together.
mnemonicBg: CART (каруца) + WRIGHT (майстор) — помисли за братя Райт: те майсторили самолети, а cartwright майстори каруци.
bookSentenceEn: These were specially favoured by millers, smiths, ropers, and **cartwrights**, and others of that sort; for even when they had holes to live in, Hobbits had long been accustomed to build sheds and workshops.

definition: A simple roofed structure used for storage or shelter.
explanationBg: Малка постройка в двора — барака или навес, където се прибират инструменти, колела и какво ли не.
explanationEn: A small simple building for storing things.
exampleEn: We turned the old garden shed into a tiny studio for recording songs.
mnemonicBg: „Шед“ ≈ „шетам“: дядо по цял ден шета из бараката и реди чукове, пирони и стари колела.
bookSentenceEn: These were specially favoured by millers, smiths, ropers, and cartwrights, and others of that sort; for even when they had holes to live in, Hobbits had long been accustomed to build **sheds** and workshops.

definition: Walking slowly and with effort, as if the legs are weighted; sluggish.
explanationBg: С натежали крака — движиш се бавно и с усилие, сякаш влачиш тежести на глезените.
explanationEn: Moving slowly, as if your legs are very heavy.
exampleEn: By the last lap of the cross-country race I was heavy-legged and barely jogging.
mnemonicBg: HEAVY (тежки) + LEGS (крака): денят след тренировка за крака — слизаш по стълбите като ръждясал робот.
bookSentenceEn: The Hobbits of that quarter, the Eastfarthing, were rather large and **heavy-legged**, and they wore dwarf-boots in muddy weather.

definition: A gently rolling hill, especially of chalk grassland in southern England.
explanationBg: Полегат, заоблен тревист хълм — такива меки зелени възвишения има най-вече в Южна Англия.
explanationEn: A gentle grassy hill, especially in southern England.
exampleEn: We flew kites on the down above the village until the wind died.
mnemonicBg: Парадокс за запомняне: DOWN значи „надолу“, а тук е хълм нагоре — изкачваш се по down, за да тичаш после надолу.
bookSentenceEn: But they were well known to be Stoors in a large part of their blood, as indeed was shown by **the down** that many grew on their chins.

definition: Originating in the distant past; very old.
explanationBg: Толкова древен, че никой не помни кога е започнал — началото му се губи в мъглата на времето.
explanationEn: So old that nobody remembers when it began.
exampleEn: Arguing over whose turn it is to wash the dishes is an immemorial tradition in our family.
mnemonicBg: IM- (не) + MEMORY (памет): от „незапомнени времена“ — дотам човешката памет просто не стига.
bookSentenceEn: Three Elf-towers of **immemorial** age were still to be seen on the Tower Hills beyond the western marches.

definition: Feelings of doubt or apprehension about a future event.
explanationBg: Тревожни съмнения дали нещо ще мине добре — онова свито чувство в стомаха: „ами ако е грешка?“
explanationEn: Worried feelings of doubt about what may happen.
exampleEn: I had misgivings about joining the chemistry club, but it turned out to be the best part of my week.
mnemonicBg: MIS (грешно) + GIVING (даване): подаваш подаръка и сърцето ти се свива — „дали не сбърках?“
bookSentenceEn: Most Hobbits regarded even rivers and small boats with deep **misgivings**, and not many of them could swim.

definition: Grass and the surface layer of earth held together by its roots.
explanationBg: Тревата заедно с горния слой пръст, който корените ѝ държат — зеленият „килим“ на двора или стадиона.
explanationEn: Grass with the top layer of soil held together by roots.
exampleEn: By half-time the players' boots had torn big chunks out of the turf.
mnemonicBg: „Търф“ звучи като ТУФА: изскубваш туфа трева с пръстта — и държиш turf в ръка.
bookSentenceEn: The ﬂowers glowed red and golden: snap-dragons and sunﬂowers, and nasturtians trailing all over the **turf** walls and peeping in at the round windows.

definition: Tending to associate closely with one’s own group and exclude others.
explanationBg: Който се събира само със своята групичка или род и не пуска външни хора — затворена компания.
explanationEn: Staying close to your own group and shutting others out.
exampleEn: The seniors at our school are so clannish that they barely talk to anyone younger.
mnemonicBg: От CLAN — като клановете в онлайн игрите: приемат само „своите“, всички други чакат отвън.
bookSentenceEn: 10 prologue **clannish** and reckoned up their relationships with great care.

definition: To drink, especially alcohol; also to absorb ideas or knowledge.
explanationBg: Книжна дума за „пия“; преносно — да попиваш знания и идеи като гъба.
explanationEn: To drink something, or to soak up ideas and knowledge.
exampleEn: On the beach we imbibed litres of lemonade and somehow still felt thirsty.
mnemonicBg: В IMBIBE се крие „биб“ като БИБЕрон: бебето смуче и попива всичко.
bookSentenceEn: 2 Concerning Pipe-weed There is another astonishing thing about Hobbits of old that must be mentioned, an astonishing habit: they **imbibed** or inhaled, through pipes of clay or wood, the smoke of the burning leaves of a herb, which they called pipe-weed or leaf, a variety probably of Nicotiana.

definition: The ancient past, especially the period before the Middle Ages.
explanationBg: Далечната древност — времето на старите цивилизации като Гърция и Рим, преди Средновековието.
explanationEn: The ancient past, especially before the Middle Ages.
exampleEn: Our history teacher makes antiquity sound exciting, full of stories about Greek and Roman teenagers.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш „АНТИКА“ — стара ценна вещ; antiquity е цялата епоха, от която идват антиките.
bookSentenceEn: All that could be discovered about it in **antiquity** was put together by Meriadoc Brandybuck (later Master of Buckland), and since he and the tobacco of the Southfarthing play a part in the history that follows, his remarks in the introduction to his Herblore of the Shire may be quoted.

definition: Surpassing all others; very distinguished in some way.
explanationBg: Който изпъква над всички останали в своята област — пръв сред първите.
explanationEn: Better and more famous than all the others.
exampleEn: She is the pre-eminent sprinter in our region; nobody has beaten her for two years.
mnemonicBg: Чети го „при-ЕМИНЕМ-т“: като Eminem на сцената — изпъкнал пред всички.
bookSentenceEn: It is true that the Took family had long been **pre-eminent**; for the ofﬁce of Thain had passed to them (from the Oldbucks) some centuries before, and the chief Took had borne that title ever since.

definition: An assembly of people, especially one for legal or governmental discussion.
explanationBg: Събрание, на което хората се събират да обсъждат и решават общи въпроси — като старинен народен съвет.
explanationEn: A meeting where people discuss and decide important matters.
exampleEn: Our class held a kind of moot to decide where the end-of-year trip should go.
mnemonicBg: „Муут“ — представи си събор на крави: гласуват с дълго „мууу!“ за всяко решение.
bookSentenceEn: The Thain was the master of the Shiremoot, and captain of the Shire-muster and the Hobbitry-inarms; but as muster and **moot** were only held in times of emergency, which no longer occurred, the Thainship had ceased to be more than a nominal dignity.

definition: A formal gathering of troops, especially for inspection or to prepare for battle.
explanationBg: Сбор на войници на едно място — за проверка, преброяване или подготовка за битка.
explanationEn: A gathering of soldiers for inspection or before battle.
exampleEn: Before announcing the line-up, the coach called a muster of the whole squad on the pitch.
mnemonicBg: МУСтър ≈ МУСкетари: тримата мускетари се строяват за проверка — всички на сбор!
bookSentenceEn: The Thain was the master of the Shiremoot, and captain of the Shire-**muster** and the Hobbitry-inarms; but as muster and moot were only held in times of emergency, which no longer occurred, the Thainship had ceased to be more than a nominal dignity.

definition: The action of calculating or estimating something; settling of accounts.
explanationBg: Пресмятане или преценка — смяташ, теглиш чертата и виждаш какво излиза; понякога значи и разчистване на сметки.
explanationEn: The act of calculating or judging something; settling accounts.
exampleEn: By my reckoning, we need three more wins to reach the playoffs.
mnemonicBg: „РЕКъН-инг“ ≈ „рекох“: дядо смята наум и отсича: „Рекох! Толкова прави.“
bookSentenceEn: With them he set out, to his own lasting astonishment, on a morning of April, it being then the year1341Shire-**reckoning**, on a quest of great treasure, the dwarf-hoards of the Kings under the Mountain, beneath Erebor in Dale, far off in the East.

definition: Stocks or stores of money or valued objects, typically secret or carefully guarded.
explanationBg: Тайни запаси от пари или ценности, които някой трупа и пази ревниво само за себе си.
explanationEn: Secret stores of money or treasures that someone guards.
exampleEn: My little brother keeps hoards of Halloween candy hidden under his bed.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „орди“: цели орди златни монети, струпани тайно в пещерата на дракон.
bookSentenceEn: With them he set out, to his own lasting astonishment, on a morning of April, it being then the year1341Shire-reckoning, on a quest of great treasure, the dwarf-**hoards** of the Kings under the Mountain, beneath Erebor in Dale, far off in the East.

definition: To attack violently; to make a concerted or vigorous effort to defeat or undermine.
explanationBg: Да се нахвърлиш върху някого или нещо — със сила или с упорит натиск, за да го победиш или сломиш. Може да е и с думи, не само с юмруци — например да те „нападнат“ с въпроси.
explanationEn: To attack someone or something with force or great energy.
exampleEn: As soon as I walked in, my little brother assailed me with questions about the match.
mnemonicBg: Assail звучи като „сейл“ (разпродажба) — представи си как тълпата щурмува магазина в секундата, в която почне сейлът.
bookSentenceEn: The party was **assailed** by Orcs in a high pass of the Misty Mountains as they went towards Wilderland; and so it happened that Bilbo was lost for a while in the black orcmines deep under the mountains, and there, as he groped in vain in the dark, he put his hand on a ring, lying on the ﬂoor of a tunnel.

definition: To feel about or search blindly with the hands.
explanationBg: Да търсиш нещо пипнешком — протягаш ръце и опипваш наоколо, защото не виждаш къде е.
explanationEn: To search for something with your hands because you cannot see.
exampleEn: When the lights went out, I had to grope along the wall to find the switch.
mnemonicBg: Grope звучи като „гроб“ — в тъмна като гроб стая опипваш стената, за да намериш ключа на лампата.
bookSentenceEn: The party was assailed by Orcs in a high pass of the Misty Mountains as they went towards Wilderland; and so it happened that Bilbo was lost for a while in the black orcmines deep under the mountains, and there, as he **groped** in vain in the dark, he put his hand on a ring, lying on the ﬂoor of a tunnel.

definition: to be completely confused, puzzled, or at a loss for an answer because a problem or question is too difficult
explanationBg: Когато въпросът е толкова труден, че умът ти блокира — гледаш задачата и просто нямаш никаква идея за отговора.
explanationEn: Completely confused and unable to find the answer.
exampleEn: The last question on the maths test completely stumped me.
mnemonicBg: Stump на английски е „пън“ — когато си stumped, стоиш като пън пред задачата и нищо не ти идва наум.
bookSentenceEn: In the end Bilbo won the game, more by luck (as it seemed) than by wits; for he was **stumped** at last for a riddle to ask, and cried out, as his hand came upon the ring he had picked up and forgotten: What have I got in my pocket?

definition: Covered with or resembling slime; unpleasantly slippery and wet.
explanationBg: Покрит с лепкава слуз — мокър, хлъзгав и неприятен на пипане.
explanationEn: Covered in slime; wet and unpleasantly slippery.
exampleEn: The fish slipped right out of my hands because it was so slimy.
mnemonicBg: Slimy идва от slime — онзи лепкав слайм за мачкане: хлъзгав, лигав и леко гаден.
bookSentenceEn: And Bilbo pressed him to keep his word; for the thought came to him that this **slimy** creature might prove false, even though such promises were held sacred, and of old all but the wickedest things feared to break them.

definition: Serious and immediate danger.
explanationBg: Сериозна опасност, която е съвсем наблизо и заплашва да ти се случи всеки момент.
explanationEn: Serious danger that is very close.
exampleEn: The lifeguard warned us that swimming past the buoys puts you in real peril.
mnemonicBg: Peril звучи като „перило“ — счупено перило на стълбите е чиста опасност.
bookSentenceEn: Just in time Bilbo saw his **peril**, and he ﬂed blindly up the passage away from the water; and once more he was saved by his luck.

definition: With the intention of preventing; for fear that.
translation: да не би, за да не
explanationBg: Книжна думичка, която значи „да не би да“ или „за да не“ — правиш нещо, за да предотвратиш друго, или от страх то да не се случи.
explanationEn: A formal word meaning 'so that something bad does not happen'.
exampleEn: I wrote the homework in my planner at once, lest I forget it by the evening.
mnemonicBg: Представи си баба с вдигнат пръст: „Облечи се, lest настинеш!“ — „да не би да настинеш“.
bookSentenceEn: So it was that Gollum passed him without seeing him, and went to guard the way out, **lest** the ‘thief ’ should escape.

definition: To bring or come to an abrupt stop.
explanationBg: Да спреш рязко или да накараш нещо да спре — движение, игра, разговор: стоп, дотук.
explanationEn: To stop suddenly, or to make something stop.
exampleEn: The referee halted the match when the rain turned into a storm.
mnemonicBg: Halt е като командата „Халт!“ от старите военни филми — всички замръзват на място.
bookSentenceEn: At length they came to a **halt** before an unseen opening that led to the lower gates of the mines, on the eastward side of the mountains.

definition: Above all; mainly or principally.
explanationBg: Главно, преди всичко — когато нещо се дължи най-вече на една причина или важи най-вече за едно нещо.
explanationEn: Mainly; more than anything else.
exampleEn: We won chiefly because our goalkeeper made three incredible saves.
mnemonicBg: Chief значи „шеф“ — chiefly е „главно“: каквото каже шефът, това е главното.

definition: To add as an extra or subordinate part, especially to a document; to take possession of territory.
explanationBg: Да присъединиш нещо към друго като допълнение — например приложение към документ. Казва се и когато държава си присвои чужда територия.
explanationEn: To add something to a bigger thing, or to take control of land.
exampleEn: The older kids tried to annex our half of the pitch during the break.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „анекс“ към договор или сграда — допълнение, което се присъединява към основното.
bookSentenceEn: But **annexed** to it and preserved with it, probably in a single red case, were the three large volumes, bound in red leather, that Bilbo gave to him as a parting gift.

definition: To leave out or exclude (someone or something), either intentionally or forgetfully.
explanationBg: Да пропуснеш или изпуснеш нещо — нарочно или по разсеяност — така че то да липсва.
explanationEn: To leave something out, on purpose or by accident.
exampleEn: I omitted my name from the test paper, and the teacher almost didn't mark it.
mnemonicBg: Omit звучи като „омитам се“ — думата се омита от изречението и я няма: пропусната!
bookSentenceEn: The Thain’s Book was thus the ﬁrst copy made of the Red Book and contained much that was later **omitted** or lost.

definition: A written work dealing formally and systematically with a subject.
explanationBg: Сериозен писмен труд, който разглежда една тема подробно, изчерпателно и по всички правила на науката.
explanationEn: A long, serious piece of writing about one subject.
exampleEn: My essay on gaming got so long and serious that the teacher called it a treatise.
mnemonicBg: Treatise звучи като „три тези“ — научен труд, в който защитаваш цели три тези.
bookSentenceEn: He also wrote a short **treatise** on Old Words and Names in the Shire , showing special interest in discovering the kinship with the language of the Rohirrim of such ‘shire-words’ as mathom and old elements in place names.

definition: Blood relationship; a sharing of characteristics or origins.
explanationBg: Роднинска връзка по кръв — или онова топло усещане за близост, когато с някого си приличате по характер или произход.
explanationEn: A family connection, or a feeling of being similar and close to someone.
exampleEn: I felt an instant kinship with the new girl because we love the same band.
mnemonicBg: Представи си кораб (ship), пълен само с роднини (kin) — цялото родословно дърво на една палуба.
bookSentenceEn: He also wrote a short treatise on Old Words and Names in the Shire , showing special interest in discovering the **kinship** with the language of the Rohirrim of such ‘shire-words’ as mathom and old elements in place names.

definition: A conclusion formed on the basis of incomplete information; conjecture.
explanationBg: Извод, който си правиш при непълна информация — предположение или догадка, а не доказан факт.
explanationEn: A guess based on incomplete information.
exampleEn: Nobody knows why the band split up — everything online is pure conjecture.
mnemonicBg: Чува се „кон“ в началото — представи си кон-гадател, който тегли късметчета: чисто предположение, не факт.

definition: Continuing for a long time or longer than usual; lengthy.
explanationBg: Който продължава дълго — по-дълго от обичайното — и сякаш не иска да свърши.
explanationEn: Lasting a long time, or longer than usual.
exampleEn: After the prolonged summer holidays, waking up at seven felt impossible.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие long (дълъг) — като мач, отишъл в безкрайни продължения.
bookSentenceEn: And if that was not enough for fame, there was also his **prolonged** vigour to marvel at.

definition: Physical strength and good health; effort and energy.
explanationBg: Телесна сила и свежест — енергията и жарта, с които се захващаш за нещо.
explanationEn: Physical strength and energy.
exampleEn: She attacked the drum solo with such vigour that the whole hall shook.
mnemonicBg: Vigour звучи като „вихър“ — енергия, която връхлита като вихрушка.
bookSentenceEn: And if that was not enough for fame, there was also his prolonged **vigour** to marvel at.

definition: Never ending or changing; occurring repeatedly.
explanationBg: Вечен и нескончаем — който не спира и не се променя, или се повтаря отново и отново.
explanationEn: Never ending, or happening again and again.
exampleEn: My phone lives in a perpetual state of low battery.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „перпетуум мобиле“ — вечния двигател, който никога не спира: perpetual.
bookSentenceEn: There were some that shook their heads and thought this was too much of a good thing; it seemed unfair that anyone should possess (apparently) **perpetual** youth as well as (reputedly) inexhaustible wealth.

definition: According to general belief; as is generally said.
explanationBg: Според онова, което се говори — хората смятат, че е така, но никой не го е доказал със сигурност.
explanationEn: According to what people say, but not proved.
exampleEn: The empty house at the end of our street is reputedly haunted.
mnemonicBg: Идва от „репутация“ — каквото мълвата говори: уж, според слуховете.
bookSentenceEn: There were some that shook their heads and thought this was too much of a good thing; it seemed unfair that anyone should possess (apparently) perpetual youth as well as (**reputedly**) inexhaustible wealth.

definition: (Informal/dated) used to express annoyance or to emphasise; also: ran quickly.
explanationBg: Старомодна думичка, с която англичаните изпускат яда си — нещо като нашето „проклет“ или „пуст опустял“. Може да значи и „хукнал, втурнал се“.
explanationEn: An old-fashioned word used to show annoyance; it can also mean 'ran quickly'.
exampleEn: Grandpa spilled his tea and muttered 'dashed nuisance!' before dashing after the cat.
mnemonicBg: Представи си дядо, който разлива чая и виква „Dashed!“ („Проклетия!“), а после хуква (dash) подир котката.
bookSentenceEn: When Bilbo was ninety-nine he adopted Frodo as his heir, and brought him to live at Bag End; and the hopes of the Sackville-Bagginses were ﬁnally **dashed**.

definition: A person fond of making jokes; a habitual joker.
explanationBg: Човек, който обича да пуска шеги и да разсмива всички — роден майтапчия.
explanationEn: A person who loves making jokes.
exampleEn: Marko is the class wag — he can turn the most boring lesson into a comedy show.
mnemonicBg: Wag значи и „махам с опашка“ — шегаджията е като весело куче: влезе ли, настроението скача.
bookSentenceEn: Tongues began to **wag** in Hobbiton and Bywater; and rumour of the coming event travelled all over the Shire.

definition: An elderly man, especially a rustic or old countryman.
explanationBg: Стар човек, дядка — особено възрастен мъж от село, който е видял много и обича да разказва.
explanationEn: An old man, especially one from the countryside.
exampleEn: The old gaffer next door tells us fishing stories every summer.
mnemonicBg: Gaffer звучи като „гаф“ — дядка, който все прави смешни гафове и сам им се смее.
bookSentenceEn: ‘A very nice well-spoken gentlehobbit is Mr. Bilbo, as I’ve always said,’ the **Gaffer** declared.

definition: Points at which parts of a body or structure are joined together; also large cuts of meat for roasting.
explanationBg: Местата, където частите на тялото или на една конструкция се свързват — стави и сглобки. Така се казват и големите парчета месо за печене.
explanationEn: The places where parts of a body or structure connect; also large pieces of meat for roasting.
exampleEn: After the long hike, my knee joints ached for two days.
mnemonicBg: Joint звучи като „джойстик“ — ставата е джойстикът на тялото: върти се, за да движи ръката или крака.
bookSentenceEn: Now that he was himself growing old and stiff in the **joints**, the job was mainly carried on by his youngest son, Sam Gamgee.

definition: Food provisions; victuals (informal/dialect).
explanationBg: Простичка, селска думичка за храна и провизии — каквото има за хапване.
explanationEn: An informal old word for food.
exampleEn: Gran packed our rucksacks with enough vittles for the whole camping weekend.
mnemonicBg: Звучи почти като „витамини“ — бабината дума за ядене: „Сядай, виж какви vittles съм наготвила!“.
bookSentenceEn: And Mr. Drogo was staying at Brandy Hall with his father-in-law, old Master Gorbadoc, as he often did after his marriage (him being partial to his **vittles**, and old Gorbadoc keeping a mighty generous table); and he went out

definition: Left without the means to move from somewhere; abandoned.
explanationBg: Останал някъде без начин да се прибереш — закъсал, зарязан без превоз и без помощ.
explanationEn: Stuck somewhere with no way to leave.
exampleEn: We missed the last bus and were stranded at the mall until Mum rescued us.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е strand (бряг) — корабокрушенец, изхвърлен на брега: заседнал, без лодка и без обхват.
bookSentenceEn: Anyway: there was this Mr. Frodo left an orphan and **stranded**, as you might say, among those queer Bucklanders, being brought up anyhow in Brandy Hall.

definition: A network of interconnecting rabbit burrows; a densely populated or labyrinthine area.
explanationBg: Мрежа от заешки дупки и тунели под земята. Така наричат и място, заплетено като лабиринт — тесни улички, коридори и проходи.
explanationEn: A network of rabbit tunnels, or a place with many confusing passages.
exampleEn: The old school building is a warren of corridors where new students always get lost.
mnemonicBg: Представи си заек на име Уорън, който копае тунел след тунел, докато дворът стане лабиринт.
bookSentenceEn: A regular **warren**, by all accounts.

definition: The action of treading on and crushing something.
explanationBg: Да тъпчеш нещо с крака и да го мачкаш — да го изпогазиш.
explanationEn: To step on something heavily and crush it.
exampleEn: The fans rushed the field and nearly trampled the flower beds by the gate.
mnemonicBg: Trample звучи като „трамбовам“ — тъпчеш и мачкаш с крака, все едно трамбоваш пръст.
bookSentenceEn: a long-expected party 31 had me up at Bag End helping him to keep folks from **trampling** and trapessing all over the garden while the sale was on.

definition: To walk or move wearily or reluctantly over a long distance.
explanationBg: Да се влачиш дълго пеша — уморено и без капка желание, а краката ти се тътрят сами.
explanationEn: To walk somewhere slowly and tiredly, without wanting to.
exampleEn: We traipsed around the shopping centre for hours looking for one pair of trainers.
mnemonicBg: Чуй звука „трррейпс“ — чехли, които се влачат по пода: тътрене без капчица желание.

definition: Looking or sounding bizarre or unfamiliar; strange and unfamiliar.
explanationBg: Толкова странен и необичаен на вид или на звучене, че изглежда дошъл от друг свят — чудат.
explanationEn: Very strange and unusual.
exampleEn: He showed up with such an outlandish haircut that the whole class went silent.
mnemonicBg: Буквално „извън земята“ (out + land) — толкова чудато, сякаш е паднало от друга планета.
bookSentenceEn: And look at the **outlandish** folk that visit him: dwarves coming at night, and that old wandering conjuror, Gandalf, and all.

definition: A person who performs magic tricks; an entertainer.
explanationBg: Фокусник — артист, който прави фокуси и магически трикове пред публика.
explanationEn: A person who performs magic tricks.
exampleEn: The conjuror at my cousin's party pulled a coin from behind my ear.
mnemonicBg: Звучи почти като „жонгльор“ — само че вместо да жонглира, вади зайци от шапката: фокусник.
bookSentenceEn: And look at the outlandish folk that visit him: dwarves coming at night, and that old wandering **conjuror**, Gandalf, and all.

definition: A garden plant with round leaves and bright orange, yellow, or red flowers.
explanationBg: Градинско цвете с кръгли листа и ярки оранжеви, жълти или червени цветове — на български му казваме латинка.
explanationEn: A garden plant with round leaves and bright orange, yellow, or red flowers.
exampleEn: We planted nasturtiums along the fence, and by July the yard glowed orange.
mnemonicBg: Чува се „нас тършува“ — баба тършува из лехата с латинки и кичи салатата с оранжевите им (ядливи!) цветчета.
bookSentenceEn: These ‘corrections’ include the altering of dwarves to dwarfs, elvish to elﬁsh , further to farther, nasturtians to **nasturtiums**, try and say to try to say and (‘worst of all’ to Tolkien) elven to elﬁn .

definition: A plant with two-lipped flowers that open and shut like a mouth when squeezed.
explanationBg: Цвете, чиито цветчета имат две „устни“ — стиснеш ли ги леко, отварят се и се затварят като устичка. На български: лъвска уста.
explanationEn: A flower that opens and shuts like a small mouth when you squeeze it.
exampleEn: Grandma showed me how to squeeze a snapdragon so it opens like a tiny mouth.
mnemonicBg: Буквално „щракащ дракон“ (snap + dragon) — стиснеш ли цветчето, то отваря уста като малко змейче.

definition: A raw material or primary agricultural product that can be bought and sold.
explanationBg: Стока — суровина или земеделски продукт, които се купуват и продават: жито, кафе, памук, петрол.
explanationEn: A product or raw material that people buy and sell.
exampleEn: In economics class we learned that coffee is one of the world's most traded commodities.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „комод“ — представи си пазар, където се търгуват комоди, жито и кафе: все стоки.
bookSentenceEn: There might have been some grumbling about ‘dealing locally’, but that very week orders began to pour out of Bag End for every kind of provision, **commodity**, or luxury that could be obtained in Hobbiton or Bywater or anywhere in the neighbourhood.

definition: A thing added to something else in order to complete or enhance it.
explanationBg: Добавка — нещо, което слагаш към друго, за да го допълни или подобри.
explanationEn: Something added to another thing to complete or improve it.
exampleEn: Coach says protein bars are a supplement, not a replacement for real meals.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „суплементите“ на фитнес маниаците — добавка към храненето, не замяна.
bookSentenceEn: A draught of cooks, from every inn and eating-house for miles around, arrived to **supplement** the dwarves and other odd folk that were quartered at Bag End.

definition: Of various kinds; several; miscellaneous.
explanationBg: Разни и всякакви — сбирщина от различни неща, всяко от своя порода.
explanationEn: Of various different kinds.
exampleEn: My backpack holds sundry treasures: chargers, gum, three pens and one mystery sock.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като sundae — сладолед с „всичко отгоре“: разни и всякакви неща наведнъж.
bookSentenceEn: He gave away presents to all and **sundry** – the latter were those who went out again by a back way and came in again by the gate.

definition: A short break for refreshment, typically with a snack, taken at about eleven o’clock.
explanationBg: Кратка почивка за похапване около единайсет сутринта — чай, бисквитки, нещо дребно. Много британски навик!
explanationEn: A small snack break at about eleven in the morning.
exampleEn: At summer camp we always stopped for elevenses — juice and biscuits before the big hike.
mnemonicBg: Eleven е 11 — в единайсет коремът звъни като звънец за междучасие: време за чай и бисквитки.
bookSentenceEn: At other times there were merely lots of people eating and drinking – continuously from **elevenses** until six-thirty, when the ﬁreworks started.

definition: Small firework devices that burn with a hissing sound before exploding.
explanationBg: Малки фойерверки, които съскат и свистят, преди да изпукат.
explanationEn: Small fireworks that hiss before they bang.
exampleEn: On New Year's Eve we heard squibs hissing and popping all over the park.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „с-с-скуиб!“ — съскането на малка пиратка, която свисти, пуква и угасва.
bookSentenceEn: But there was also a generous distribution of **squibs**, crackers, backarappers, sparklers, torches, dwarf-candles, elffountains, goblin-barkers and thunder-claps.

definition: Cardboard tubes with a small explosive charge that bang when pulled, also small fireworks.
explanationBg: Картонени тръбички с мъничък заряд, които гръмват, когато двама ги дръпнат от двете страни — английска коледна традиция. Може да значи и малки пиратки.
explanationEn: Cardboard tubes that bang when two people pull them; also small fireworks.
exampleEn: We pulled crackers at Christmas dinner and everyone wore the silly paper crowns.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „крекери“, но тези не се ядат — дръпваш тръбичката и БУМ: отвътре пада хартиена коронка.
bookSentenceEn: But there was also a generous distribution of squibs, **crackers**, backarappers, sparklers, torches, dwarf-candles, elffountains, goblin-barkers and thunder-claps.

definition: A type of small firework (Tolkien usage; in the book they are noisy crackers).
explanationBg: Рядка старовремска дума за дребни шумни пиратки, които гърмят с пукот една след друга — ще я срещнеш почти само в книгата.
explanationEn: Small noisy firecrackers.
exampleEn: The neighbours set off backrapers after the final, and our dog hid under the bed.
mnemonicBg: Пиратка, която гръмва зад гърба (back) ти — и ти подскачаш до тавана.

definition: A crashing sound of thunder; a sudden loud noise like thunder.
explanationBg: Трясъкът на гръмотевица — или внезапен оглушителен звук, който прилича на гръм.
explanationEn: The loud crash of thunder, or a sudden noise like it.
exampleEn: A sudden thunderclap made the whole class jump in the middle of the test.
mnemonicBg: Буквално thunder + clap: небето „плясва с ръце“ — и всички подскачат.

definition: Sparkling or shining brightly; brilliantly and excitingly clever.
explanationBg: Който искри и блести ярко. За разговор или изпълнение — блестящ, остроумен и увлекателен.
explanationEn: Sparkling brightly; also brilliantly clever and exciting.
exampleEn: Lunch with her is never boring — the conversation is always scintillating.
mnemonicBg: Чува се „синтезатор“ — клавиши, от които при всяко докосване изхвърчат искри.
bookSentenceEn: There were rockets like a ﬂight of **scintillating** birds singing with sweet voices.

definition: Of the most impressive or splendid kind; excellent.
explanationBg: Превъзходен, великолепен — от най-впечатляващия, най-добрия вид.
explanationEn: Extremely good; excellent.
exampleEn: Her free kick in the final was absolutely superb.
mnemonicBg: Това е „супер“ с бонус „б“ накрая — супер с черешка отгоре: великолепно.
bookSentenceEn: They were all **superb**.

definition: A body of troops or police officers in close formation; a group standing together.
explanationBg: Плътен строй от войници или полицаи, наредени рамо до рамо — група хора, застанали като стена.
explanationEn: A group of people standing close together in a tight formation.
exampleEn: A phalanx of security guards stood between the fans and the stage.
mnemonicBg: На български също е „фаланга“ — спартанци, залепени щит до щит като жива стена.
bookSentenceEn: There were fountains of butterﬂies that ﬂew glittering into the trees; there were pillars of coloured ﬁres that rose and turned into eagles, or sailing ships, or a **phalanx** of ﬂying swans; there was a red thunderstorm and a shower of yellow rain; there was a forest of silver spears that sprang suddenly into the air with a yell like an embattled…

definition: Engaged in or prepared for a battle; beset with problems or difficulties.
explanationBg: Който е в битка или е готов за бой. В по-широк смисъл — притиснат отвсякъде от проблеми и трудности.
explanationEn: Fighting in a battle, or surrounded by many problems.
exampleEn: Our embattled goalkeeper faced shot after shot but never gave up.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие battle (битка) — играч, срещу когото тича целият противников отбор.
bookSentenceEn: …phalanx of ﬂying swans; there was a red thunderstorm and a shower of yellow rain; there was a forest of silver spears that sprang suddenly into the air with a yell like an **embattled** army, and came down again into the Water with a hiss like a hundred hot snakes.

definition: To a great extent; extremely.
explanationBg: Извънредно, страшно много — в най-висока степен.
explanationEn: Very much; extremely.
exampleEn: The new level is exceedingly hard — nobody at school has beaten it yet.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е exceed („надхвърлям“) — стрелка, която минава червената черта на скоростомера.
bookSentenceEn: And there was also one last surprise, in honour of Bilbo, and it startled the hobbits **exceedingly**, as Gandalf intended.

definition: The highest point of a hill or mountain; the peak.
explanationBg: Най-високата точка на хълм или планина — самият връх.
explanationEn: The very top of a mountain or hill.
exampleEn: We reached the summit just before sunrise, and the view was unreal.
mnemonicBg: Сещаш се за „самит“ — срещата „на върха“: summit е буквално върхът, най-високата точка.
bookSentenceEn: It shaped itself like a mountain seen in the distance, and began to glow at the **summit**.

definition: An acrobatic movement in which a person turns head over heels.
explanationBg: Акробатично премятане през глава — салто или кълбо напред или назад.
explanationEn: A movement in which you roll head over heels.
exampleEn: She landed a perfect somersault off the diving board and everyone cheered.
mnemonicBg: Чуваш ли „салто“ накрая (somer-SAULT)? — лятно салто на батута.
bookSentenceEn: The dragon passed like an express train, turned a **somersault**, and burst over Bywater with a deafening explosion.

definition: Lying stretched out on the ground with one’s face downwards; overcome or helpless.
explanationBg: Проснат на земята по очи, изпънат в цял ръст. Казва се и за човек, напълно сломен и безпомощен.
explanationEn: Lying flat on the ground face down; completely exhausted or helpless.
exampleEn: After the cross-country race he lay prostrate on the grass, too tired to speak.
mnemonicBg: Почти като нашето „прострян“ — проснат на тревата като пране след тежка тренировка.
bookSentenceEn: The pain and alarm vanished at once, and the **prostrate** hobbits leaped to their feet.

definition: Food, especially dry feed for livestock; provisions.
explanationBg: Храна и провизии — най-вече сухата храна за животните: зоб, сено, фураж.
explanationEn: Food supplies, especially dry food for animals.
exampleEn: Before visiting the stables we loaded the car with provender for the horses.
mnemonicBg: Чува се „провизии“ — чували със зоб и сено: храна за из път, главно за животните.
bookSentenceEn: Bringing up young hobbits took a lot of **provender**.

definition: Connections (British older spelling); links or relationships, especially family.
explanationBg: Старовремският британски правопис на думата за „връзки“ — отношения между хора, най-вече роднински или полезни познанства.
explanationEn: An old British spelling of 'connections' — links between people, especially family ties.
exampleEn: In the Austen novel we're reading for class, the heroine's rich connexions arrange everything.
mnemonicBg: Същото като connections, но със старовремско „x“ — стара карта, на която роднинските връзки са отбелязани с Х.
bookSentenceEn: a long-expected party 37 There were many Bagginses and Bofﬁns, and also many Tooks and Brandybucks; there were various Grubbs (relations of Bilbo Baggins’ grandmother), and various Chubbs (**connexions** of his Took grandfather); and a selection of Burrowses, Bolgers, Bracegirdles, Brockhouses, Goodbodies, Hornblowers and Proudfoots.

definition: Likely to do or to be something; legally responsible.
explanationBg: Склонен към нещо — има голяма вероятност да го направи или то да му се случи. В правото значи и „носещ отговорност“.
explanationEn: Likely to do something or to have it happen; also legally responsible.
exampleEn: If you leave your bike unlocked at school, it's liable to disappear.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е able („способен“) — способен всеки момент да направи беля: склонен е.
bookSentenceEn: He was **liable** to drag in bits of what he called poetry; and sometimes, after a glass or two, would allude to the absurd adventures of his mysterious journey.

definition: To suggest or call attention to indirectly; to hint at.
explanationBg: Да намекнеш за нещо, без да го кажеш направо — само го докосваш с думи, заобиколно.
explanationEn: To mention something indirectly; to hint at it.
exampleEn: She never said who broke the window, but she kept alluding to someone in our class.
mnemonicBg: Роднина на думата „алюзия“ — намек със заобикалки: „Хм, някой е изял шоколада…“.
bookSentenceEn: He was liable to drag in bits of what he called poetry; and sometimes, after a glass or two, would **allude** to the absurd adventures of his mysterious journey.

definition: Absorbing all one’s attention or interest; fascinating.
explanationBg: Толкова интересен и увличащ, че те грабва изцяло — забравяш всичко около себе си, докато четеш или гледаш.
explanationEn: So interesting that it takes all your attention.
exampleEn: The mystery game was so engrossing that we missed our bus stop.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „грос“ като в „гросмайстор“ — потънал в шахматната партия, светът изчезва: точно това прави една engrossing книга.
bookSentenceEn: The guests were not disappointed: they had a very pleasant feast, in fact an **engrossing** entertainment: rich, abundant, varied, and prolonged.

definition: Taking small, gentle bites of food.
explanationBg: Ядене на съвсем малки хапки — гризваш по мъничко, бавно и внимателно, вместо да лапаш наведнъж.
explanationEn: Eating something with small, gentle bites.
exampleEn: She watched the whole film, nibbling at the same slice of pizza for half an hour.
mnemonicBg: Представи си хамстерче: гриз-гриз-гриз по трошичка — nibbling е точно това ситно, кротко гризкане.
bookSentenceEn: They were sipping their favourite drinks, and **nibbling** at their favourite dainties, and their fears were forgotten.

definition: Delicious or choice small items of food; delicacies.
explanationBg: Малки, изискани и много вкусни неща за хапване — дребни сладкиши и деликатеси, които са истинско удоволствие.
explanationEn: Small pieces of especially tasty, fine food.
exampleEn: At the school fair, the French club sold little dainties like macarons and mini tarts.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „дай ни ти!“ — „Дай ни тия сладки!“ — мъничките вкусотии, към които всички посягат първо.
bookSentenceEn: They were sipping their favourite drinks, and nibbling at their favourite **dainties**, and their fears were forgotten.

definition: Done without being planned or rehearsed; on the spur of the moment.
explanationBg: Направен в момента, без никаква подготовка или репетиция — просто се случва спонтанно, на мига.
explanationEn: Done suddenly, without any planning or practice.
exampleEn: Our picnic turned into an impromptu football match when someone brought a ball.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „импро“ като в „импро театър“ — без сценарий, без репетиция, всичко се ражда на мига.
bookSentenceEn: Indeed, in one corner some of the young Tooks and Brandybucks, supposing Uncle Bilbo to have ﬁnished (since he had plainly said all that was necessary), now got up an **impromptu** orchestra, and began a merry dance-tune.

definition: Strong, healthy, and full of energy.
explanationBg: Силен, здрав и пълен с енергия — човек или движение, в което има живот и мощ.
explanationEn: Strong, healthy and full of energy.
exampleEn: A vigorous warm-up before practice keeps you from pulling a muscle.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „игър“ във „ви-ГЪР-ъс“ — почти „тигър“: енергичен и силен като тигър на сутрешен крос.
bookSentenceEn: Master Everard Took and Miss Melilot Brandybuck got on a table and with bells in their hands began to dance the Springle-ring: a pretty dance, but rather **vigorous**.

definition: Stubbornly refusing to change one’s opinion or course of action.
explanationBg: Който твърдоглаво отказва да промени мнението или решението си, каквото и да му казваш.
explanationEn: Refusing to change your mind, no matter what.
exampleEn: My obstinate little brother refuses to wear a jacket even in December.
mnemonicBg: „Об-СТЕНА-т“ — инат като СТЕНА: блъскаш, говориш, молиш — не помръдва.
bookSentenceEn: **Obstinate** silence.

definition: About to happen; impending.
explanationBg: Който всеки момент ще се случи — толкова е близо, че почти го усещаш как идва.
explanationEn: Going to happen very soon.
exampleEn: With exams imminent, the library suddenly got crowded.
mnemonicBg: „И-МИНЪНТ“ — до МИНУТА ще се случи: толкова е наблизо, че вече чуваш стъпките му.
bookSentenceEn: They all feared that a song or some poetry was now **imminent**; and they were getting bored.

definition: Greatly surprised or astonished.
explanationBg: Толкова изненадан, че оставаш с отворена уста и не можеш да кажеш и дума.
explanationEn: Extremely surprised; almost unable to speak.
exampleEn: I was flabbergasted when my quiet friend won the school rap battle.
mnemonicBg: „ФЛАБЪ-ГАСТ-ед“ — изненадата сякаш ти ГАСи мозъка за секунда и оставаш зяпнал.

definition: To bring down (one’s foot) heavily on the ground or on something.
explanationBg: Да тропнеш силно с крак по земята или върху нещо — от яд, нетърпение или за да го смачкаш.
explanationEn: To hit the ground hard with your foot.
exampleEn: She stamped her foot in frustration when the Wi-Fi dropped during the final boss.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш stamp като пощенска марка — тук „подпечатваш“ пода с крак: ТУП! Печат от подметка.
bookSentenceEn: Old Odo Proudfoot removed his feet from the table and **stamped**.

definition: Feeling or showing anger because of something unjust.
explanationBg: Ядосан и засегнат, защото усещаш, че нещо е несправедливо — възмущението те изпълва.
explanationEn: Angry because something seems unfair.
exampleEn: She got indignant when the teacher blamed the whole class for one person's prank.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие „дигн“ от dignity (достойнство) — настъпили са достойнството ти и кипваш: несправедливо е!
bookSentenceEn: He had difﬁculty in keeping from laughter at the **indignant** surprise of the guests.

definition: In an active, quick, or energetic way.
explanationBg: Бързо, живо и с енергия — без бавене и мотаене.
explanationEn: Quickly and with energy.
exampleEn: We walked briskly to school because the first bell had already rung.
mnemonicBg: „Бриск“ звучи като „бриз“ — движиш се свежо и пъргаво като утринен морски бриз.
bookSentenceEn: He walked **briskly** back to his hole, and stood for a moment listening with a smile to the din in the pavilion, and to the sounds of merrymaking in other parts of the ﬁeld.

definition: A loud, unpleasant, and prolonged noise.
explanationBg: Силен, неприятен шум, който продължава дълго и не ти дава покой — глъчка, тропот и викове наведнъж.
explanationEn: A loud, unpleasant noise that goes on and on.
exampleEn: Over the din of the cafeteria, I could barely hear my friend's story.
mnemonicBg: ДИН! ДИН! ДИН! — като камбана и тенджери едновременно: непрекъсната, оглушителна врява.
bookSentenceEn: He walked briskly back to his hole, and stood for a moment listening with a smile to the **din** in the pavilion, and to the sounds of merrymaking in other parts of the ﬁeld.

definition: Very thin, soft paper used for wrapping or protecting delicate objects.
explanationBg: Много тънка и мека хартия, с която се опаковат подаръци или се пазят чупливи и нежни предмети.
explanationEn: Very thin, soft paper for wrapping presents or delicate things.
exampleEn: I wrapped Mum's birthday mug in layers of tissue-paper so it wouldn't break.
mnemonicBg: „Тишу“ — като меките кърпички tissues: същата нежна, тъничка хартийка, но за опаковане на подаръци.
bookSentenceEn: He took off his party clothes, folded up and wrapped in **tissue-paper** his embroidered silk waistcoat, and put it away.

definition: A sheath for the blade of a sword or dagger.
explanationBg: Калъфът, в който се прибира острието на меч или кинжал, за да е защитено и безопасно.
explanationEn: A cover that holds and protects the blade of a sword.
exampleEn: For her cosplay, she made a silver scabbard out of cardboard to hold the foam sword.
mnemonicBg: Звучи почти като „шкаф-ърд“ — личният „шкаф“ на меча: прибираш острието вътре, за да спи.
bookSentenceEn: On it he hung a short sword in a battered black-leather **scabbard**.

definition: Small balls of naphthalene or camphor stored with clothes to keep moths away.
explanationBg: Малки бели топчета със силна миризма, които се слагат при дрехите в гардероба, за да гонят молците.
explanationEn: Small strong-smelling balls kept with clothes to keep moths away.
exampleEn: When we opened Grandma's old suitcase, the smell of moth-balls filled the room.
mnemonicBg: Moth значи „молец“ — топчета-бодигардове на пуловерите: миришат на бабин гардероб и гонят молците.
bookSentenceEn: From a locked drawer, smelling of **moth-balls**, he took out an old cloak and hood.

definition: Mended with a piece of material covering a hole or worn place.
explanationBg: Закърпен — върху скъсаното или протритото място е пришито парче плат, което го покрива.
explanationEn: Repaired with a piece of material sewn over a hole.
exampleEn: His favourite jeans are patched at both knees from years of skateboarding falls.
mnemonicBg: Като patch в игрите — кръпка, която запушва дупка: тук кръпката е истинско парче плат върху скъсаните дънки.
bookSentenceEn: They had been locked up as if they were very precious, but they were so **patched** and weatherstained that their original colour could hardly be guessed: it might have been dark green.

definition: Marked or discoloured by long exposure to the weather.
explanationBg: С петна и избеляла повърхност от дълго стоене навън — дъждът, слънцето и вятърът са оставили следите си.
explanationEn: Marked and faded because it stayed outside in rain and sun for a long time.
exampleEn: The weatherstained picnic table by the courts has gone grey after years of sun and rain.
mnemonicBg: Разглоби я: weather (време) + stained (изцапан) — времето е „изцапало“ дървото с дъжд, слънце и вятър.
bookSentenceEn: They had been locked up as if they were very precious, but they were so patched and **weatherstained** that their original colour could hardly be guessed: it might have been dark green.

definition: A meddlesome person who interferes in others’ affairs.
explanationBg: Човек, който постоянно си пъха носа в чуждите работи и се меси, без никой да го е молил.
explanationEn: A person who is too interested in other people's business.
exampleEn: The class busybody somehow knew about the surprise party before the birthday girl did.
mnemonicBg: Busy (зает) + body (човек) — уж „много зает“… но с чуждите работи: носът му е във всяка паница.
bookSentenceEn: You are an interfering old **busybody**,’ laughed Bilbo, ‘but I expect you know best, as usual.’

definition: (Informal) used to express annoyance; also: utterly confused.
explanationBg: Дума, с която изпускаш яда си — нещо като „проклет“ или „пуст да е“. Може да значи и „напълно объркан“.
explanationEn: A word people say when they are annoyed; it can also mean totally confused.
exampleEn: Where is my confounded charger? My phone is at one percent!
mnemonicBg: „Кон-ФАУНДЕД“ — обърканият КОН се мотае из двора, а ти мърмориш: „Проклетият кон!“ — двете значения в едно.
bookSentenceEn: In peace and quiet, without a lot of relatives prying around, and a string of **confounded** visitors hanging on the bell.

definition: Repeatedly asking or pestering someone for something.
explanationBg: Постоянно повтаряне на едно и също искане — врънкаш и досаждаш на някого, докато не се предаде.
explanationEn: Asking someone again and again until they get annoyed.
exampleEn: He kept badgering his parents for a gaming chair until his birthday finally came.
mnemonicBg: Badger е язовец — представи си язовец, който те ръчка с муцунка на всеки пет секунди: „Хайде де! Хайде де!“
bookSentenceEn: ‘You are always **badgering** me about my ring; but you have never bothered me about the other things that I got on my journey.’

definition: Items or remnants of something, especially of cloth; bits and pieces.
explanationBg: Дребни останали неща — парченца, изрезки и джунджурии, особено от плат, които не са част от нищо цяло.
explanationEn: Small leftover bits and pieces, especially of cloth.
exampleEn: Her sewing box was full of oddments of bright cloth left over from old projects.
mnemonicBg: Odd значи „несдвоен, странен“ — чекмеджето с несдвоени чорапи, копчета и парченца плат: oddments.
bookSentenceEn: I am leaving everything to him, of course, except a few **oddments**.

definition: In a stubborn manner; refusing to change.
explanationBg: Упорито и твърдоглаво — без да отстъпиш и милиметър, каквото и да ти говорят.
explanationEn: In a stubborn way, refusing to change.
exampleEn: She obstinately replayed the same level for hours, refusing to look up a walkthrough.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „стена“ в „об-СТЕНА-тли“ — стоиш като стена и не мърдаш от своето.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I’ll do as I choose and go as I please,’ said Bilbo **obstinately**.

definition: The handle of a sword or dagger.
explanationBg: Дръжката на меч или кинжал — частта, за която го хващаш.
explanationEn: The handle of a sword or dagger.
exampleEn: In fencing club, the coach showed us how to grip the hilt without squeezing too hard.
mnemonicBg: „Хилт“ звучи като „хилка“ — хващаш меча за „хилката“: дръжката, не острието!
bookSentenceEn: His hand strayed to the **hilt** of his small sword.

definition: In a manner expressing regret or sorrow, often mixed with amusement.
explanationBg: Със съжаление и лека тъга, често примесени с усмивка — както когато се смееш на собствената си грешка.
explanationEn: In a way that shows regret, often with a small sad smile.
exampleEn: He grinned ruefully after scoring an own goal in the last minute.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „руини“ — гледаш руините на плана си, въздъхваш и се усмихваш тъжно: ruefully.
bookSentenceEn: Then he shrugged his shoulders, and smiled rather **ruefully**.

definition: To go somewhere casually and briskly, often on foot.
explanationBg: Да прескочиш донякъде с бърза, лека крачка — отиваш си спокойно, но чевръсто, без да се влачиш.
explanationEn: To go somewhere quickly and casually on foot.
exampleEn: After the last lesson we trotted down to the bakery before it closed.
mnemonicBg: Trot е конски тръс — припкаш надолу по улицата в лек тръс: туп-туп-туп до магазина и обратно.

definition: A fence or boundary formed by closely growing bushes or shrubs.
explanationBg: Ограда от гъсто израснали храсти — жива стена от зеленина около двор или градина.
explanationEn: A line of bushes growing close together like a fence.
exampleEn: Our football kept flying over the hedge into the neighbour's garden.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за hedgehog (таралеж) — „животинчето на живия плет“: hedge е зеленият плет, в който той шумоли.
bookSentenceEn: He jumped over a low place in the **hedge** at the bottom, and took to the meadows, passing into the night like a rustle of wind in the grass.

definition: A small cart with one wheel at the front, pushed by handles at the rear.
translation: количка с едно колело, ръчна количка
explanationBg: Малка градинска количка с едно колело отпред, която буташ за двете дръжки отзад.
explanationEn: A small one-wheeled cart that you push by two handles.
exampleEn: We raced across the yard, one of us pushing the other in a wheel-barrow.
mnemonicBg: Wheel = колело — количка с ЕДНО-единствено колело, която се клатушка като пингвин с тежък товар.

definition: Without intention; accidentally.
explanationBg: Без да искаш и без да забележиш — става по невнимание, а не нарочно.
explanationEn: By accident, without meaning to.
exampleEn: I inadvertently liked a photo from 2019 while scrolling through her profile.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „върт“ в „инад-ВЪРТ-ънтли“ — нещо се завърта само, без да искаш: опа, неволно стана!
bookSentenceEn: Gardeners came by arrangement, and removed in wheelbarrows those that had **inadvertently** remained behind.

definition: The decorative paper wrapping of a Christmas cracker, often colourful.
explanationBg: Шарената хартия от коледна „пиратка“ — британска празнична бомбичка с изненада вътре. Двама я дърпат от двете страни, тя гръмва и хартията остава по масата.
explanationEn: The colourful paper around a Christmas cracker.
exampleEn: After Christmas lunch, the floor was covered in torn cracker-paper and tiny plastic toys.
mnemonicBg: Crack = „пук!“ — хартийката, която остава след пук-а на коледната пиратка: шарен спомен от гърмежа.
bookSentenceEn: People came and began (by orders) to clear away the pavilions and the tables and the chairs, and the spoons and knives and bottles and plates, and the lanterns, and the ﬂowering shrubs in boxes, and the crumbs and **cracker-paper**, the forgotten bags and gloves and handkerchiefs, and the uneaten food (a very small item).

definition: A mirror curved outwards, giving a wider but smaller image.
explanationBg: Огледало, което е издуто навън — показва по-широка картина, но образът в него изглежда по-малък.
explanationEn: A mirror that curves outwards and shows a wider but smaller picture.
exampleEn: The convex mirror at the blind corner of the bike path shows you if anyone is coming.
mnemonicBg: Convex = изпъкнал — представи си огледало с издуто „коремче“ напред, затова вижда нашироко.
bookSentenceEn: For ANGELICA’S use, from Uncle Bilbo; on a round **convex mirror**.

definition: Having an attractive or well-proportioned shape.
explanationBg: С красива, добре оформена фигура или форма — всичко е в правилните пропорции.
explanationEn: Having an attractive, well-proportioned shape.
exampleEn: In art class she turned a lump of clay into a surprisingly shapely vase.
mnemonicBg: Shape (форма) + -ly — нещо „с форма“: изваяно сякаш от скулптор, всичко на мястото си.
bookSentenceEn: She was a young Baggins, and too obviously considered her face **shapely**.

definition: A person who gives something, especially money, to help achieve a result.
explanationBg: Човек, който дава нещо — често пари — за да помогне дадена кауза или начинание да успее.
explanationEn: Someone who gives something, often money, to help a cause.
exampleEn: Every contributor to the school fundraiser got their name on the thank-you wall.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е tribute (дар, принос) — con-TRIBUT-or е човекът, който носи своя принос в общата каса.
bookSentenceEn: For the collection of HUGO BRACEGIRDLE, from a **contributor**; on an (empty) book-case.

definition: To crowd a place untidily with miscellaneous things.
explanationBg: Да затрупаш някое място с купища разхвърляни вещи, докато стане тясно и разбъркано.
explanationEn: To fill a place with too many untidy things.
exampleEn: Old worksheets and empty bottles clutter up my desk by the end of every week.
mnemonicBg: „КЛЪТЪР“ — представи си КУПчини, които се КЛАТушкат на бюрото: още едно нещо и всичко пада!

definition: A tool with a flat metal blade and a long handle, used for digging.
explanationBg: Инструмент за копаене — дълга дръжка с плоско метално острие, с което обръщаш пръстта.
explanationEn: A digging tool with a flat metal blade and a long handle.
exampleEn: Grab a spade — we're digging a fire pit at the campsite tonight.
mnemonicBg: Пиката от картите се казва spade — копаеш с гигантска карта „пика“: формата ѝ е точно като острие на лопата.
