bookSentenceEn: Frodo looked at it closely, and rather suspiciously (like one who has lent a trinket to a **juggler**).

definition: In a very dangerous way.
explanationBg: По много опасен начин — толкова рисковано, че всеки момент може да се случи беда.
explanationEn: In a very dangerous way.
exampleEn: His phone balanced perilously on the edge of the desk all through the lesson.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е „peril“ (опасност), а звучи като „перило“ — надвесиш ли се през перилото на балкона, висиш опасно: perilously.
bookSentenceEn: He was perhaps a triﬂe annoyed with Tom for seeming to make so light of what even Gandalf thought so **perilously** important.

definition: A thing of little value or importance; a small amount.
explanationBg: Дреболия — нещо толкова дребно и маловажно, че не си струва да се ядосваш или тревожиш за него.
explanationEn: A small thing that is not important.
exampleEn: Stop stressing over such a trifle — it was one wrong answer out of fifty.
mnemonicBg: „Трайфъл“ — представи си нещо, което струва само „три лева“: дреболия, за която не си заслужава да спориш.

definition: Heavily built nocturnal mammals with grey fur and black-and-white striped faces.
explanationBg: Язовците са набити нощни животни със сива козина и черно-бели ивици на муцуната. Денем спят в дупки под земята, а нощем излизат да търсят храна.
explanationEn: Strong grey night animals with black-and-white striped faces.
exampleEn: On the night hike we spotted two badgers digging near the forest path.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е „badge“ (значка) — язовецът носи черно-белите ивици на муцуната си като служебна значка „нощен пазач на гората“.
bookSentenceEn: He waited for an opportunity, when the talk was going again, and Tom was telling an absurd story about **badgers** and their queer ways – then he slipped the Ring on.

definition: (Archaic) anything at all.
explanationBg: Старинна дума за „нещо“ или „каквото и да е“ — днес ще я срещнеш само в стари книги, балади и приказки.
explanationEn: An old word meaning anything at all.
exampleEn: 'If you know aught about the missing snacks, speak now,' my sister said in her detective voice.
mnemonicBg: Запомни двойката: nAUGHT значи „нищо“, а AUGHT — „нещо“: само едно „н“ дели нищото от нещото.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I am no weather-master,’ said he; ‘nor is **aught** that goes on two legs.’

definition: Playful and full of energy.
explanationBg: Игрив и зареден с енергия — като кутре, което тича, подскача и не може да се спре на едно място.
explanationEn: Playful and full of energy.
exampleEn: Our kitten gets frisky at midnight and races around the whole flat.
mnemonicBg: „Frisky“ звучи като „фръцкав“ — фръц-фръц насам, фръц натам: цялото в игра и енергия.
bookSentenceEn: Their quiet ponies were almost **frisky**, snifﬁng and moving restlessly.

definition: Flowing down in small waves or undulating movements.
explanationBg: Който се спуска или стича надолу на меки вълнички — като коса, падаща на вълни по раменете, или поточе по склон.
explanationEn: Flowing or falling down in small soft waves.
exampleEn: Her hair came rippling down over her shoulders when she took off her helmet.
mnemonicBg: „Ripple“ звучи като „рипвам“ — камъчето рипва във водата и вълничките плъзват надолу една след друга.
bookSentenceEn: He was so distressed that he turned back; but at that moment a clear call came **rippling down**.

definition: The upper edge or crest of a hill.
explanationBg: Най-горният ръб на хълма — неговото „чело“, мястото, откъдето склонът тръгва надолу.
explanationEn: The top edge of a hill.
exampleEn: We stopped our bikes at the hill-brow to catch our breath and enjoy the view.
mnemonicBg: „Brow“ значи „вежда, чело“ — хълмът също има чело: застанеш ли на hill-brow, стоиш точно на челото му.
bookSentenceEn: There on the **hill-brow** she stood beckoning to them: her hair was ﬂying loose, and as it caught the sun it shone and shimmered.

definition: Making a gesture to encourage someone to come nearer or follow.
explanationBg: Да махаш с ръка или да кимаш на някого в знак „ела насам“ или „последвай ме“.
explanationEn: Waving or signalling to someone to come closer.
exampleEn: My friends were beckoning me over to their table in the cafeteria.
mnemonicBg: Чуй началото на „BEck-oning“ — някой ти маха с ръка: „Бе, ела насам!“
bookSentenceEn: There on the hill-brow she stood **beckoning** to them: her hair was ﬂying loose, and as it caught the sun it shone and shimmered.

definition: Wet with dew or like dew.
explanationBg: Мокър от роса — покрит със ситни хладни капчици, каквато е тревата рано сутрин.
explanationEn: Wet with small drops of morning water.
exampleEn: My socks got soaked walking across the dewy grass before sunrise.
mnemonicBg: Представи си патето Дюи от „Патешки истории“, което гази в росната трева и става мокро от глава до пети — dewy.
bookSentenceEn: fog on the barrow-downs 177 light like the glint of water on **dewy** grass ﬂashed from under her feet as she danced.

definition: A long, narrow hilltop, mountain range, or watershed.
explanationBg: Дългият тесен „гръб“ на планина или хълм — горната линия, по която минава билото.
explanationEn: The long narrow top of a hill or mountain.
exampleEn: We hiked along the ridge with deep valleys on both sides of us.
mnemonicBg: „Ridge“ звучи почти като нашето „рид“ — ридът си е ridge: дълъг гръб на хълм.
bookSentenceEn: Each time they climbed a **ridge** the breeze seemed to have grown less.

definition: Crushed or pressed into wrinkles or folds.
explanationBg: Смачкан на гънки и бръчки — като лист хартия, който си стискал в юмрука си.
explanationEn: Crushed into wrinkles and folds.
exampleEn: He pulled a crumpled permission slip from the bottom of his backpack.
mnemonicBg: „Кръмпъл!“ — самият звук на лист, смачкан в юмрук: чуеш ли хрущенето, помниш думата.
bookSentenceEn: It seemed fainthearted to go jogging aside over the **crumpled** skirts of the downs towards the Road, when they should be leaping, as lusty as Tom, over the stepping stones of the hills straight towards the Mountains.

definition: Able to spring back quickly into shape; resilient and elastic.
explanationBg: Който пружинира — поддава, когато го натиснеш, и веднага отскача обратно, като батут или гумена топка.
explanationEn: Elastic and bouncy, returning quickly to its shape.
exampleEn: The new gym mats are so springy that everyone wants to practise flips on them.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е „spring“ (пружина) — стъпиш ли, пружинката те изстрелва нагоре: springy!
bookSentenceEn: There was no tree nor any visible water: it was a country of grass and short **springy** turf, silent except for the whisper of the air over the edges of the land, and high lonely cries of strange birds.

definition: Former units of distance, usually about three miles or five kilometres.
explanationBg: Левгата е стара мярка за разстояние — около пет километра. В старите книги героите често пътуват „левги наред“.
explanationEn: Old units of distance, each about five kilometres.
exampleEn: Grandpa jokes that he walked leagues to school every day, uphill both ways.
mnemonicBg: „League“ ти напомня футболната Лига — представи си, че до всеки мач от Лигата вървиш пеша по пет километра: цяла левга.
bookSentenceEn: All along it for many **leagues** east of the Bridge there are trees growing.

definition: A complete amount; as much as something can hold (used as a noun: "had his fill").
explanationBg: Количеството, което ти е напълно достатъчно — когато си ял или правил нещо „до насита“, получил си точно толкова, колкото ти стига.
explanationEn: As much of something as you want or can take.
exampleEn: After three slices of pizza I had eaten my fill and gave the rest to my brother.
mnemonicBg: „Fill“ звучи като „филия“ — след десетата филия си получил своя fill: до насита!

definition: (Of hair) long, limp, and straight; ungracefully thin.
explanationBg: За коса: права, безжизнено увиснала и без обем — виси надолу, сякаш няма никаква сила.
explanationEn: Hair that hangs straight, flat, and lifeless.
exampleEn: After a week at camp with no shampoo, my hair looked completely lank.
mnemonicBg: „Ланк“ звучи като „ланец“ — косата виси права и тежка надолу, като ланче без живот.
bookSentenceEn: As they went down the mist became colder and damper, and their hair hung **lank** and dripping on their foreheads.

definition: Wet with or as if with dew; sprinkled with moisture.
explanationBg: Покрит с роса или със ситни капчици влага — сякаш някой го е напръскал с вода рано сутринта.
explanationEn: Covered with dew or tiny drops of water.
exampleEn: The tents were bedewed when we crawled out at dawn for the sunrise hike.
mnemonicBg: „Bed“ (легло) + „dew“ (роса) — заспиш ли на легло от трева, осъмваш bedewed: целият в капчици.
bookSentenceEn: When they reached the bottom it was so chill that they halted and got out cloaks and hoods, which soon became **bedewed** with grey drops.

definition: A doorway with no top frame, or open at the head.
explanationBg: Врата или отвор без горна греда — рамката няма „глава“ отгоре и стои отворена нагоре.
explanationEn: A doorway with no top part of the frame.
exampleEn: The old garden shed has a headless door, so even my tall cousin walks in without ducking.
mnemonicBg: „Head“ значи „глава“ — врата без глава: някой ѝ е махнал горната греда, както на снежен човек махат главата.
bookSentenceEn: The dark patches grew darker, but they shrank; and suddenly he saw, towering ominous before him and leaning slightly towards one another like the pillars of a **headless door**, two huge standing stones.

definition: In a hurried, excited, or disorganised way; wildly.
explanationBg: Трескаво и панически — когато правиш нещо лудо бързо и хаотично, защото времето или страхът те притискат.
explanationEn: In a wild, hurried, and panicked way.
exampleEn: I searched frantically for my bus pass while the driver waited.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „тик“ вътре — хваща те нервен тик и почваш да вършиш всичко неистово бързо: fran-TIC-ally.
bookSentenceEn: As he struggled on he called again, and kept on calling more and more **frantically**; but he heard no answer for some time, and then it seemed faint and far ahead and high above him.

definition: Great fear or apprehension; anticipated with great fear.
explanationBg: Силен страх от нещо, което предстои — онова свиване в стомаха, когато чакаш да се случи нещо лошо.
explanationEn: A strong fear of something that is going to happen.
exampleEn: A wave of dread hit me when the teacher said, 'Surprise test, clear your desks.'
mnemonicBg: Чакаш си РЕДа пред зъболекаря — d-РЕД! — и стомахът ти се свива от ужас: dread.
bookSentenceEn: fog on the barrow-downs 183 When he came to himself again, for a moment he could recall nothing except a sense of **dread**.

definition: An ancient burial mound; also a wheelbarrow.
explanationBg: Древна гробна могила — хълмче от пръст, насипано над гроб преди хиляди години. Със същата дума англичаните наричат и ръчната градинска количка.
explanationEn: An ancient mound of earth built over a grave; it can also mean a wheelbarrow.
exampleEn: Archaeologists let our class watch while they scanned the ancient barrow with radar.
mnemonicBg: „Barrow“ звучи близко до „баир“ — древно баирче, насипано от хора върху гроб.
bookSentenceEn: A **Barrow**-wight had taken him, and he was probably already under the dreadful spells of the Barrow-wights about which whispered tales spoke.

definition: Lacking internal strength or structure; not firm or stiff.
explanationBg: Отпуснат и мек, без сила и стегнатост — като ръка, която виси безжизнено, или клюмнало цвете.
explanationEn: Soft and weak, without firmness or strength.
exampleEn: After the toughest training session of the season, my arms went completely limp.
mnemonicBg: Вдигни преварена спагета — увисва отпусната и безсилна: точно това е limp.
bookSentenceEn: He found himself stiffening, as if for a ﬁnal spring; he no longer felt **limp** like a helpless prey.

definition: Becoming or making stiff or rigid.
explanationBg: Когато нещо меко или подвижно започва да става твърдо и неподвижно — мускулите се вкочаняват, тялото се изпъва.
explanationEn: Becoming hard, stiff, or rigid.
exampleEn: I felt my legs stiffening after the three-hour bus ride to the tournament.
mnemonicBg: „Stiff“ звучи като „щифт“ — мускулите ти се втвърдяват като метални щифтове: stiffening.
bookSentenceEn: He found himself **stiffening**, as if for a ﬁnal spring; he no longer felt limp like a helpless prey.

definition: Small circular bands, especially of precious metal, worn on the head.
explanationBg: Тънки кръгли обръчи, най-често от злато или сребро, които се носят на главата — като малки, скромни коронки.
explanationEn: Thin round metal bands worn on the head.
exampleEn: The dancers wore silver circlets that sparkled under the stage lights.
mnemonicBg: „Circle“ (кръг) + „-let“ (мъничко) — мънички кръгчета-коронки, кацнали на главите.
bookSentenceEn: On their heads were **circlets**, gold chains were about their waists, and on their ﬁngers were many rings.

definition: To an extent or degree that cannot be measured.
explanationBg: Толкова много, че не може да се измери — без граница и без край.
explanationEn: So much that it cannot be measured.
exampleEn: Having my best friend in the same class made the school year immeasurably better.
mnemonicBg: Представи си линийка, която се чупи и се предава: „Не мога да го измеря!“ — im-MEASURE-ably.
bookSentenceEn: The voice seemed far away and **immeasurably** dreary, sometimes high in the air and thin, sometimes like a low moan from the ground.

definition: Depressingly dull and bleak or repetitive.
explanationBg: Сив, скучен и потискащ — като дъждовен ноемврийски следобед, в който нищо интересно не се случва.
explanationEn: Dull, grey, and depressing.
exampleEn: The dreary weather ruined our skate park plans for the whole weekend.
mnemonicBg: „Dreary“ звучи като „дрямка“ — ден толкова сив и скучен, че ти се дреме само като го погледнеш.
bookSentenceEn: The voice seemed far away and immeasurably **dreary**, sometimes high in the air and thin, sometimes like a low moan from the ground.

definition: Firm determination to do something; the act of deciding.
explanationBg: Твърда решителност — онова стиснато „ще го направя и точка“, което не ти позволява да се откажеш.
explanationEn: Strong determination to do something.
exampleEn: Losing the first set only strengthened her resolve to win the match.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е „solve“ (решавам) — решил си твърдо и никой не може да те разубеди: това е resolve.
bookSentenceEn: Suddenly **resolve** hardened in him, and he seized a short sword that lay beside him, and kneeling he stooped low over the bodies of his companions.

definition: To chop or cut with an axe, sword, or other tool.
explanationBg: Да сечеш или разсичаш с брадва, меч или друго остро сечиво — с тежки, силни удари.
explanationEn: To chop or cut something with an axe or sword.
exampleEn: For the survival challenge we had to hew branches for a shelter with a small axe.
mnemonicBg: Дърварят Хю — „Хю-ХРЯС!“ — замахва с брадвата и отсича клона с един удар: hew.
bookSentenceEn: With what strength he had he **hewed** at the crawling arm near the wrist, and the hand broke off; but at the same moment the sword splintered up to the hilt.

definition: To break into thin, sharp pieces.
explanationBg: Да натрошиш нещо на тънки, остри тресчици — както суха дъска се пръска на стотици иглички.
explanationEn: To break into thin sharp pieces.
exampleEn: My cheap hockey stick splintered up after one hard slapshot.
mnemonicBg: „Splinter“ звучи като „спринтьор“ — спринтьор пробива дървена ограда и тя се пръсва на трески.

definition: A feeling of great surprise or wonder.
explanationBg: Огромно учудване — когато нещо те смае така, че оставаш със зяпнала уста.
explanationEn: A feeling of great surprise or wonder.
exampleEn: To everyone's amazement, the quietest kid in class won the rap battle.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е „maze“ (лабиринт) — стоиш в центъра на лабиринта със зяпнала уста: a-MAZE-ment.
bookSentenceEn: They looked about in **amazement**, ﬁrst at Frodo, and then at Tom standing large as life on the barrow-top above them; and then at themselves in their thin white rags, crowned and belted with pale gold, and jingling with trinkets.

definition: Pieces of old, torn, or worn-out cloth.
explanationBg: Стари, скъсани и износени парчета плат — дрипи, които стават вече само за бърсане.
explanationEn: Old torn pieces of cloth.
exampleEn: We cut Dad's old T-shirts into rags for cleaning our bikes.
mnemonicBg: Котката РЪГа нокти в завесата — ръг-ръг — и я прави на rags: парцали.
bookSentenceEn: They looked about in amazement, ﬁrst at Frodo, and then at Tom standing large as life on the barrow-top above them; and then at themselves in their thin white **rags**, crowned and belted with pale gold, and jingling with trinkets.

definition: A circular ornament, especially one worn on the head.
explanationBg: Кръгло украшение за глава — тънък метален обръч, който прилича на лека коронка или диадема.
explanationEn: A round ornament worn on the head like a thin crown.
exampleEn: For the school play she wore a golden circlet instead of a heavy crown.
mnemonicBg: Представи си рицаря Сър Кръглет, който вместо шлем носи тънко златно кръгче на главата — circlet.
bookSentenceEn: ‘What in the name of wonder?’ began Merry, feeling the golden **circlet** that had slipped over one eye.

definition: Short trousers fastened just below the knee.
explanationBg: Старомодни къси панталони, които стигат до под коляното и там се закопчават — носели са ги ездачи и господа в миналото.
explanationEn: Short trousers that fasten just below the knee.
exampleEn: For the history play at school, Tom had to wear breeches and long white socks.
mnemonicBg: Английското breeches звучи почти като нашите „бричове“ — това си е същата дреха: панталони до коляното.
bookSentenceEn: He ﬂung his circlet, belt, and rings on the grass, and looked round helplessly, as if he expected to ﬁnd his cloak, jacket, and **breeches**, and other hobbit-garments lying somewhere to hand.

definition: Lying exposed to warmth and light, typically for pleasure.
explanationBg: Да се излежаваш блажено на топло и светло — както котка се пече на слънце, без да бърза за никъде.
explanationEn: Lying in warm light and enjoying it, like sunbathing.
exampleEn: After exams we spent the whole afternoon basking in the sun at the beach.
mnemonicBg: След БАСКетбол лягаш на тревата и се печеш на слънце — това е basking.
bookSentenceEn: Then they lay **basking** in the sun with the delight of those that have been wafted suddenly from bitter winter to a friendly clime, or of people that, after being long ill and bedridden, wake one day to ﬁnd that they are unexpectedly well and the day is again full of promise.

definition: Articles of clothing.
explanationBg: По-официална дума за дрехи — всяко отделно парче облекло: риза, панталон, рокля.
explanationEn: Pieces of clothing.
exampleEn: She folded all her garments neatly before packing them into the suitcase.
mnemonicBg: Запомни: garment спи в ГАРдероба — и двете започват с „гар“.
bookSentenceEn: Merry, Sam, and Pippin now clothed themselves in spare **garments** from their packs; and they soon felt too hot, for they were obliged to put on some of the thicker and warmer things that they had brought against the oncoming of winter.

definition: A pace of a horse or quadruped faster than a walk, in which the diagonal legs move together.
explanationBg: Тръс — бягът на кон, по-бърз от ходене, но по-бавен от галоп; равномерно подтичване.
explanationEn: A horse's steady pace that is faster than walking but slower than galloping.
exampleEn: Our dog broke into a happy trot the moment he saw the park gates.
mnemonicBg: Чуй копитата: „трот-трот-трот“ — самата дума тропа в тръс.
bookSentenceEn: For you cannot easily talk to hobbits that are riding, when you’re on your own legs trying to **trot** beside them.’

definition: Close-fitting cover or case for the blade of a knife or sword.
explanationBg: Калъфи за нож или меч — плътни обвивки, в които се прибира острието, за да е защитено и безопасно.
explanationEn: Covers that protect the blades of knives or swords.
exampleEn: At scout camp we learned to keep our pocket knives in their sheaths.
mnemonicBg: Острието стои заШИТо в калъфа си — sheath е като ушито палтенце за меча.
bookSentenceEn: They gleamed as he drew them from their black **sheaths**, wrought of some strange metal, light and strong, and set with many ﬁery stones.

definition: Behaviour showing high moral standards; a quality of efficacy or power.
explanationBg: Добродетел — качеството да постъпваш честно и добре; понякога значи и силата или полезното действие на нещо.
explanationEn: Goodness and high moral behaviour; also the special power or useful quality of something.
exampleEn: Patience is a virtue you really need when your Wi-Fi keeps dropping mid-game.
mnemonicBg: Virtue звучи като „виртуоз“ — виртуоз не на пианото, а в правенето на добро.
bookSentenceEn: Whether by some **virtue** in these sheaths or because of the spell that lay on the mound, the blades seemed untouched by time, unrusted, sharp, glittering in the sun.

definition: The action of loading a ship or vehicle with cargo.
explanationBg: Старовремска дума за товарене — слагането на стока на кораб или каруца; може да значи и самия товар.
explanationEn: The loading of goods onto a ship or vehicle; also the cargo itself.
exampleEn: From the pier we watched the lading of the huge container ship all morning.
mnemonicBg: В lading се чува „ладия“ — старата дума за лодка: товарят ладията.
bookSentenceEn: They made ready, packing their bags and **lading** their ponies.

definition: The measurement around the middle of something; a band fastening a saddle.
explanationBg: Обиколката на нещо по средата — например на дърво или корем; при конете е и коланът, който държи седлото.
explanationEn: The distance around the middle of something; also the strap that holds a saddle on a horse.
exampleEn: It took four of us holding hands to measure the girth of the old oak tree.
mnemonicBg: Girth звучи като „гърди“ — мериш обиколката около гърдите на коня, за да стегнеш седлото.
bookSentenceEn: It was a merry journey with Tom Bombadil trotting gaily beside them, or before them, on Fatty Lumpkin, who could move much faster than his **girth** promised.

definition: In a cheerful or light-hearted manner.
explanationBg: Весело и безгрижно — когато правиш нещо с усмивка и леко сърце.
explanationEn: In a happy, cheerful way.
exampleEn: She waved gaily from the bus window as the team set off for the tournament.
mnemonicBg: Чуеш ли ГАЙдата — хорото тръгва весело и бодро: gaily!
bookSentenceEn: It was a merry journey with Tom Bombadil trotting **gaily** beside them, or before them, on Fatty Lumpkin, who could move much faster than his girth promised.

definition: Units of distance equal to an eighth of a mile (about 201 metres).
explanationBg: Стара английска мярка за разстояние — един фърлонг е около 200 метра; и днес се ползва в конните надбягвания.
explanationEn: Old units of distance; one furlong is about 200 metres.
exampleEn: The favourite horse sprinted the last two furlongs and won the race.
mnemonicBg: Fur (козина) + long (дълъг): пухкав кон тича дълга отсечка от 200 метра — furlong.
bookSentenceEn: They galloped their ponies over the last **furlongs**, and halted under the long shadows of the trees.

definition: Holes in a road surface caused by wear or water damage.
explanationBg: Дупките по асфалта, отворени от дъжд и износване — онези, в които колата друсва, а колелото пропада.
explanationEn: Holes in the road made by weather and damage.
exampleEn: I nearly flew over the handlebars when my bike hit one of the pot-holes on our street.
mnemonicBg: Pot е тенджера, hole е дупка — пътят е надупчен, сякаш някой е вадил тенджери от асфалта.
bookSentenceEn: It was rutted and bore many signs of the recent heavy rain; there were pools and **pot-holes** full of water.

definition: The side of a person, animal, or hill; the side of a body of troops.
explanationBg: Хълбокът, страната — на човек, животно или хълм; във футбола и игрите е крилото, страничната зона.
explanationEn: The side of a body, an animal, a hill, or a group such as an army or a team.
exampleEn: Our winger raced down the left flank and crossed the ball for the striker.
mnemonicBg: Това е нашият „фланг“ от футбола и игрите — атакуваш отстрани, по фланга.

definition: (Of a horse) springing from the hind legs while moving forward.
explanationBg: Когато кон подскача наперено на задните си крака, докато върви — гордо, танцуващо движение.
explanationEn: Moving forward with proud, springy steps, like a show horse.
exampleEn: The puppy was prancing around the garden as if it had just won a medal.
mnemonicBg: В prancing се чува „принц“ — конят стъпва като принц на парад.
bookSentenceEn: Chapter 9 AT THE SIGN OF THE **PRANCING** PONY Bree was the chief village of the Bree-land, a small inhabited region, like an island in the empty lands round about.

definition: A wooded area that has been managed or shaped by people.
explanationBg: Гора, подредена и поддържана от хора — с пътеки и разчистени дървета, а не дива пустош.
explanationEn: A forest that people manage and keep tidy, not a wild one.
exampleEn: The park behind our school feels like tamed woodland, with neat paths between the trees.
mnemonicBg: Представи си гора, минала през фризьор — подстригана и послушна: опитомена, tamed.
bookSentenceEn: Lying round Bree-hill and the villages was a small country of ﬁelds and **tamed woodland** only a few miles broad.

definition: Houses, flats, or other places of residence.
explanationBg: Места, в които живеят хора — къщи, апартаменти, домове; малко по-книжна дума за жилища.
explanationEn: Places where people live, such as houses or flats.
exampleEn: From the plane window the village dwellings looked like tiny toy houses.
mnemonicBg: Двама съседи излизат на ДУЕЛ пред своите dwellings — чий дом е по-хубав.
bookSentenceEn: In those days no other Men had settled **dwellings** so far west, or within a hundred leagues of the Shire.

definition: People who do not belong to a particular group or area.
explanationBg: Хора „отвън“ — които не принадлежат към дадена група, компания или място и затова ги усещат като чужди.
explanationEn: People who do not belong to a group or place.
exampleEn: The new kids felt like outsiders until the class invited them to game night.
mnemonicBg: Out (вън) + side (страна) — стоиш отвън, отстрани на купона: външен човек.
bookSentenceEn: There were probably many more **Outsiders** scattered about in the West of the World in those days than the people of the Shire imagined.

definition: Lacking good manners, refinement, or grace.
explanationBg: Недодялан и грубоват — човек без обноски, който се държи просташки или тромаво пред хора.
explanationEn: Rude and without good manners.
exampleEn: Talking with your mouth full at a birthday dinner looks really uncouth.
mnemonicBg: Uncouth звучи като „ън-КЮТук“ — седи на масата като кютук: недодялан и груб.
bookSentenceEn: The Shire-hobbits referred to those of Bree, and to any others that lived beyond the borders, as Outsiders, and took very little interest in them, considering them dull and **uncouth**.

definition: Distributed at intervals over an area; sparsely spaced.
explanationBg: Разпръснат тук-там из някаква площ — не на едно място, а на отделни парченца или групички.
explanationEn: Spread out in different places over an area.
exampleEn: After movie night, popcorn was scattered all over the living-room floor.
mnemonicBg: Вътре в sCATtered се крие cat — котката, която е разпиляла всичко из стаята.
bookSentenceEn: There were probably many more Outsiders **scattered** about in the West of the World in those days than the people of the Shire imagined.

definition: Successful, especially financially; flourishing.
explanationBg: Преуспяващ и заможен — комуто работите вървят и парите стигат, който цъфти в това, което прави.
explanationEn: Successful and doing well, especially with money.
exampleEn: Her family's tiny bakery grew so prosperous that they opened three more shops.
mnemonicBg: Чуваш „просперитет“ вътре — който просперира, е prosperous.
bookSentenceEn: But in the Bree-land, at any rate, the hobbits were decent and **prosperous**, and no more rustic than most of their distant relatives Inside.

definition: Small houses, especially in the country, used as temporary accommodation.
explanationBg: Малки къщички, най-често сред природата — хижи или вили, в които се отсяда за кратко, например на почивка.
explanationEn: Small country houses where people stay for a short time.
exampleEn: We rented one of the wooden lodges by the lake for the school ski trip.
mnemonicBg: Lodge звучи като „ложе“ (легло) — къщичка, в която лягаш да преспиш след цял ден ски.
bookSentenceEn: The gates were closed at nightfall; but just inside them were small **lodges** for the gatekeepers.

definition: A long wall or embankment built to prevent flooding from the sea.
explanationBg: Дига — дълъг насип или стена, която пази сушата да не я залее морето.
explanationEn: A long wall of earth or stone that stops the sea from flooding the land.
exampleEn: In the Netherlands we cycled along a huge dike that holds back the sea.
mnemonicBg: Dike и „дига“ са почти една дума — вДИГАш стена срещу вълните.
bookSentenceEn: On that side, running in more than half a circle from the hill and back to it, there was a deep **dike** with a thick hedge on the inner side.

definition: A person who owns or manages an inn.
explanationBg: Ханджия — човекът, който държи хан или малък крайпътен хотел и посреща пътниците.
explanationEn: The person who runs an inn or small hotel.
exampleEn: The friendly innkeeper at the mountain guesthouse showed us where to dry our wet boots.
mnemonicBg: Като goalkeeper, но на хан — inn (хан) + keeper (пазач): пазачът на хана и гостите му.
bookSentenceEn: The Inn of Bree was still there, however, and the **innkeeper** was an important person.

definition: (Of a person) avoiding work; lazy; not active or in use.
explanationBg: Безделен, мързелив — който нищо не върши; казва се и за машина или телефон, които стоят, без да се използват.
explanationEn: Lazy or doing nothing; not being used.
exampleEn: My brother spent a completely idle Sunday on the couch, not even finishing one episode.
mnemonicBg: Idle звучи като „айде“ — на безделника му викаш: „Айде де, размърдай се!“
bookSentenceEn: His house was a meeting place for the **idle**, talkative, and inquisitive among the inhabitants, large and small, of the four villages; and a resort of Rangers and other wanderers, and for such travellers (mostly dwarves) as still journeyed on the East Road, to and from the Mountains.

definition: A board displaying the name of a shop or other establishment.
explanationBg: Табела — дъска с името на магазин или заведение, закачена отпред, за да я виждат всички.
explanationEn: A board showing the name of a shop or business.
exampleEn: The new cafe's neon signboard lights up the whole street at night.
mnemonicBg: Sign (знак) + board (дъска): представи си скейтборд, закован над вратата като табела.
bookSentenceEn: Above the arch there was a lamp, and beneath it swung a large **signboard**: a fat white pony reared up on its hind legs.

definition: (Of an animal) rose on its hind legs; stood upright suddenly.
explanationBg: Изправил се рязко на задните си крака — както прави подплашен или разигран кон.
explanationEn: Stood up suddenly on the back legs, like a frightened horse.
exampleEn: The horse reared up when a plastic bag blew across the path.
mnemonicBg: Конят изРЕВа и се изправи на задни крака — reared up.
bookSentenceEn: Above the arch there was a lamp, and beneath it swung a large signboard: a fat white pony **reared up** on its hind legs.

definition: At the back; rear (especially of an animal’s legs); also a female deer.
explanationBg: Заден — най-често за задните крака на животно; същата дума може да значи и кошута, женски елен.
explanationEn: At the back, like an animal's back legs; also a female deer.
exampleEn: Our dog balances on his hind legs whenever he smells a treat.
mnemonicBg: Махни „би-“ от behind (отзад) и остава hind — задното.
bookSentenceEn: Above the arch there was a lamp, and beneath it swung a large signboard: a fat white pony reared up on its **hind** legs.

definition: A protective garment worn over the front of one’s clothes.
explanationBg: Престилка — връзваш я отпред, за да не си изцапаш дрехите, докато готвиш или рисуваш.
explanationEn: A piece of clothing worn over your clothes to keep them clean.
exampleEn: Dad puts on his lucky apron every time he makes pancakes.
mnemonicBg: Apron — „опрян“: престилката стои опряна отпред на дрехите ти.
bookSentenceEn: He had a white **apron** on, and was bustling out of one door and in through another, carrying a tray laden with full mugs.

definition: Accommodation for horses; the act of putting a horse in a stable.
explanationBg: Подслон за коне — конюшни; също и самото настаняване на кон в обор.
explanationEn: Space in stables where horses can stay.
exampleEn: The riding club offers stabling for ten horses during the summer camp.
mnemonicBg: Конят иска СТАБИЛен покрив над главата — stabling, място в конюшнята.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Beds for four, and **stabling** for ﬁve ponies, if that can be managed.

definition: Flows in a continuous stream; rains heavily.
explanationBg: Лее се — тече силно и без прекъсване; за дъжд значи, че вали като из ведро.
explanationEn: Flows strongly or rains very heavily.
exampleEn: Every time we plan a picnic, it pours all afternoon.
mnemonicBg: Pours звучи като „порой“ — дъждът се лее като порой.
bookSentenceEn: It never rains but it **pours**, we say in Bree.’

definition: Having feet covered with thick hair, like a hobbit; padding softly.
explanationBg: С мъхнати, космати стъпала — затова стъпва меко и безшумно, сякаш ходи по пухкави чорапи.
explanationEn: Having feet covered with soft thick hair, so the steps make no sound.
exampleEn: In my fluffy slippers I was practically woolly-footed, sneaking downstairs for a midnight snack.
mnemonicBg: Wool е вълна — стъпала с вградени вълнени терлици: woolly-footed.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Where are you, you **woolly-footed** slowcoach?

definition: (Informal British) a person who acts or moves slowly.
explanationBg: Шеговита британска дума за муден човек — който вечно се бави и всички го чакат.
explanationEn: A person who moves or works too slowly.
exampleEn: Hurry up, slow-coach — the bus leaves in two minutes!
mnemonicBg: Slow (бавна) + coach (каляска): каляска, теглена от охлюви — все нея чакаш.

definition: To appear briefly with a sudden bouncing or popping movement.
explanationBg: Да изскочиш за миг с подскачащо движение — да се покажеш внезапно и пак да се скриеш.
explanationEn: To pop out suddenly with a quick bouncing movement.
exampleEn: A little fish kept bobbing out of the water next to our paddleboard.
mnemonicBg: Представи си зрънце боб, което подскача и изскача от купата — bob out!

definition: A sitting room in a private house, especially in an inn or for receiving visitors.
explanationBg: Гостна — стаята, в която се посрещат гости; в стар хан това е уютният салон край огъня.
explanationEn: A sitting room where guests are received.
exampleEn: Grandma keeps her best armchairs in the parlour for special guests.
mnemonicBg: Parlour е роднина на „парламент“ — и двете значат „стая за приказки“: гостната е домашният парламент.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Here is a nice little **parlour**!’ he said.

definition: Going at a moderately fast pace, faster than walking.
explanationBg: Подтичване в тръс — равномерно, леко бягане, по-бързо от ходене, но далеч от спринт.
explanationEn: Moving at a light, steady run, faster than walking.
exampleEn: We warmed up by trotting twice around the track before PE.
mnemonicBg: Подтичваш по ТРОТоара, за да хванеш автобуса — trotting.
bookSentenceEn: I must be **trotting**.

definition: A very short time; an instant ("in a twinkling").
explanationBg: Съвсем кратък миг — колкото да мигнеш или звезда да трепне.
explanationEn: A very short moment; an instant.
exampleEn: The pizza disappeared in a twinkling once the whole team got home.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „Twinkle, twinkle, little star“ — едно трепване на звездичката трае точно един миг.
bookSentenceEn: In **a twinkling** the table was laid.

definition: Quantities of bread baked in single pieces, usually elongated.
explanationBg: Самуни хляб — цели изпечени хлябове, обикновено продълговати.
explanationEn: Whole baked breads; more than one loaf.
exampleEn: The bakery near school sells warm loaves straight from the oven at seven in the morning.
mnemonicBg: Сутрешен ЛОВ на топли самуни — тръгваш на лов за loaves от фурната.
bookSentenceEn: There was hot soup, cold meats, a blackberry tart, new **loaves**, slabs of butter, and half a ripe cheese: good plain food, as good as the Shire could show,

definition: To make a doubt, feeling, or belief disappear.
explanationBg: Да разсееш съмнение, страх или погрешна представа — да ги накараш да изчезнат, както вятър разгонва мъгла.
explanationEn: To make a doubt, fear, or wrong idea go away.
exampleEn: Scoring in her first match dispelled all her doubts about joining the team.
mnemonicBg: Dis + spell (магия): разваляш магията на страха и той се разпръсва.
bookSentenceEn: 202 the fellowship of the ring and homelike enough to **dispel** the last of Sam’s misgivings (already much relieved by the excellence of the beer).

definition: A fire built using logs of wood as fuel.
explanationBg: Огън от цели цепеници — какъвто гори в камина или на лагер, с пукащи дърва и много топлина.
explanationEn: A fire made with big pieces of wood.
exampleEn: We toasted marshmallows over the log-fire at the campsite.
mnemonicBg: Вечер не се логваш в играта, а при камината — log значи и цепеница: log-fire.

definition: Great surprise or amazement.
explanationBg: Огромно учудване — когато нещо те смае така, че оставаш с отворена уста.
explanationEn: Very great surprise.
exampleEn: To everyone's astonishment, the quietest kid in class won the rap battle.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие stone (камък) — от изумление се вкаменяваш на място.
bookSentenceEn: He said he was thinking of writing a book (at which there was silent **astonishment**), and that he and his friends wanted to collect information about hobbits living outside the Shire, especially in the eastern lands.

definition: Having eyes that look in different directions; cross-eyed.
explanationBg: Кривоглед — с очи, които гледат в различни посоки или с присвит, кос поглед.
explanationEn: Having eyes that look in different directions.
exampleEn: The kitten was slightly squint-eyed, which made her look adorably confused.
mnemonicBg: Представи си очи, които играят на жмичка едно с друго — всяко гледа в своя посока: squint-eyed.
bookSentenceEn: One of the travellers, a **squint-eyed** ill-favoured fellow, was foretelling that more and more people would be coming north in the near future.

definition: Having an unpleasant appearance; ugly.
explanationBg: Грозноват, неприятен на вид — външност, която природата не е поглезила с хубост.
explanationEn: Not nice to look at; rather ugly.
exampleEn: The game's villain is ill-favoured on purpose, so you distrust him at first sight.
mnemonicBg: Ill (зле) + favour (услуга): външността не му е направила услуга.
bookSentenceEn: One of the travellers, a squint-eyed **ill-favoured** fellow, was foretelling that more and more people would be coming north in the near future.

definition: A rented room or rooms in another person’s house.
explanationBg: Квартира — стая или стаи под наем в чужда къща, където отсядаш за известно време.
explanationEn: A rented room or rooms where someone stays.
exampleEn: My cousin found cheap lodgings near the university, with a kind old landlady.
mnemonicBg: Квартирка с ЛОДЖИЯ (балконче) — lodgings: стаичка под наем с гледка.
bookSentenceEn: Big Folk could hardly beg for **lodgings** in hobbit-holes.

definition: A soft white rock; a piece used for writing or drawing.
explanationBg: Тебешир — мек бял камък, с който се пише на дъска или се рисува по асфалта.
explanationEn: A soft white stone used for writing on boards or pavements.
exampleEn: We drew a hopscotch grid on the playground with pink chalk.
mnemonicBg: „Чок-чок“ — тебеширът чука по дъската: chalk.
bookSentenceEn: Pippin roused a good deal of laughter with an account of the collapse of the roof of the Town Hole in Michel Delving: Will Whitfoot, the Mayor, and the fattest hobbit in the Westfarthing, had been buried in **chalk**, and came out like a ﬂoured dumpling.

definition: A small mass of dough cooked by boiling or steaming; (informal) a short, round person.
explanationBg: Кнедла — топче тесто, сварено в супа или на пара; шеговито така наричат и нисък, закръглен човек.
explanationEn: A small ball of boiled dough; also a playful word for a short, round person.
exampleEn: We ordered a basket of steamed dumplings at the new Asian place in the mall.
mnemonicBg: ДЪМ-плинг! — топчето тесто цопва в супата с весело „плинг“.
bookSentenceEn: Pippin roused a good deal of laughter with an account of the collapse of the roof of the Town Hole in Michel Delving: Will Whitfoot, the Mayor, and the fattest hobbit in the Westfarthing, had been buried in chalk, and came out like a ﬂoured **dumpling**.

definition: Bending and moving easily and gracefully; flexible.
explanationBg: Гъвкав — огъва се и се движи леко и плавно, без да се схваща; като гимнастичка или мека кожа.
explanationEn: Bending and moving easily; flexible.
exampleEn: Years of gymnastics have made her amazingly supple.
mnemonicBg: Като спагети в СУПа — омекват и се огъват накъдето искаш: supple.
bookSentenceEn: His legs were stretched out before him, showing high boots of **supple** leather that ﬁtted him well, but had seen much wear and were now caked with mud.

definition: The lower parts of the legs, especially between knee and ankle.
explanationBg: Пищялите — частта на крака между коляното и глезена; думата често звучи шеговито или старовремски.
explanationEn: The lower parts of the legs, below the knees.
exampleEn: After the hike through the bushes, my shanks were covered in scratches.
mnemonicBg: Дългите пищяли на спринтьора подвикват: „Нямаш ШАНС да ни стигнеш!“ — shanks.
bookSentenceEn: Goes about at a great pace on his long **shanks**; though he don’t tell nobody what cause he has to hurry.

definition: Marked or sprinkled with small spots or patches of colour.
explanationBg: Изпъстрен със ситни петънца или пръски цвят — сякаш някой го е наръсил с боя.
explanationEn: Covered with small spots or dots of colour.
exampleEn: Her white trainers came back from art class flecked with blue paint.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „леке“ вътре: ф-ЛЕКЕ-д — на ситни лекенца от боя.

definition: Serious and unrelenting, especially in the assertion of authority.
explanationBg: Строг и суров — не се шегува и не отстъпва, особено когато налага правила.
explanationEn: Very serious and strict.
exampleEn: One stern look from the coach was enough to silence the whole bench.
mnemonicBg: Гласът на строгия директор СТЪРЖЕ като шкурка — stern.
bookSentenceEn: As Frodo drew near he threw back his hood, showing a shaggy head of dark hair ﬂecked with grey, and in a pale **stern** face a pair of keen grey eyes.

definition: In a way that cannot be explained or accounted for.
explanationBg: Необяснимо — по начин, за който никой не може да каже защо или как се е случил.
explanationEn: In a way that nobody can explain.
exampleEn: My phone battery unaccountably dropped from eighty percent to five during the maths test.
mnemonicBg: Account значи сметка — нещо, което не излиза по никоя сметка, е необяснимо: unaccountably.
bookSentenceEn: He felt the Ring on its chain, and quite **unaccountably** the desire came over him to slip it on and vanish out of the silly situation.

definition: To undertake a risky or daring journey or course of action.
explanationBg: Да се осмелиш на нещо рисковано — да тръгнеш смело към непознатото, въпреки че може да е опасно.
explanationEn: To dare to do something risky or go somewhere dangerous.
exampleEn: Nobody ventured into the dark basement until Mia grabbed a flashlight and led the way.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „аВАНТЮра“ във venture — хвърляш се смело в приключение.
bookSentenceEn: He spoke ‘a few suitable words’, as they would have said in the Shire: We are all very much gratiﬁed by the kindness of your reception, and I **venture** to hope that my brief visit will help to renew the old ties of

definition: A man employed at an inn to look after the horses of guests.
explanationBg: Така едно време са наричали човека в хана, който се грижи за конете на гостите — разседлава ги, храни ги и ги прибира в конюшнята.
explanationEn: A man who worked at an inn and looked after the guests' horses.
exampleEn: On our school trip to the open-air museum, an actor played the ostler and let us help brush the horses.
mnemonicBg: Звучи почти като „осел-ър“ — представи си коняря в хана, който по погрешка вкарва осел при конете на гостите.
bookSentenceEn: The **ostler** has a tipsy cat that plays a ﬁve-stringed ﬁddle; And up and down he runs his bow, Now squeaking high, now purring low, now sawing in the middle.

definition: The back part of something; (verb) to bring up offspring.
explanationBg: Задната част на нещо — на автобус, кола или сграда. Като глагол значи и да отглеждаш деца или малки животни.
explanationEn: The back part of something; as a verb, to raise children or young animals.
exampleEn: We always grab the seats at the rear of the bus so we can chat in peace.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „rear-view mirror“ — огледалото в колата, което гледа точно НАЗАД.
bookSentenceEn: They rolled the Man slowly up the hill and bundled him into the Moon, While his horses galloped up in **rear**, And the cow came capering like a deer, and a dish ran up with the spoon. * See note 2, III, p. 1462

definition: Skipping or dancing about in a lively or playful way.
explanationBg: Весело подскачане и лудуване — като козле на поляна, което скача насам-натам от чиста радост.
explanationEn: Jumping and dancing around in a playful, happy way.
exampleEn: The puppy started capering around the yard the second we picked up its leash.
mnemonicBg: „Caper“ и „каприз“ идват от една и съща дума за коза — представи си капризно козле, което подскача и лудува.
bookSentenceEn: They rolled the Man slowly up the hill and bundled him into the Moon, While his horses galloped up in rear, And the cow came **capering** like a deer, and a dish ran up with the spoon. * See note 2, III, p. 1462

definition: (Of a person) having a dark complexion or skin.
explanationBg: Мургав — с тъмна кожа или тъмен тен, най-вече на лицето.
explanationEn: Having naturally dark skin, especially on the face.
exampleEn: The lifeguard was a tall, swarthy young man who seemed to live on the beach.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за Арнолд ШВАРЦ-енегер — „шварц“ значи черен, а swarthy е човек с тъмна, мургава кожа.
bookSentenceEn: But there was one **swarthy** Bree-lander, who stood looking at them with a knowing and half-mocking expression that made them feel very uncomfortable.

definition: Reports or descriptions that disagree with each other.
explanationBg: Разкази за едно и също събитие, които си противоречат — всеки свидетел разправя различна версия и историите не се връзват.
explanationEn: Different reports about the same event that do not agree with each other.
exampleEn: The teacher heard so many conflicting accounts of the corridor fight that she gave up finding the truth.
mnemonicBg: Конфликт между разказите — версиите се „карат“ помежду си и не могат да се разберат коя е вярната.

definition: Earthenware pots or jars.
explanationBg: Глинени гърнета и делви — съдове от печена глина, в които някога са държали мляко, мед или туршия.
explanationEn: Pots and jars made of baked clay.
exampleEn: Grandma still keeps her homemade pickles in heavy crocks in the cellar.
mnemonicBg: „Крок!“ — звукът, когато глинено гърне се чукне в друго; crocks са точно такива гърнета.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Frightening my customers and breaking up my **crocks** with your acrobatics!’

definition: Bundles of sticks or twigs bound together as fuel.
explanationBg: Снопчета съчки, вързани заедно, за да се пали с тях огън — едно време така са носели дървата за горене.
explanationEn: Bundles of sticks tied together for burning on a fire.
exampleEn: We tied the dry twigs into faggots so the campfire would light faster.
mnemonicBg: Представи си музикалния ФАГОТ, само че направен от съчки — стегнат дълъг сноп дръвца за огъня.
bookSentenceEn: It was not until they had puffed up the embers into a blaze and thrown on a couple of **faggots** that they discovered Strider had come with them.

definition: A mischievous or cheeky person, especially a child or man.
explanationBg: Палавник и хитрец — най-често дете, което прави бели, но е толкова чаровно, че не можеш да му се сърдиш дълго. Казва се и за непочтен човек.
explanationEn: A cheeky person, often a child, who plays tricks and gets into mischief.
exampleEn: My little brother is a proper rascal — he hid my phone and recorded me searching for it.
mnemonicBg: РАЗ-КАЛ-ян хлапак — пак е газил в калта, хили се до уши и вече крои следващата беля: rascal.
bookSentenceEn: He suspected now that he had fallen in with a **rascal**, and he thought uncomfortably that he had brought only a little money with him.

definition: A dishonest or unprincipled person; a mischievous person.
explanationBg: Мошеник — човек без задръжки, който лъже и мами за своя изгода. Понякога се казва и по-меко, за чаровен немирник.
explanationEn: A dishonest person who tricks others; sometimes a charming troublemaker.
exampleEn: The man selling 'brand new' earbuds at the market turned out to be a rogue — they died in two days.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „рог“ — щом намисли измама, на мошеника му никнат дяволски рогчета: rogue.
bookSentenceEn: All of it would hardly satisfy a **rogue**, and he could not spare any of it.

definition: An angry or bad-tempered facial expression.
explanationBg: Сърдито, навъсено изражение — смръщени вежди и поглед, който казва „не ме закачай“.
explanationEn: An angry frown on someone's face.
exampleEn: Maria's smile turned into a scowl when the teacher announced a surprise test.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие „owl“ (сова) — представи си навъсена сова, която те гледа мрачно изпод вежди: scOWL.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Now, don’t mistake me!’ he cried, as Frodo rose from his seat, and Sam jumped up with a **scowl**.

definition: People who wander from place to place without a settled home or job.
explanationBg: Скитници — хора без постоянен дом и работа, които бродят от място на място и никъде не се задържат.
explanationEn: People who wander from place to place with no fixed home or job.
exampleEn: In the summer we joked about becoming vagabonds and hiking across Europe with one backpack.
mnemonicBg: На български си имаме същата дума — „вагабонтин“: скитник, който броди където му видят очите.
bookSentenceEn: Only he does not altogether like mysterious **vagabonds** of my sort.’

definition: Like a rascal; mischievously dishonest.
explanationBg: Хитро и дяволито, по маниера на палавник — с лека доза непочтеност, но повече закачка.
explanationEn: Behaving like a rascal — playful, cheeky and a bit dishonest.
exampleEn: That rascally cat from next door steals socks from half the street.
mnemonicBg: Просто „rascal“ + „-ly“: всичко, направено като от разкаляния палавник — хитро, дяволито, мошенически.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Well, I have rather a **rascally** look, have I not?’ said Strider with a curl of his lip and a queer gleam in his eye.

definition: Smiling or speaking in a contemptuous or mocking way.
explanationBg: Който гледа или говори с крива усмивка и презрение — все едно ти казва, че си под нивото му.
explanationEn: Smiling or speaking in a mocking way that shows contempt.
exampleEn: His sneering comments every time someone makes a mistake ruin the whole class chat.
mnemonicBg: „Sneer“ започва като „snake“ — представи си змия с крива, подигравателна усмивчица, която те гледа отвисоко.
bookSentenceEn: You must have noticed him among the company: a swarthy **sneering** fellow.

definition: A split or indentation between two parts; a fissure.
explanationBg: Цепнатина или процеп — тясно разделение между две части, например в скала или на брадичката.
explanationEn: A narrow split or crack between two parts of something.
exampleEn: We wedged the climbing rope into a cleft in the rock before going down.
mnemonicBg: „Клъц!“ — ножицата клъцва и оставя тесен процеп: cleft звучи точно като бързо „клъц“.
bookSentenceEn: ‘ But this one is taller than some and fairer than most, and he has a **cleft** in his chin: perky chap with a bright eye.

definition: Done with excessive speed or urgency; hurried.
explanationBg: Прибързан — направен на крак, без да се помисли. От такова бързане често се раждат глупави грешки.
explanationEn: Done too quickly, without enough thought.
exampleEn: My hasty answer on the last question cost me five points.
mnemonicBg: „Хей-СТОЙ!“ — викаш на припрения приятел, хукнал нанякъде, преди да е чул целия план: hasty.
bookSentenceEn: He’s a bit **hasty**.

definition: A dangerous, difficult, or otherwise unfortunate situation.
explanationBg: Тежко, окаяно положение — беда, в която някой е закъсал и от която трудно ще се измъкне сам.
explanationEn: A difficult or dangerous situation that someone is in.
exampleEn: The documentary showed the plight of stray dogs left out in the cold.
mnemonicBg: Като „flight“ без F: самолетът излита, а ти оставаш на летището без билет и багаж — ето това е plight.
bookSentenceEn: ‘But if I was in your **plight**, I wouldn’t take up with a Ranger.’

definition: A person’s head, especially the top of it.
explanationBg: Шеговита, старомодна дума за главата — най-вече за темето, горната ѝ част.
explanationEn: A person's head, especially the top of it.
exampleEn: Dad rubbed sunscreen on his bald pate before the beach volleyball game.
mnemonicBg: Пише се като „пате“ — представи си жълто пате, кацнало върху голото теме на чичо ти.
bookSentenceEn: Even our Nob has been doing some guessing in his slow **pate**; and there are others in Bree quicker in the uptake than he is.’

definition: The ability to understand something quickly ("quick on the uptake").
explanationBg: Бързината, с която схващаш нещо ново — за човек, който загрява моментално, се казва, че е бърз в схващането.
explanationEn: How quickly someone understands new information.
exampleEn: Lena is so quick on the uptake that she learned the new card game in one round.
mnemonicBg: Up + take: мозъкът „взема нагоре“ информацията като асансьор — щом стигне горе, лампичката светва.
bookSentenceEn: Even our Nob has been doing some guessing in his slow pate; and there are others in Bree quicker in the **uptake** than he is.’

definition: Ghosts or apparitions; supernatural beings.
explanationBg: Призраци и духове — съществата от страшните истории, които уж се появяват нощем.
explanationEn: Ghosts or spirits.
exampleEn: We told stories about spooks around the campfire until nobody dared walk to the tents alone.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш „spooky“ от Хелоуин — spooks са самите призрачета, които изскачат с „Буу!“.
bookSentenceEn: ‘But **spooks** or no spooks, they won’t get in The Pony so easy.

definition: With little or no delay; immediately.
explanationBg: Незабавно, без никакво бавене — нещо става на момента, веднага.
explanationEn: Immediately, without delay.
exampleEn: She answered my message so promptly that I had not even locked my phone.
mnemonicBg: Като промпт към чатбот — пращаш го и отговорът цъфва НА СЕКУНДАТА: promptly.
bookSentenceEn: PPPS. I hope Butterbur sends this **promptly**.

definition: A room used to store unused or unwanted articles.
explanationBg: Стая за стари и ненужни вещи — там се трупат счупени столове, кашони и прашни куфари.
explanationEn: A room where people store old things they no longer use.
exampleEn: We found Mum's old vinyl records in the lumber-room behind a broken wardrobe.
mnemonicBg: Room = стая, lumber = стари дъски и мебели: стаята-пенсия, където вехториите отиват да си доживеят.

definition: To make or become tired; to lose patience or interest.
explanationBg: Уморява или изтощава — изцежда ти силите или търпението, докато съвсем ти писне.
explanationEn: Makes someone tired or bored.
exampleEn: Studying for three tests in one week wearies even the best students.
mnemonicBg: Произнеси го с прозявка — „уиъ-риз“ — звучи като човек, на когото вече не му останаха сили: wearies = уморява.
bookSentenceEn: A hunted man sometimes **wearies** of distrust and longs for friendship.

definition: Discouraged or intimidated.
explanationBg: Обезкуражен и поуплашен от нещо, което изглежда прекалено трудно — ръцете ти увисват още преди да си започнал.
explanationEn: Feeling discouraged or a bit scared by something difficult.
exampleEn: I felt daunted by the size of the climbing wall, but I still reached the top.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „down“ вътре — нещо те смъква надолу духом и ти идва да се откажеш: daunted.
bookSentenceEn: Pippin subsided; but Sam was not **daunted**, and he still eyed Strider dubiously.

definition: News; information.
explanationBg: Старовремска дума за новини и вести — онова, което вестоносецът идва да съобщи.
explanationEn: An old word for news.
exampleEn: Grandpa always asks for tidings from school when I visit him on Sundays.
mnemonicBg: Като прилива („tide“) новините идват на вълни — tidings са вести, които доплуват до теб.
bookSentenceEn: The **tidings** had gone far and wide that Gandalf was missing and the horsemen had been seen.

definition: Held back or delayed; impeded.
explanationBg: Спъван, забавян — нещо ти пречи да вървиш напред или да си свършиш работата гладко.
explanationEn: Slowed down or blocked from making progress.
exampleEn: Our hike was hindered by deep mud that grabbed our trainers at every step.
mnemonicBg: „Хиндърд“ — все едно някой те е хванал за раницата и те дърпа назад, докато ти напираш напред.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I do not know of anything else that could have **hindered** him, except the Enemy himself,’ said Strider.

definition: A tight grasp or hold; a small bag carried by a woman.
explanationBg: Здраво стискане, хватка — сграбчваш нещо и не го пускаш. Така се нарича и малка дамска чанта, която се носи стисната в ръка.
explanationEn: A very tight hold or grip on something.
exampleEn: The goalkeeper kept the ball in such a firm clutch that nobody could knock it free.
mnemonicBg: Геймърите казват „клъч момент“ — стискаш контролера до побеляване и удържаш сам: clutch = желязна хватка.
bookSentenceEn: But their power is in terror, and already some in Bree are in their **clutch**.

definition: Unfortunate or unhappy people; despicable or contemptible people.
explanationBg: Клетници — нещастни хора, за които ти става мъчно; казано със злоба, значи и жалки негодници.
explanationEn: Poor, unhappy people; or people you despise.
exampleEn: The kittens looked like tiny soaked wretches after the storm, so we dried them with a towel.
mnemonicBg: „Речиз“ — представи си подгизнали клетници край реката, които мърморят тъжни речи под носа си.
bookSentenceEn: They will drive these **wretches** to some evil work: Ferny, and some of the strangers, and, maybe, the gatekeeper too.

definition: Thinking about something carefully, especially for a long time.
explanationBg: Дълго и внимателно мислене — въртиш въпроса в главата си от всички страни, преди да решиш.
explanationEn: Thinking about something slowly and carefully.
exampleEn: I spent the whole bus ride pondering whether to join the volleyball team or the drama club.
mnemonicBg: Седнал ПОД ДЪРвото като мислител — ponder-ing: дълбоко размишляване на сянка.
bookSentenceEn: Merry was still reading and **pondering** Gandalf ’s letter when Strider and Nob returned.

definition: A long, firm pillow or cushion placed under a regular pillow for support.
explanationBg: Дълга, твърда възглавница, която се слага под обикновената за опора — като мек валяк по цялата ширина на леглото.
explanationEn: A long, firm pillow that supports your normal pillow.
exampleEn: The hotel bed had a giant bolster, so I used it as a wall against my snoring brother.
mnemonicBg: БОЛярска възглавница — болярите се изтягали върху дълги, твърди възглавници-валяци: bolster.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Well Masters,’ said Nob, ‘I’ve rufﬂed up the clothes and put in a **bolster** down the middle of each bed.

definition: Succeeded in forcing a way into or through (something).
explanationBg: Проникнал — успял да си пробие път навътре или да мине през нещо въпреки преградата.
explanationEn: Managed to force a way into or through something.
exampleEn: The cold penetrated my jacket before the ski lift reached the top.
mnemonicBg: Представи си монетка, която се промушва през тесния процеп на касичката — penetrate: прониквам.
bookSentenceEn: ‘But what will happen when they have **penetrated** the disguise?’

definition: Cautious and surreptitious action or movement.
explanationBg: Тихо, скрито действие или промъкване — правиш нещо така, че никой да не те усети.
explanationEn: Moving or acting quietly and secretly so nobody notices.
exampleEn: He finished the whole level in stealth, without alerting a single guard.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш stealth мисиите в игрите — промъкваш се приведен и безшумен и никой не те засича.
bookSentenceEn: There came the soft sound of horses led with **stealth** along the lane.

definition: Drawn out of a sheath or covering; bared.
explanationBg: Изваден от ножницата или калъфа — за меч или нож, който вече е оголен и готов за действие.
explanationEn: Pulled out of its cover, ready for use (usually a blade).
exampleEn: The chef unsheathed his favourite knife and sliced the tomatoes like a TV star.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „шиш“ по средата — изваждаш лъскавия шиш от калъфа му: un-ШИЙТ-d, оголен и готов.
bookSentenceEn: In the dark without moon or stars a drawn blade gleamed, as if a chill light had been **unsheathed**.

definition: Wooden beams or planks, especially used in building or ships.
explanationBg: Дървени греди и дебели дъски — едрият строителен материал за къщи, покриви и кораби.
explanationEn: Large wooden beams or planks used for building.
exampleEn: The old gym's roof timbers creak whenever the wind picks up.
mnemonicBg: „ТИМБЪР!“ — викът при падащо отсечено дърво (познат и от Minecraft); от тези дървета стават гредите: timbers.
bookSentenceEn: At a second blow the door yielded and fell back, with **timbers** burst and lock broken.

definition: To suffer death, typically in a violent or sudden way.
explanationBg: Да загинеш — да умреш внезапно, обикновено при бедствие, студ или катастрофа.
explanationEn: To die, especially suddenly or in a disaster.
exampleEn: Without water even the toughest cactus on my windowsill will perish.
mnemonicBg: Ако ПЕРЕШ телефона си в пералнята, той ще perish — загива геройски на 40 градуса.
bookSentenceEn: As soon as he saw the dark shapes creep from the garden, he knew that he must run for it, or **perish**.

definition: A loud, resonant metallic sound.
explanationBg: Силен, кънтящ метален звук — като удар на камбана или изтървана тенджера върху плочки.
explanationEn: A loud ringing sound made by metal hitting something.
exampleEn: The clang of the school bell made the whole corridor jump.
mnemonicBg: КЛАНГ! — думата сама си прави звука: изтърви металната тава и я чуй как се представя по име.
bookSentenceEn: Strider had drawn the curtains and pushed back the shutters with a **clang**.

definition: Long firm pillows or cushions used for support.
explanationBg: Дълги, твърди възглавници за опора — нареждат се по ширината на леглото или зад гърба.
explanationEn: Long, firm pillows used for support.
exampleEn: We lined up the sofa bolsters into a wall for our movie-night fort.
mnemonicBg: Пак болярските възглавници — цял куп дълги, твърди валяци, наредени на леглото: bolsters.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Guests unable to sleep in their beds, and good **bolsters** ruined and all!

definition: A piece of coarse material placed on the floor or used as a covering.
explanationBg: Постелка от груб или дебел материал, която стои на пода — пред врата, в банята или за тренировка.
explanationEn: A piece of thick material that you put on the floor.
exampleEn: Coach told us to wipe our trainers on the mat before stepping into the hall.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш „йога мат“ — постелката за пода; баба би ѝ казала рогозка.
bookSentenceEn: When they saw them they were glad that they had taken his advice: the windows had been forced open and were swinging, and the curtains were ﬂapping; the beds were tossed about, and the bolsters slashed and ﬂung upon the ﬂoor; the brown **mat** was torn to pieces.

definition: Concern and distress caused by something unexpected.
explanationBg: Смут и тревога от неприятна изненада — оставаш слисан, защото нещата изведнъж тръгват на зле.
explanationEn: A worried, unhappy feeling caused by an unpleasant surprise.
exampleEn: To my dismay, the concert sold out while my payment was still loading.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „май“ вътре — „МАЙко мила!“ възкликваш при лошата изненада: dis-MAY.
bookSentenceEn: But very soon he came back in **dismay**.

definition: In a way that shows open resistance or bold disobedience.
explanationBg: Непокорно, напук — с цялото си поведение показваш, че няма да се подчиниш, и то пред очите на всички.
explanationEn: In a bold way that shows you refuse to obey.
exampleEn: She defiantly kept her headphones on after the coach told everyone to line up.
mnemonicBg: Представи си я как ДЕФИлира с вирната брадичка точно покрай забранителната табела — defiantly, напук.

definition: Entering someone’s land or property without permission.
explanationBg: Влизане в чужд имот без разрешение — да прескочиш ограда или да минеш през двор, където нямаш работа.
explanationEn: Going onto someone's land without permission.
exampleEn: The farmer yelled that we were trespassing when we hopped the fence after our ball.
mnemonicBg: ТРЯС + pass: минаваш през чуждия двор, оградата прави „тряс“ и кучето вече тича към теб.
bookSentenceEn: Any attempt to set off across country at once would only make matters worse: half the inhabitants would follow them, to see what they were up to, and to prevent them from **trespassing**.

definition: Not marked by interesting or exciting events.
explanationBg: Спокоен, без особени случки — ден или пътуване, в които не става нищо вълнуващо (а понякога точно това е хубавото).
explanationEn: Quiet and ordinary, with nothing exciting happening.
exampleEn: The flight home was completely uneventful — I slept the whole way.
mnemonicBg: Un + event: ден без нито един „ивент“ в календара — нула случки, нула драма.
bookSentenceEn: Frodo’s vanishing trick; the appearance of the black horsemen; the robbing of the stables; and not least the news that Strider the Ranger had joined the mysterious hobbits, made such a tale as would last for many **uneventful** years.

definition: Sad and depressed; dispirited.
explanationBg: Унил и без капка настроение — главата клюмва, раменете увисват, духът е на нулата.
explanationEn: Feeling very sad and without hope.
exampleEn: The team walked off dejected after losing the final on penalties.
mnemonicBg: Като „eject“ в игрите — животът те е изхвърлил от мача и седиш унил на пейката: dejected.
bookSentenceEn: He walked in front with Frodo; next came Merry and Pippin; and last came Sam leading the pony, which was laden with as much of their baggage as they had the heart to give it; but already it looked less **dejected**, as if it approved of the change in its fortunes.

definition: A state of confused and noisy disturbance.
explanationBg: Шумна суматоха — викове, тичане и блъсканица, при които никой не разбира какво всъщност става.
explanationEn: A lot of noise and confused movement.
exampleEn: A wasp in the cafeteria caused a huge commotion at lunch.
mnemonicBg: Co + motion: всички в движение едновременно — стаята кипва като разклатена газирана вода: commotion.
bookSentenceEn: For there was a great **commotion** as soon as the remaining guests were astir and heard news of the raid on the inn.

definition: A rapid surprise attack on an enemy by troops or by police.
explanationBg: Внезапно, светкавично нападение — връхлиташ изненадващо, удряш бързо и изчезваш.
explanationEn: A quick surprise attack on a place.
exampleEn: Our clan planned a midnight raid on the rival base in the game.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш „рейд“ от игрите — изненадващ удар по чуждата база; точно това значи и на английски.
bookSentenceEn: For there was a great commotion as soon as the remaining guests were astir and heard news of the **raid** on the inn.

definition: In a state of excited movement; in motion or awake.
explanationBg: Раздвижен и буден — всичко живо е на крак, нещо се случва и никой вече не спи.
explanationEn: Awake and moving around; full of activity.
exampleEn: By six in the morning the campsite was astir with people packing their tents.
mnemonicBg: A + stir (разбърквам): все едно гигантска лъжица е разбъркала къщата и всички са се завъртели на крак.
bookSentenceEn: For there was a great commotion as soon as the remaining guests were **astir** and heard news of the raid on the inn.

definition: (Of a person’s face or complexion) of an unhealthy yellow or pale brown colour.
explanationBg: Болнаво жълтеникав тен на лицето — кожа без свежест, която издава умора или болест.
explanationEn: Having slightly yellow, unhealthy-looking skin.
exampleEn: After a week of flu his face looked sallow in every photo.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „САЛо“ — жълтеникаво-бледо като стара сланина: sallow тен.
bookSentenceEn: In one of the windows he caught a glimpse of a **sallow** face with sly, slanting eyes; but it vanished at once.

definition: Feeling or expressing contempt or derision.
explanationBg: Изпълнен с презрение — гледаш или говориш така, сякаш отсреща стои нещо жалко и недостойно.
explanationEn: Showing that you think someone deserves no respect.
exampleEn: Her scornful look when I mentioned my favourite band honestly stung.
mnemonicBg: Презрителен като СКОРпион с вдигната опашка — гледа те отвисоко и съска: scornful.
bookSentenceEn: He had heavy black brows, and dark **scornful** eyes; his large mouth curled in a sneer.

definition: Walked with long, decisive steps in a continued manner.
explanationBg: Продължи напред с дълги, решителни крачки — без спиране и без обръщане назад.
explanationEn: Kept walking forward with long, confident steps.
exampleEn: Ignoring the rain, the coach strode on across the pitch to check the goal.
mnemonicBg: Като войник в СТРОя — дълги, отсечени крачки все напред: strode on.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Waste of a good apple,’ said Sam regretfully, and **strode on**.

definition: People who lag behind a group or fail to keep up.
explanationBg: Тези, които се влачат най-отзад и изостават от групата — последните, които всички чакат.
explanationEn: People who fall behind the rest of the group.
exampleEn: The teacher stood at the museum door, counting the stragglers from our class.
mnemonicBg: Чуй как „стръ-гъл-ърс“ стържат с подметки по асфалта — влачат се последни и едва пъплят.
bookSentenceEn: The escort of children and **stragglers** that had followed them got tired and turned back at the South-gate.

definition: Low-lying lands that are flooded in wet seasons.
explanationBg: Ниски, блатисти земи, които се наводняват през дъждовните сезони — меки, мокри и обрасли с тръстика.
explanationEn: Low, wet land that floods in rainy seasons.
exampleEn: On the biology field trip we watched herons hunting frogs in the marshes.
mnemonicBg: „МАРШ през блатото!“ — и обувките тръгват с жвак-жвак през мочурищата: marshes.
bookSentenceEn: They were far beyond the borders of the Bree-land, out in the pathless wilderness, and drawing near to the Midgewater **Marshes**.

definition: Twisting turns or bends, especially as in a path or river.
explanationBg: Извивки и резки завои — например когато пътека или река криволичи ту насам, ту натам.
explanationEn: Twists and turns, for example in a path or a river.
exampleEn: The mountain trail had so many doublings that we lost all sense of direction.
mnemonicBg: В doublings се крие double („двойно“): пътеката се сгъва на две — завой, пак завой, като двойно прегъната панделка.
bookSentenceEn: He was taking a wandering course with many turns and **doublings**, to put off any pursuit.

definition: (Of a bird) singing with a succession of high quavering notes.
explanationBg: Пеене на птица с високи, трептящи тонове, които се преливат един в друг — нежно чуруликане с трели.
explanationEn: Singing with high, shaky musical notes, like a bird.
exampleEn: We woke up to a blackbird warbling outside our tent at sunrise.
mnemonicBg: „Уор-БЛИНГ“ — представи си птиче с лъскав „блинг“ медальон, което се фука на клона и сипе трели.
bookSentenceEn: The ground now became damp, and in places boggy and here and there they came upon pools, and wide stretches of reeds and rushes ﬁlled with the **warbling** of little hidden birds.

definition: Crossing or walking without wetting one’s feet.
explanationBg: Да преминеш през вода или кално място, без да си намокриш краката — да минеш „на сухо“.
explanationEn: Crossing or walking somewhere without getting your feet wet.
exampleEn: We hopped across the stepping stones and reached the other bank dry-footed.
mnemonicBg: Dry = сухо, foot = крак: скачаш по камъните като нинджа и маратонките ти остават сухи.
bookSentenceEn: They had to pick their way carefully to keep both **dry-footed** and on their proper course.

definition: Soft boggy areas of land that give way underfoot.
explanationBg: Меки, блатисти места, където земята поддава под краката ти и можеш да затънеш.
explanationEn: Soft, muddy areas of ground that sink under your feet.
exampleEn: After a week of rain, the fields around our campsite turned into quagmires that swallowed our trainers.
mnemonicBg: „КВАГ-майър“ — чуй „ква“: където жабата квака, там е quagmire — стъпиш ли, затъваш.
bookSentenceEn: The marshes were bewildering and treacherous, and there was no permanent trail even for Rangers to ﬁnd through their shifting **quagmires**.

definition: Small two-winged flies that occur in swarms, especially near water.
explanationBg: Дребни хвърчащи мушици, които се събират на цели рояци, най-вече около вода.
explanationEn: Tiny flies that gather in big swarms, especially near water.
exampleEn: A cloud of midges attacked us the moment we sat down by the lake.
mnemonicBg: Midges звучи като „мижи“: рояк мушици ти налита в очите и ти мижиш, за да се спасиш.
bookSentenceEn: Though the Neekerbreekers (as Sam called them) had been left behind, the **midges** still pursued them.

definition: Small, dense bushy clumps of grass.
explanationBg: Малки, гъсти китки трева, които стърчат над земята като бухнали възглавнички.
explanationEn: Small thick clumps of grass that stick up from the ground.
exampleEn: The meadow was full of tussocks, so running across it felt like an obstacle course.
mnemonicBg: Tussock звучи почти като „туфичка“ — туфа трева, щръкнала като рошава коса след сън.
bookSentenceEn: There were also abominable creatures haunting the reeds and **tussocks** that from the sound of them were evil relatives of the cricket.

definition: Wild or distraught with fear, anxiety, or other emotion.
explanationBg: Обезумял от страх, тревога или друго силно чувство — в пълна паника, без капка спокойствие.
explanationEn: So worried, scared, or excited that you cannot stay calm.
exampleEn: I was frantic when I couldn't find my phone five minutes before the exam.
mnemonicBg: „ФРАН-тик“ — Франи с нервен тик търчи из стаята минута преди изпита: паника на макс.
bookSentenceEn: There were thousands of them, and they squeaked all round, neek-breek, breek-neek, unceasingly all the night, until the hobbits were nearly **frantic**.

definition: Spread out untidily over a large area; falling behind a main body.
explanationBg: Разпилян безредно върху голяма площ; или влачещ се най-отзад, изостанал от групата.
explanationEn: Spread out in a messy way, or falling behind the rest of a group.
exampleEn: A few straggling runners crossed the finish line long after the rest of the class.
mnemonicBg: Представи си екскурзия: групата отпред, а двама се мъкнат най-отзад с телефони в ръка — те са straggling.
bookSentenceEn: They had not gone far on the ﬁfth day when they left the last **straggling** pools and reed-beds of the marshes behind them.

definition: An uncultivated, uninhabited, and inhospitable region.
explanationBg: Дива, необитаема и негостоприемна местност — без хора, къщи и пътища, само природа.
explanationEn: A wild area with no people, houses, or farms.
exampleEn: Our scout camp was deep in the wilderness, two hours from the nearest shop.
mnemonicBg: В wilderness няма Wi-Fi — само wild („диво“): пустош без хора и без обхват.
bookSentenceEn: If the Riders fail to ﬁnd us in the **wilderness**, they are likely to make for Weathertop themselves.

definition: Sad because of lack of friends or company; lonely.
explanationBg: Тъжен, защото си сам и ти липсва компания — самотен и оклюмал.
explanationEn: Feeling sad because you are alone.
exampleEn: The first week at the new school felt pretty lonesome until I met Maya.
mnemonicBg: Lonesome завършва като „сам съм“: лоун-СЪМ — сам съм и ми е криво.
bookSentenceEn: ‘You do make me feel uncomfortable and **lonesome**, Strider!’ he said.

definition: Walked doggedly and slowly with heavy steps.
explanationBg: Вървеше бавно, упорито и с тежки стъпки — мъкнеше се напред въпреки умората.
explanationEn: Walked slowly and heavily, without giving up.
exampleEn: We plodded up the last hill with our heavy backpacks, dreaming of pizza.
mnemonicBg: „ПЛОД-ид“ — мъкнеш чувал с плодове и стъпваш тежко: плод… плод… plodded.
bookSentenceEn: All that day they **plodded** along, until the cold and early evening came down.

definition: (Of land) too poor to produce much or any vegetation; bleak.
explanationBg: За земя — толкова бедна, че по нея почти нищо не расте; гола и пуста.
explanationEn: Land that is too poor for plants to grow on.
exampleEn: Nothing grew in that barren corner of the garden, no matter what we planted.
mnemonicBg: „Барен“ се римува с „бурен“: на barren земя не никне дори бурен.
bookSentenceEn: The land became drier and more **barren**; but mists and vapours lay behind them on the marshes.

definition: (Of water or air) not flowing; showing no activity.
explanationBg: За вода или въздух — който не тече и стои на едно място; без движение, често с мирис на застояло.
explanationEn: Not moving or flowing, like old water in a pond.
exampleEn: The water in the abandoned pool was stagnant and smelled awful.
mnemonicBg: Като „стагнация“ — всичко е спряло: водата стои, не мърда и мирише на застояло.
bookSentenceEn: a knife in the dark 241 At the day’s end they came to a stream that wandered down from the hills to lose itself in the **stagnant** marshland, and they went up along its banks while the light lasted.

definition: Land that consists of marshes; wetland.
explanationBg: Земя, покрита с блата и мочури — мокра, мека и кална, с висока трева и вода навсякъде.
explanationEn: An area of soft, wet land full of marshes.
exampleEn: The birdwatching club visits the marshland every spring to photograph the herons.
mnemonicBg: Marsh звучи като „марш!“: „Марш в калта!“ — и цопваш в мочурището.
