bookSentenceEn: a knife in the dark 241 At the day’s end they came to a stream that wandered down from the hills to lose itself in the stagnant **marshland**, and they went up along its banks while the light lasted.

definition: A piece of open land for public use, especially in a village.
explanationBg: Открито място в село или градче, което е общо за всички — всеки може да го ползва за паша, игри или разходка.
explanationEn: Open land in a village or town that everyone can use.
exampleEn: After school we meet on the commons to kick a ball around.
mnemonicBg: Commons идва от common („общ“) — като „комуна“: общата поляна на цялото село.
bookSentenceEn: Already they were getting used to much walking on short **commons** – shorter at any rate than what in the Shire they would have thought barely enough to keep them on their legs.

definition: A ghost or ghostlike image of someone, especially seen shortly before death.
explanationBg: Призрак или призрачно видение на човек — според старите поверия се появява малко преди смъртта му.
explanationEn: A ghost, or a ghost-like image of a person.
exampleEn: In the horror game, a pale wraith drifts through the walls of the old mansion.
mnemonicBg: Wraith звучи като „рейт“ (rate): призрак, който ти дава пет звезди рейтинг и се стопява през стената.
bookSentenceEn: I hope the thinning process will not go on indeﬁnitely, or I shall become **a wraith**.’

definition: The playing of pipes; a thin high sound.
explanationBg: Свирене на свирки или гайди; също така тънък, висок звук — като писукане.
explanationEn: The sound of playing pipes, or any thin, high sound.
exampleEn: We heard the piping of a flute coming from the music room.
mnemonicBg: Pipe = тръба: духни през тръбичка и излиза тънко „пиииип“ — това е piping.
bookSentenceEn: A few melancholy birds were **piping** and wailing, until the round red sun sank slowly into the western shadows; then an empty silence fell.

definition: Substances diffused or suspended in the air, especially mist or fume.
explanationBg: Изпарения, мъгла или дим, които се носят разтворени във въздуха.
explanationEn: Mist, steam, or fumes floating in the air.
exampleEn: Strange vapours rose from the chemistry teacher's demonstration, so we all stepped back.
mnemonicBg: „ВЕЙ-пърс“ — като облачето от вейп: пара, която се носи и стопява във въздуха.
bookSentenceEn: The land became drier and more barren; but mists and **vapours** lay behind them on the marshes.

definition: (Of an area of land) bare, exposed, and not welcoming; harsh.
explanationBg: За местност — гола, брулена от вятъра и неприветлива; сурова и мрачна на вид.
explanationEn: Bare, cold-looking, and not welcoming.
exampleEn: The beach looked bleak in November — grey sky, empty sand, icy wind.
mnemonicBg: Bleak звучи като „блед“: бледа, гола и мрачна земя без капка цвят.
bookSentenceEn: Ahead there loomed now against the dusky sky the **bleak** and treeless backs of the hills.

definition: Sincere and intense conviction; seriousness.
explanationBg: Искрена и дълбока убеденост; сериозност, с която човек влага цялото си сърце в нещо.
explanationEn: Deep sincerity and seriousness about something.
exampleEn: She talked about the recycling project with such earnestness that even the back row listened.
mnemonicBg: Представи си най-сериозния отличник Ърнест (Earnest): говори искрено и никога не се шегува.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Do not speak of such things!’ said Strider quickly, and with surprising **earnestness**.

definition: Having a smoothly rising and falling form or movement.
explanationBg: Който плавно се издига и спуска като вълни — например хълмист терен или полюшващо се жито.
explanationEn: Rising and falling smoothly, like waves.
exampleEn: The cycling route winds through undulating hills outside the city.
mnemonicBg: Като „ондулация“ на коса — вълни нагоре-надолу: undulating е вълнист като къдрици.
bookSentenceEn: They made an **undulating** ridge, often rising almost to a thousand feet, and here and there falling again to low clefts or passes leading into the eastern land beyond.

definition: Long walls or embankments built to prevent flooding; ditches.
explanationBg: Дълги стени или насипи, строени да спират наводнения; понякога така се наричат и изкопани ровове.
explanationEn: Long walls of earth built to stop water from flooding the land.
exampleEn: On our trip to the Netherlands we cycled along the dikes that hold back the sea.
mnemonicBg: Лесно: dike = дига — почти същата дума: стена-насип срещу водата.
bookSentenceEn: Along the crest of the ridge the hobbits could see what looked to be the remains of green-grown walls and **dikes**, and in the clefts there still stood the ruins of old works of stone.

definition: (Past participle of hew) chopped, cut, or shaped with rough strokes.
explanationBg: Изсечен или издялан с груби удари — за камък или дърво, обработени с брадва или длето.
explanationEn: Cut or shaped roughly with a tool like an axe.
exampleEn: The benches around the campfire were hewn from old logs.
mnemonicBg: „ХЮ-ън“ — дървар замахва: „хън!“ — и дънерът е издялан. Хън → hewn.
bookSentenceEn: It dived into dells, and hugged steep banks; and where it passed over ﬂatter and more open ground on either side of it there were lines of large boulders and **hewn** stones that screened the travellers almost like a hedge.

definition: People who play the harp.
explanationBg: Хора, които свирят на арфа — старинно название на арфистите.
explanationEn: People who play the harp.
exampleEn: Two harpers opened the school concert with a surprisingly cool duet.
mnemonicBg: Harp = арфа (само с „х“ отпред): harpers са хората с арфите.
bookSentenceEn: Of him the **harpers** sadly sing: the last whose realm was fair and free between the Mountains and the Sea.

definition: A long weapon with a wooden shaft and a pointed steel head, used by horsemen.
explanationBg: Дълго оръжие с дървена дръжка и остър стоманен връх — копието на конните воини и рицарите.
explanationEn: A long spear used by soldiers riding horses.
exampleEn: At the museum we tried lifting a knight's lance, and it was heavier than my school bag.
mnemonicBg: Като рицаря Ланселот: Ланс-елот никога не излиза без своя lance.
bookSentenceEn: His sword was long, his **lance** was keen, his shining helm afar was seen; the countless stars of heaven’s ﬁeld were mirrored in his silver shield.

definition: (Archaic) dwells; lives or resides.
explanationBg: Старинна форма на „dwells“ — означава „живее, обитава“; среща се в стари песни и предания.
explanationEn: An old-fashioned way to say 'dwells', meaning lives somewhere.
exampleEn: The riddle in our escape room read: 'Here dwelleth the keeper of the final key.'
mnemonicBg: „ДУЕЛ-ет“ — в замъка обитава рицар, който кани всеки гост на дуел: тук живее дуелистът.
bookSentenceEn: a knife in the dark 243 But long ago he rode away, and where he **dwelleth** none can say; for into darkness fell his star in Mordor where the shadows are.

definition: A short narrative or lyric poem, especially one meant to be sung.
explanationBg: Кратка поема или песен, която разказва история — старинна дума за балада.
explanationEn: A short poem or song that tells a story.
exampleEn: For the talent show she turned an old folk lay into a modern pop ballad.
mnemonicBg: Lay звучи като „лей“: певецът лее песен — баладата се лее от сцената.
bookSentenceEn: ‘It is part of the **lay** that is called The Fall of Gil-galad , which is in an ancient tongue.

definition: The action of hiding something or preventing it from being known.
explanationBg: Скриването на нещо — действието, с което пазиш нещо да не бъде видяно или узнато.
explanationEn: The act of hiding something so others cannot see or know it.
exampleEn: The concealment of the surprise party meant hiding a whole cake in my locker.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се чува seal („печат“): запечатваш тайната в плик и никой не я узнава.
bookSentenceEn: **Concealment** was no longer possible, and they could only hope that no enemy or spy was observing them.

definition: A mound of rough stones built as a memorial or landmark.
explanationBg: Купчина от грубо натрупани камъни, издигната за спомен или като знак — например да бележи пътека в планината.
explanationEn: A pile of stones built as a marker or a memorial.
exampleEn: We followed the stone cairns to find the trail back down the mountain.
mnemonicBg: Представи си леля Карън, която реди камъче върху камъче на върха — купчината на Карън е cairn.
bookSentenceEn: Suddenly he stooped and looked at the stone on the top of the **cairn**; it was ﬂatter than the others, and whiter, as if it had escaped the ﬁre.

definition: Heaped or stacked together in a mass.
explanationBg: Натрупан на куп — много неща, струпани едно върху друго.
explanationEn: Put together in a heap or stack.
exampleEn: Dirty clothes piled up in my room until Mum declared a state of emergency.
mnemonicBg: Pie + pie + pie = piled: кула от пайове, натрупани един върху друг.
bookSentenceEn: But in the centre a cairn of broken stones had been **piled**.

definition: Burned or made discoloured by heat; dried up.
explanationBg: Обгорен или потъмнял от силна топлина; изсъхнал от жега — като трева след горещо лято.
explanationEn: Burned or dried out by strong heat.
exampleEn: I scorched my toast again because I was watching videos instead of the toaster.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „с коричка“: забравиш ли филийката в тостера, излиза scorched — с черна коричка.
bookSentenceEn: About them the turf was burned to the roots and all within the ring the grass was **scorched** and shrivelled, as if ﬂames had swept the hilltop; but there was no sign of any living thing.

definition: Wrinkled and contracted, especially due to loss of moisture.
explanationBg: Сбръчкан и свит, защото е изгубил влагата си — изсъхнал като стафида.
explanationEn: Wrinkled and smaller because it has dried out.
exampleEn: I found a shrivelled orange at the bottom of my school bag from last term.
mnemonicBg: В shrivelled чуй „се свил“: гроздето се свило, свило — и станало стафида.
bookSentenceEn: About them the turf was burned to the roots and all within the ring the grass was scorched and **shrivelled**, as if ﬂames had swept the hilltop; but there was no sign of any living thing.

definition: Lacking distinctive features; uniform or monotonous.
explanationBg: Без отличителни черти — еднообразен и монотонен, без нищо, по което да го запомниш.
explanationEn: Plain and all the same, with nothing special to notice.
exampleEn: The new mall is a featureless grey box compared to the old town square.
mnemonicBg: Feature = черта, -less = без: лице без черти — гладко и скучно като яйце.

definition: Stretched or extended in a long, narrow, continuous form.
explanationBg: Проточи се като дълга, тясна и непрекъсната ивица — така описваме път или река, виещи се през пейзажа.
explanationEn: Stretched out long and narrow, like a ribbon.
exampleEn: From the cable car, the river ran like a ribbon through the green valley.
mnemonicBg: Ribbon = панделка: дръпни панделката от подаръка и я пусни по пода — пътят се вие точно като нея.
bookSentenceEn: Beneath them on this southern side there **ran like a ribbon** the Old Road, coming out of the West and winding up and down, until it faded behind a ridge of dark land to the east.

definition: Dark or dull in colour or tone; grave and solemn.
explanationBg: Тъмен или убит на цвят; също и мрачен, сериозен и тъжен по настроение.
explanationEn: Dark in colour, or serious and sad in mood.
exampleEn: The locker room was sombre after we lost the final on penalties.
mnemonicBg: Като „сомбреро“, но наобратно: вместо слънчева шапка — тъмен, мрачен облак над главата.
bookSentenceEn: Following its line eastward with their eyes they saw the Mountains: the nearer foothills were brown and **sombre**; behind them stood taller shapes of grey, and behind those again were high white peaks glimmering among the clouds.

definition: A single act of moving the hand or an object across something; a sudden event.
explanationBg: Едно движение на ръката или на предмет по нещо — замах, щрих или погалване; понякога значи и внезапно събитие.
explanationEn: One movement of your hand or a tool across something.
exampleEn: With one stroke of the brush she fixed the whole sky in her painting.
mnemonicBg: В stroke чуй „щрих“: един замах на четката = един щрих.
bookSentenceEn: ‘There seems to be a **stroke**, a dot, and three more strokes,’ he said.

definition: With excessive speed or urgency; hurriedly.
explanationBg: Прекалено бързо и припряно — както правим нещата, когато закъсняваме и нямаме време.
explanationEn: Very quickly, in a hurried way.
exampleEn: I hastily shoved my books into my bag when the bus showed up early.
mnemonicBg: „ХЕЙСТ-или“ — „Хайде, или ще закъснеем!“ — и всичко става на бегом.
bookSentenceEn: **Hastily** they crept away and slipped down the north side of the hill to ﬁnd their companions.

definition: Tiny spots or particles.
explanationBg: Съвсем мънички петънца или частици — точици, които едва се виждат.
explanationEn: Very small spots or bits of something.
exampleEn: After art class there were specks of blue paint all over my sleeves.
mnemonicBg: Specks звучи като „спекс“ (очила): точици прах по стъклата — бършеш, а петънцата остават.
bookSentenceEn: Suddenly he was aware that two black **specks** were moving slowly along it, going westward; and looking again he saw that three others were creeping eastward to meet them.

definition: The flat-topped flower clusters of hemlock plants.
explanationBg: Плоските съцветия-чадърчета на отровното растение бучиниш — много дребни бели цветчета, събрани заедно.
explanationEn: The flat, umbrella-shaped flower clusters of the hemlock plant.
exampleEn: In biology class we sketched hemlock-umbels and learned never to touch the plant itself.
mnemonicBg: Umbel идва от „умбрела“ (чадър): цветчетата на бучиниша са наредени като малки отворени чадърчета.
bookSentenceEn: He was silent for some time, and then he began not to speak but to chant softly: The leaves were long, the grass was green, The **hemlock-umbels** tall and fair, And in the glade a light was seen Of stars in shadow shimmering.

definition: Bundles of cut hemlock stems and flowers.
explanationBg: Снопи от отрязани стъбла и цветове на бучиниш, вързани заедно като житни снопи.
explanationEn: Bundles of cut hemlock plants tied together.
exampleEn: The gardener carried away hemlock-sheaves after clearing the overgrown path.
mnemonicBg: Sheaf звучи като „шеф“: шефът в кухнята връзва магданоза на снопчета — sheaves са снопи.
bookSentenceEn: Now withered lay the **hemlock-sheaves**, And one by one with sighing sound Whispering fell the beechen leaves In the wintry woodland wavering.

definition: Scattered or spread untidily over a surface or area.
explanationBg: Разпилян безредно по някаква повърхност или място — пръснат навсякъде без ред.
explanationEn: Scattered messily over an area.
exampleEn: Crisps and controllers were strewn across the floor after the sleepover.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „с трохи“: масата след купон е strewn — посипана с трохи и салфетки навсякъде.
bookSentenceEn: Her mantle glinted in the moon, As on a hill-top high and far She danced, and at her feet was **strewn** A mist of silver quivering.

definition: Not causing anxiety, distress, or worry.
explanationBg: Който не носи тревога, страдание или притеснение — оставя те напълно спокоен.
explanationEn: Not causing any worry or stress.
exampleEn: The test turned out to be untroubling — just two pages of easy questions.
mnemonicBg: Trouble = проблем, un- = без: un-trouble-ing — нещо „без проблем“, което не буди тревога.
bookSentenceEn: He saw the elven-ﬂowers spring About her feet, and healed again He longed by her to dance and sing Upon the grass **untroubling**.

definition: Free from sorrow; without sadness.
explanationBg: Без капка тъга — състояние, в което скръбта просто я няма.
explanationEn: Completely free from sadness.
exampleEn: Those sorrowless summer days at my grandparents' house felt endless.
mnemonicBg: Sorrow (скръб) + less (без): тъгата се изпарява като локва на слънце — ден без скръб.
bookSentenceEn: The Sundering Seas between them lay, And yet at last they met once more, And long ago they passed away In the forest singing **sorrowless**.

definition: Strongly wanting to do or have something; enthusiastic.
explanationBg: Който силно желае нещо и няма търпение да го направи или получи — въодушевен и запален.
explanationEn: Wanting to do or have something very much.
exampleEn: Everyone was eager to try the new ramen place after school.
mnemonicBg: „ИЙ-гър“ — като запален геймър: няма търпение да пробва новата игра още в полунощ.
bookSentenceEn: As Strider was speaking they watched his strange **eager** face, dimly lit in the red glow of the wood-ﬁre.

definition: Splitting apart; separating.
explanationBg: Разцепване или разделяне на части — когато нещо цяло се разкъсва на две.
explanationEn: Splitting or breaking something apart.
exampleEn: The earthquake left a deep crack sundering the old playground in two.
mnemonicBg: Sunder звучи като thunder (гръм): светкавицата разцепва небето на две.
bookSentenceEn: But she chose mortality, and to die from the world, so that she might follow him; and it is sung that they met again beyond the **Sundering** Seas, and after a brief time walking alive once more in the green woods, together they passed, long ago, beyond the conﬁnes of this world.

definition: Far on or ahead in development or progress; moved forward.
explanationBg: Напреднал — стигнал далеч в развитието или напредъка си; придвижен напред.
explanationEn: Far ahead in progress, or moved forward.
exampleEn: She moved up to the advanced swimming group after just one season.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „аванс“: който получи аванс, е крачка напред — advanced.
bookSentenceEn: Then the shapes slowly **advanced**.

definition: Shaking or trembling, especially from fear.
explanationBg: Който се тресе и трепери — най-често от страх.
explanationEn: Shaking or trembling, usually from fear.
exampleEn: I was quaking backstage before my solo in the school concert.
mnemonicBg: Като earthquake (земетресение): коленете ти правят мини земетръс — трепериш от страх.
bookSentenceEn: Frodo was hardly less terriﬁed than his companions; he was **quaking** as if he was bitter cold, but his terror was swallowed up in a sudden temptation to put on the Ring.

definition: Having or showing eagerness or enthusiasm; sharp or piercing.
explanationBg: Изпълнен с желание и ентусиазъм за нещо; за острие, звук или вятър — остър, пронизващ.
explanationEn: Very enthusiastic about something; or sharp and piercing.
exampleEn: Marko is so keen on basketball that he turns up an hour before practice.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „кинжал“: keen е остър като кинжал — и желанието е също толкова остро.
bookSentenceEn: In their white faces burned **keen** and merciless eyes; under their mantles were long grey robes; upon their grey hairs were helms of silver; in their haggard hands were swords of steel.

definition: Loose sleeveless cloaks or shawls; coverings.
explanationBg: Широки наметала без ръкави — пелерини или мантии, които се мятат върху раменете; в по-широк смисъл — покривала.
explanationEn: Loose capes or cloaks worn over the shoulders.
exampleEn: For the cosplay contest we sewed dark mantles out of old curtains.
mnemonicBg: Лесно: mantle = мантия — мяташ мантията на раменете като супергерой.
bookSentenceEn: In their white faces burned keen and merciless eyes; under their **mantles** were long grey robes; upon their grey hairs were helms of silver; in their haggard hands were swords of steel.

definition: Looking exhausted and unwell, especially from fatigue, worry, or suffering.
explanationBg: Който изглежда изтощен и зле — с изпито, измъчено лице от умора, тревоги или страдание.
explanationEn: Looking very tired and unwell from stress or lack of sleep.
exampleEn: After the all-night gaming marathon he came to school looking completely haggard.
mnemonicBg: Представи си Хагрид след изпитна сесия: блед, рошав и скапан — haggard.
bookSentenceEn: In their white faces burned keen and merciless eyes; under their mantles were long grey robes; upon their grey hairs were helms of silver; in their **haggard** hands were swords of steel.

definition: In a clear and obvious way; simply.
explanationBg: Когато нещо се вижда, чува или казва ясно и направо, без увъртания — толкова очевидно е, че няма как да го пропуснеш.
explanationEn: In a clear and obvious way that is easy to see or understand.
exampleEn: You could plainly see she wasn't happy with the test results.
mnemonicBg: „Plain“ е равнина — на широко равно поле всичко се вижда ясно като на длан: plainly.
bookSentenceEn: Sam **plainly** was beginning to have doubts again about Strider; but while they were talking he returned, appearing suddenly out of the shadows.

definition: The edge of a piece of cloth that has been folded under and sewn.
explanationBg: Краят на дреха или плат, който е подгънат навътре и зашит, за да не се разнищва — подгъвът на пола, панталон или ръкав.
explanationEn: The folded and sewn edge of a piece of clothing or cloth.
exampleEn: Mum shortened my jeans by sewing a new hem the night before the school party.
mnemonicBg: Шивачката оглежда ръба на роклята, мърмори „хм… хм…“ и го подгъва — hem!
bookSentenceEn: A foot above the lower **hem** there was a slash.

definition: A small bag or other flexible container.
explanationBg: Малка мека торбичка или кесийка, в която носиш дребни неща — монети, слушалки, лакомства.
explanationEn: A small soft bag for carrying little things.
exampleEn: She keeps her earbuds and charger in a little pouch in her backpack.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „пауч“ с котешка храна — точно това е pouch: малка мека торбичка.
bookSentenceEn: From the **pouch** at his belt he drew out the long leaves of a plant.

definition: In a tired manner, showing fatigue.
explanationBg: Когато правиш нещо уморено и без сили — по движенията ти личи, че си напълно капнал.
explanationEn: In a tired way, with very little energy left.
exampleEn: After double PE, he climbed the stairs wearily and dropped onto his bed.
mnemonicBg: „УИЪ-ри-ли“ звучи почти като „умори ли се?“ — да, и затова всичко става едва-едва, уморено.
bookSentenceEn: The night passed slowly and **wearily**.

definition: Having a sharply strong taste or smell.
explanationBg: За миризма или вкус, които са толкова силни и остри, че направо те удрят в носа — като лук, оцет или синьо сирене.
explanationEn: Having a very strong, sharp smell or taste.
exampleEn: The pungent smell of garlic filled the whole flat while dad cooked dinner.
mnemonicBg: „ПЪН-джънт“ — миризма, която те фрасва в носа като пън: бам!
bookSentenceEn: He crushed a leaf in his ﬁngers, and it gave out a sweet and **pungent** fragrance.

definition: In a thinly distributed or scattered manner.
explanationBg: Когато нещата са малко на брой и пръснати далеч едно от друго — тук-там по едно, с много празно пространство помежду им.
explanationEn: With only a few things spread far apart from each other.
exampleEn: The stadium was sparsely filled an hour before the match, with empty seats everywhere.
mnemonicBg: Кажи го провлачено — „спааарс-ли“ — като последните три спаружени стафиди, пръснати в огромна кутия.
bookSentenceEn: Athelas they named it, and it grows now **sparsely** and only near places where they dwelt or camped of old; and it is not known in the North, except to some of those who wander in the Wild.

definition: A curve or turn in a road, river, or path.
explanationBg: Място, където път, река или пътека извива и сменя посоката си — с една дума, завой.
explanationEn: A curve or turn in a road, river, or path.
exampleEn: Slow down on your bike — there's a sharp bend in the path right after the bridge.
mnemonicBg: Представи си музикална група („бенд“), която свири точно на завоя — всички коли намаляват да я погледат.
bookSentenceEn: It was also his plan to shorten their journey by cutting across another great loop of the Road: east beyond Weathertop it changed its course and took a wide **bend** northwards.

definition: Having been prevented from growing or developing properly.
explanationBg: Който не е могъл да порасне и да се развие нормално — останал е дребен и хилав, като дръвче на гола скала без вода.
explanationEn: Not grown to full size because something stopped its development.
exampleEn: The tomato plants on our balcony stayed stunted because they got almost no sun.
mnemonicBg: „Stunted“ звучи почти като „спънато“ — растението се спънало в растежа си и си останало мъниче.
bookSentenceEn: The land before them sloped away southwards, but it was wild and pathless; bushes and **stunted** trees grew in dense patches with wide barren spaces in between.

definition: Closely compacted in substance; crowded together.
explanationBg: Гъст и плътен — частите му са натъпкани съвсем близо една до друга, като гъста гора или гъста мъгла.
explanationEn: Very thick or tightly packed together.
exampleEn: The fog was so dense this morning that we couldn't see the school gate from the street.
mnemonicBg: „ДЕНС“ — на претъпкана дискотека всички денсят толкова нагъсто, че игла няма къде да падне.
bookSentenceEn: The land before them sloped away southwards, but it was wild and pathless; bushes and stunted trees grew in **dense** patches with wide barren spaces in between.

definition: Small or insufficient in quantity or amount.
explanationBg: Твърде малко и недостатъчно — оскъдна порция, оскъдни записки, все не стига.
explanationEn: Too small in amount; not enough.
exampleEn: My notes from that class were so scanty that I had to borrow Maria's before the exam.
mnemonicBg: „СКАН-ти“ — сканираш цялата чиния с поглед, а в нея само две хапки: оскъдно!
bookSentenceEn: flight to the ford 261 **scanty**, coarse, and grey; and the leaves in the thickets were faded and falling.

definition: Rough or harsh in texture; not delicate or refined.
explanationBg: Груб на пипане, с едра и неравна повърхност — като зебло или едра морска сол; обратното на фино и гладко.
explanationEn: Rough to the touch; not smooth or fine.
exampleEn: The coarse sand on that beach scratched our feet, so we kept our flip-flops on.
mnemonicBg: „КОРС“ звучи като „кора“ — кората на дървото е точно такава: груба и грапава.
bookSentenceEn: flight to the ford 261 scanty, **coarse**, and grey; and the leaves in the thickets were faded and falling.

definition: Lacking brightness, gladness, or warmth; dreary.
explanationBg: Мрачен и без капка радост — място или ден, на които им липсват светлина, топлина и настроение.
explanationEn: Sad and grey, without any warmth or joy.
exampleEn: The empty classroom looked cheerless on the rainy Monday morning.
mnemonicBg: Чийрлидърки без помпони, без усмивки и без викове — отбор без „cheer“ = безрадостен, cheerless.
bookSentenceEn: It was a **cheerless** land, and their journey was slow and gloomy.

definition: To walk slowly and with heavy steps, typically due to weariness.
explanationBg: Да вървиш бавно и тежко, с влачещи се стъпки — когато си капнал или просто никак не ти се ходи.
explanationEn: To walk slowly with heavy, tired steps.
exampleEn: We trudged up the hill with our heavy backpacks after the camping trip.
mnemonicBg: „ТРЪДЖ“ звучи като „труд“ — всяка крачка е цял труд и едва си влачиш краката.
bookSentenceEn: They spoke little as they **trudged** along.

definition: (Of a plant) shrivelled and dry; (of a person) appearing aged and worn.
explanationBg: Повехнал и изсъхнал — като цвете, стояло седмица без вода, или лице, сбръчкано от годините.
explanationEn: Dried up and wrinkled, like a plant left without water.
exampleEn: I forgot to water the rose, and by Friday it was completely withered.
mnemonicBg: „УИ-дърд“ звучи като „Уеър?“ (къде?) — цветето се чуди „къде е водата?“, не я намира и повяхва.
bookSentenceEn: They dreaded the dark hours, and kept watch in pairs by night, expecting at any time to see black shapes stalking in the grey night, dimly lit by the cloud-veiled moon; but they saw nothing, and heard no sound but the sigh of **withered** leaves and grass.

definition: With faint or weak light; not clearly or distinctly.
explanationBg: Със слаба, мъждукаща светлина — или смътно и неясно, когато едва виждаш или едва си спомняш нещо.
explanationEn: With weak light, or in a way that is not clear.
exampleEn: The corridor was dimly lit, so we used our phone flashlights to find the door.
mnemonicBg: „ДИМ-ли“ — има ли дим в стаята, всичко се вижда мъждиво и смътно.
bookSentenceEn: They dreaded the dark hours, and kept watch in pairs by night, expecting at any time to see black shapes stalking in the grey night, **dimly** lit by the cloud-veiled moon; but they saw nothing, and heard no sound but the sigh of withered leaves and grass.

definition: A deep, narrow gorge with steep sides.
explanationBg: Дълбоко и тясно дере със стръмни стени — като огромен процеп в земята, често издълбан от река.
explanationEn: A deep, narrow valley with very steep sides.
exampleEn: On the hike we stopped at the edge of a ravine and threw stones to hear how deep it was.
mnemonicBg: „Ра-ВИЙН“ звучи като „равнина“, а е точно обратното — земята изведнъж се разцепва в дълбоко дере.
bookSentenceEn: A mile further on they came to a narrow **ravine** that led away northwards through the steep lands on the left of the Road.

definition: Curved structures forming the supports of bridges or doorways.
explanationBg: Извити като дъга конструкции, които крепят мостове, врати и прозорци — каменни или метални дъги над главата ти.
explanationEn: Curved structures that hold up bridges or doorways.
exampleEn: We took photos under the stone arches of the old bridge in the park.
mnemonicBg: Почти като нашите „арки“ — сети се за златните арки на Макдоналдс: две жълти дъги.
bookSentenceEn: They crossed the Bridge in safety, hearing no sound but the water swirling against its three great **arches**.

definition: Bad-tempered and sulky; gloomy.
explanationBg: Намусен и сърдит, без желание да говори с никого — човек с буреносен облак над главата.
explanationEn: Silent and bad-tempered, looking annoyed at everything.
exampleEn: He was sullen all afternoon because his team lost the final.
mnemonicBg: „СЪ-лън“ звучи като „сОлен“ — физиономия кисело-солена като туршия, навъсена до уши.
bookSentenceEn: Here Strider turned aside, and soon they were lost in a sombre country of dark trees winding among the feet of **sullen** hills.

definition: The way, direction, or position in which something lies; an intentionally false statement.
explanationBg: Думата има две лица: начинът, по който нещо е разположено или „лежи“ на терена, и лъжа — нарочно невярно твърдение.
explanationEn: The position of something on the ground, or a statement that is not true.
exampleEn: Before building the treehouse, we checked the lie of the ground under the old oak.
mnemonicBg: „ЛАЙ“ — кучето вдига лай, щом чуе лъжа, и после обикаля да огледа как „лежи“ дворът.
bookSentenceEn: He was going to climb up, if he could, and get a look at the **lie** of the land.

definition: A saw whose teeth have become dull and lost their sharpness.
explanationBg: Трион, чиито зъбци са се изтъпили от употреба и вече не режат, а само стържат.
explanationEn: A saw that has become dull and no longer cuts well.
exampleEn: Grandpa's blunted saw kept slipping on the branch instead of cutting through it.
mnemonicBg: „БЛЪН-тид со“ — затъпелият трион не реже, а само се блъска („блънт!“) в дървото.
bookSentenceEn: They found a passage between two hills that led them into a valley running south-east, the direction that they wished to take; but towards the end of the day they found their road again barred by a ridge of high land; its dark edge against the sky was broken into many bare points like teeth of a **blunted saw**.

definition: Knobbly, rough, and twisted, especially with age.
explanationBg: Целият на възли, грапавини и извивки — като ствола на много старо дърво или ръцете на стар човек.
explanationEn: Twisted, rough, and full of knots, usually from age.
exampleEn: We sat on the gnarled roots of the old oak to eat our sandwiches.
mnemonicBg: Пише се със скрито „g“ — gnarled — а старият дънер, цял на гънки и възли, ръмжи „гнаррр!“.
bookSentenceEn: They lit a small ﬁre down under the **gnarled** roots of an old pine, that hung over a shallow pit: it looked as if stone had once been quarried there.

definition: Extracted from a quarry (a place where stone or minerals are dug from the ground).
explanationBg: Изваден от каменоломна — мястото, където хората копаят и режат камък направо от скалите.
explanationEn: Dug out of a place where stone is cut from the ground.
exampleEn: The stone for the new school gym was quarried from the hills near our town.
mnemonicBg: „Quarry“ звучи като нашата каменна „кариера“ — quarried значи изкопан точно оттам.
bookSentenceEn: They lit a small ﬁre down under the gnarled roots of an old pine, that hung over a shallow pit: it looked as if stone had once been **quarried** there.

definition: Crowded together; nestled closely.
explanationBg: Сгушени плътно един до друг — както хора се скупчват, за да се стоплят или да се скрият от дъжда.
explanationEn: Pressed close together in a small group.
exampleEn: We huddled under one umbrella at the bus stop, laughing every time it dripped on us.
mnemonicBg: „ХЪ-дълд“ звучи като „худи“ — всички се сгушват под едно гигантско худи като пингвини на студа.
bookSentenceEn: They sat **huddled** together.

definition: A general view or examination of something.
explanationBg: Внимателен оглед на нещо отвисоко или отстрани — обхващаш с поглед цялата картина, за да я прецениш.
explanationEn: A careful look at something to check or understand it.
exampleEn: From the lifeguard tower she made a quick survey of the beach before the swimmers arrived.
mnemonicBg: Представи си рицаря „сър Вей“, който от върха на кулата прави оглед на цялото кралство.
bookSentenceEn: As soon as it was light, Strider took Merry with him and went to **survey** the country from the height to the east of the pass.

definition: (Of a problem) to trouble persistently; to surround on all sides.
explanationBg: Когато проблеми или опасности те връхлитат от всички страни и не те оставят на мира — все едно си обсаден от тях.
explanationEn: Troubled or surrounded by problems from every side.
exampleEn: Our school trip was beset by problems — rain, a late bus, and two forgotten lunches.
mnemonicBg: „Би-СЕТ“ — цял „сет“ от беди те огражда отвсякъде, като мач, в който губиш сет след сет.
bookSentenceEn: Whatever danger may **beset** it, the Road is our only way to the Ford.’

definition: Sudden rough, sharp, or violent jerking or jarring movements.
explanationBg: Резки, груби разтърсвания — като друсането в стар автобус, който минава през всички дупки на пътя.
explanationEn: Sudden rough shakes or bumps.
exampleEn: The jolts of the old school bus made it impossible to type a message without typos.
mnemonicBg: „ДЖОЛТС“ звучи почти като „жълт“ — жълтият автобус подскача по дупките: джолт, джолт!
bookSentenceEn: Bill Ferny’s poor old pony was developing an unexpected talent for picking out a path, and for sparing its rider as many **jolts** as possible.

definition: Not discovered or known about; uncertain; hard to understand.
explanationBg: Неясен, малко известен или труден за разбиране — нещо, за което почти никой не знае или което трудно проумяваш.
explanationEn: Not well known, or hard to understand.
exampleEn: He always listens to obscure bands that none of us have ever heard of.
mnemonicBg: В „обСКЮъР“ се чува „скри“ — нещо толкова скрито в тъмното, че никой не го знае.
bookSentenceEn: Even Frodo felt better in the morning light, but every now and again a mist seemed to **obscure** his sight, and he passed his hands over his eyes.

definition: Turns or twists in a path, road, or river.
explanationBg: Многото завои и извивки на път, пътека или река — когато не вървят направо, а лъкатушат.
explanationEn: The many turns and curves of a road, path, or river.
exampleEn: The windings of the mountain road made half the class feel carsick on the way to ski camp.
mnemonicBg: „УАЙН-дингс“ — на всеки завой от серпентините викаш „уааай!“, а пътят се вие ли, вие.
bookSentenceEn: When they came up with him, they saw that he had made no mistake: there were clearly the beginnings of a path, that climbed with many **windings** out of the woods below and faded away on the hill-top behind.

definition: More clear or obvious; less ornate.
explanationBg: По-ясен и по-разбираем — или по-семпъл и изчистен, без излишни украси.
explanationEn: More clear and simple; with less decoration.
exampleEn: Could you explain it in plainer words? The textbook version makes no sense to me.
mnemonicBg: Като „плейн“ кисело мляко — без захар, без плодове, чисто и просто; plainer = още по-изчистено.
bookSentenceEn: They followed the track for some while, for it offered much the easiest way down, but they went cautiously, and their anxiety increased as they came into the dark woods, and the path grew **plainer** and broader.

definition: Evergreen coniferous trees with needle-shaped leaves.
explanationBg: Вечнозелени иглолистни дървета — ели, които и през зимата си стоят зелени, с иглички вместо листа.
explanationEn: Evergreen trees with needles instead of leaves, like Christmas trees.
exampleEn: The path to the hut went through tall fir-trees that smelled amazing after the rain.
mnemonicBg: „ФЪР-триис“ — представи си елхата с пухкаво зелено „палто“ от иглички: на пипане „фъррр“.

definition: In a bent or twisted way; not in a straight line.
explanationBg: Накриво и изкривено — не по права линия, а все килнато на една страна.
explanationEn: In a bent or twisted way, not straight.
exampleEn: I hung the poster crookedly, so one corner pointed at the ceiling.
mnemonicBg: „КРУ-кид-ли“ — „crook“ е като крива кука: каквото окачиш на нея, виси накриво.
bookSentenceEn: In the stony wall there was a door hanging **crookedly** ajar upon one great hinge.

definition: A movable joint or mechanism on which a door or lid turns.
explanationBg: Металната сглобка, на която се върти врата или капак — пантата, която скърца, когато отваряш бавно.
explanationEn: The metal joint that lets a door or lid swing open and shut.
exampleEn: The door of my locker squeaks because one hinge needs oiling.
mnemonicBg: „ХИНДЖ“ — точно така скърца старата панта в страшните филми: „хииинджжж…“.
bookSentenceEn: In the stony wall there was a door hanging crookedly ajar upon one great **hinge**.

definition: Bending one’s head or body forwards and downwards.
explanationBg: Навеждане на главата и тялото напред и надолу — както се привеждаш, за да минеш през ниска врата.
explanationEn: Bending your head and body forward and down.
exampleEn: Stooping under the low doorway, he still managed to bang his head.
mnemonicBg: „СТУ-пинг“ звучи като „стъпвам“ — навеждаш се ниско, за да видиш къде стъпваш в тъмното.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Get up, old stone!’ he said, and broke his stick upon the **stooping** troll.

definition: In a manner that shows no anxiety or worry.
explanationBg: Спокойно и безгрижно, все едно нищо на света не те тревожи — без следа от притеснение.
explanationEn: In a calm way that shows no worry at all.
exampleEn: She shrugged unconcernedly when the teacher announced a surprise test.
mnemonicBg: Без „concern“ (грижа) — като котка, която се протяга и прозява, докато всички тичат в паника.
bookSentenceEn: Strider walked forward **unconcernedly**.

definition: An open space in a wood or forest.
explanationBg: Открито, светло местенце сред гората — полянка, където дърветата се разтварят и слънцето влиза.
explanationEn: An open, sunny space inside a forest.
exampleEn: We found a quiet glade in the woods, perfect for our picnic blanket.
mnemonicBg: „ГЛЕЙД“ звучи като „Гледай!“ — излизаш от тъмната гора и викаш: „Гледай, слънчева поляна!“.
bookSentenceEn: ‘It is broad daylight with a bright sun, and yet you come back trying to scare me with a tale of live trolls waiting for us in this **glade**!

definition: Ate (something) steadily and often audibly.
explanationBg: Ядеше нещо равномерно и шумно — с апетитно хрускане и мляскане, хапка след хапка.
explanationEn: Ate something steadily, often with a loud chewing sound.
exampleEn: He munched popcorn so loudly that we missed half the movie's dialogue.
mnemonicBg: „МЪНЧТ“ — хомяк с издути бузи: „мънч-мънч-мънч“, яде ли, яде, шумно и доволно.
bookSentenceEn: Troll sat alone on his seat of stone, And **munched** and mumbled a bare old bone; For many a year he had gnawed it near, For meat was hard to come by.

definition: The inner and typically larger of the two bones between the knee and the ankle.
explanationBg: Костта отпред на подбедрицата, между коляното и глезена — онази, която ужасно боли, удариш ли я в ръба на масата.
explanationEn: The big front bone of your lower leg, between the knee and the ankle.
exampleEn: A football hit him right on the shinbone, and he hopped around the pitch for a minute.
mnemonicBg: „ШИН-боун“ — счупиш ли „shin“-а, слагат ти шина: shin ~ шина, костта на пищяла.
bookSentenceEn: He can spare a share for a poor old troll, For he don’t need his **shinbone**.’

definition: (Dialect) to learn; to teach (often to teach someone a lesson).
explanationBg: Диалектна, селска форма на „уча“ — често като закана: „ще те науча аз тебе!“, тоест ще ти дам урок.
explanationEn: A dialect way of saying "to learn" or "to teach someone a lesson".
exampleEn: "That'll larn you to check the weather first!" Grandpa laughed when I came home soaked.
mnemonicBg: Това е „learn“, казано от дядо на село: „Ще те ларна аз тебе!“ — ще ти дам урок.
bookSentenceEn: Before he could mind, Tom slipped behind And gave him the boot to **larn** him.

definition: Unable to be heard.
explanationBg: Толкова тих, че не може да се чуе — звукът просто не стига до ушите ти.
explanationEn: Too quiet to be heard.
exampleEn: Her reply was almost inaudible over the noise of the cafeteria.
mnemonicBg: „Ин-“ значи „не“ + „аудио“ — като клип с изключен звук: устните мърдат, нищо не се чува.
bookSentenceEn: Sam muttered something **inaudible**.

definition: A professional joker or fool, especially one kept by a medieval ruler.
explanationBg: Придворен шут — човек, чиято работа в двореца на краля е била да разсмива всички с шеги и номера.
explanationEn: A funny entertainer who told jokes for a king in the Middle Ages.
exampleEn: In the school play, Niko got the role of the jester and stole the show with his jokes.
mnemonicBg: „ДЖЕС-тър“ звучи като „жест“ — шутът прави смешни жестове, докато кралят не се разсмее.
bookSentenceEn: First he was a conspirator, now he’s a **jester**.

definition: Underbrush bearing berries; thickets of berry-producing shrubs.
explanationBg: Ниски гъсти храсти, отрупани с горски плодове — като боровинковите туфи, през които газиш в планината.
explanationEn: Low, thick bushes that grow berries.
exampleEn: We picked blueberries from the berry brushwood along the trail until our fingers turned purple.
mnemonicBg: „Brush“ е четка — храсталакът е като огромна рошава четка, окичена с плодчета.

definition: An onomatopoeic phrase imitating the sound of trotting hooves.
explanationBg: Звукоподражание — така на английски звучи тропотът на конски копита: клип-клоп, клип-клоп.
explanationEn: A playful phrase that imitates the sound of a horse's hooves.
exampleEn: We heard a clippery-clippery-clip on the street and ran to the window to see the police horses.
mnemonicBg: Цъкни с език „цък-цък-цък“ като копитца по паваж — точно това е clippery-clippery-clip.

definition: To bend one’s head or body forwards and downwards.
explanationBg: Да се наведеш напред и надолу, със свити рамене и приведена глава — например за да минеш под нещо ниско.
explanationEn: To bend your body forward and down.
exampleEn: You'll have to stoop to get into the tent — the entrance is really low.
mnemonicBg: Двете „oo“ в „stoop“ са като две приведени рамена — самата дума се навежда.
bookSentenceEn: But Strider was now leaning forward, **stooped** to the ground, with a hand to his ear, and a look of joy on his face.

definition: The part of a bridle that fits around a horse’s head.
explanationBg: Частта от конската юзда, която обхваща главата на коня — ремъците около муцуната и зад ушите.
explanationEn: The straps of a bridle that go around a horse's head.
exampleEn: At the riding club she learned to fit the headstall gently over the pony's ears.
mnemonicBg: „Head“ = глава + „stall“ = бокс в конюшнята: „шапката“ от ремъци, с която водиш коня към бокса му.
bookSentenceEn: In the dusk its **headstall** ﬂickered and ﬂashed, as if it were studded with gems like living stars.

definition: To make a gesture with the hand or arm to encourage someone to come nearer.
explanationBg: Да махнеш с ръка на някого в смисъл „ела насам“ — жест, с който го викаш да се приближи.
explanationEn: To wave or signal with your hand so that someone comes closer.
exampleEn: She beckoned me over to her table to show me the meme on her phone.
mnemonicBg: „БЕ-кън“ звучи като „Бе, къмон!“ — махаш с ръка на приятел: „бе, ела насам!“.
bookSentenceEn: Soon Strider **beckoned** to them, and the hobbits left the

definition: Not quite right; inappropriate or out of place.
explanationBg: Когато нещо не е съвсем наред — усещаш, че има нещо нередно, макар да не знаеш точно какво.
explanationEn: Not quite right; something seems wrong.
exampleEn: The moment we walked in, we sensed something was amiss — the classroom was completely silent.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „А, мис?!“ — усещаш, че нещо не е наред, и веднага викаш учителката.
bookSentenceEn: Some of my kindred, journeying in your land beyond the Baranduin,* learned that things were **amiss**, and sent messages as swiftly as they could.

definition: Away from the correct path or direction; into error.
explanationBg: Отклонил се от правилния път или посока — изгубен, тръгнал накъдето не трябва.
explanationEn: Away from the right path or direction.
exampleEn: Without GPS we went astray and ended up in a completely different neighbourhood.
mnemonicBg: „Ъ-СТРЕЙ“ звучи като „встрани“ — тръгнеш ли встрани от пътеката, вече си се заблудил.
bookSentenceEn: They said that the Nine were abroad, and that you were **astray** bearing a great burden without guidance, for Gandalf had not returned.

definition: A thing serving as a visible or tangible representation of a fact, event, or feeling.
explanationBg: Предмет или жест, който показва нещо — малък видим знак за чувство или събитие, например подарък в знак на благодарност.
explanationEn: A small thing that shows or represents a feeling or fact.
exampleEn: She gave her coach a bracelet as a token of thanks for the great season.
mnemonicBg: „ТОУ-кън“ звучи почти като „жетон“ — мъничък предмет, който е знак, че нещо ти се полага.
bookSentenceEn: ‘It was my lot to take the Road, and I came to the Bridge of Mitheithel, and left a **token** there, nigh on seven days ago.

definition: (Archaic or literary) near; close.
explanationBg: Старинна дума за „близо“ — ще я срещнеш в приказки и стари книги, когато нещо е наблизо или наближава.
explanationEn: An old-fashioned word for "near" or "close".
exampleEn: "Winter is nigh," Dad announced dramatically as he pulled out his giant scarf.
mnemonicBg: „НАЙ“ — НАЙ-близкото нещо е nigh: чуеш ли „най“, мисли „близо“.
bookSentenceEn: ‘It was my lot to take the Road, and I came to the Bridge of Mitheithel, and left a token there, **nigh** on seven days ago.

definition: Serious or deep worry and apprehension.
explanationBg: Много сериозна, дълбока тревога — когато притеснението е тежко и не те пуска нито за миг.
explanationEn: Very serious and deep worry.
exampleEn: She waited for her exam results with grave anxiety, refreshing the page every minute.
mnemonicBg: „Grave“ значи и „гроб“ — тревога толкова тежка, че в стаята настава гробна тишина.
bookSentenceEn: Glorﬁndel caught Frodo as he sank to the ground, and taking him gently in his arms he looked in his face with **grave anxiety**.

definition: A purple-flowered evergreen shrub that grows on moors and heaths.
explanationBg: Ниско вечнозелено храстче с дребни лилави цветчета, което покрива голи хълмове и пусти поляни.
explanationEn: A small evergreen bush with purple flowers that grows on open hills.
exampleEn: The hills behind our campsite were covered in purple heather.
mnemonicBg: Хедър (Heather) е и английско момичешко име — представи си момиче на име Хедър, седнало сред лилавите цветчета по хълма.
bookSentenceEn: They cast themselves down in the **heather** a few yards from the road-side, and fell asleep immediately.

definition: To sink, subside, or droop downwards in the middle.
explanationBg: Да провиснеш или хлътнеш надолу по средата — както старо легло поддава под тежестта или въже, което се е отпуснало.
explanationEn: To bend or hang down in the middle, often because of weight.
exampleEn: The bookshelf started to sag under the weight of all my games.
mnemonicBg: Кажи провлачено „сааг“ и остави гласа си да увисне надолу — точно както провисва старо легло по средата.
bookSentenceEn: Pippin, Merry, and Sam were by that time nearly asleep on their stumbling legs; and even Strider seemed by the **sag** of his shoulders to be weary.

definition: Went or moved back or further away from a previous position.
explanationBg: Отдръпна се, отиде назад или се отдалечи — както вълните се изтеглят от брега или звук, който заглъхва в далечината.
explanationEn: Moved back or further away from where it was before.
exampleEn: After the storm, the flood water slowly receded from the streets.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „ри-СИ-ИДЕ“ — водата при отлив просто СИ ИДЕ назад към морето.
bookSentenceEn: The Riders seemed to sit upon their great steeds like threatening statues upon a hill, dark and solid, while all the woods and land about them **receded** as if into a mist.

definition: A sudden gush or burst of liquid; a sudden brief burst of activity or speed.
explanationBg: Внезапно бликване на течност или кратък прилив на сила и скорост — например последното ускорение точно преди финала.
explanationEn: A sudden short burst of liquid, speed, or energy.
exampleEn: With a final spurt of speed, she overtook everyone in the last lap.
mnemonicBg: Почти като „спринт“ без „н“ — кратък, мощен изблик на скорост точно преди финалната линия.
bookSentenceEn: A breath of deadly cold pierced him like a spear, as with a last **spurt**, like a ﬂash of white ﬁre, the elf-horse speeding as if on wings, passed right before the face of the foremost Rider.

definition: To feel or show fear or apprehension.
explanationBg: Да трепнеш и да се свиеш от страх — куражът ти за миг се изпарява пред нещо плашещо.
explanationEn: To feel afraid and show it, for example by shrinking back.
exampleEn: Even the bravest students quailed when the principal announced surprise exams.
mnemonicBg: На английски quail значи и „пъдпъдък“ — представи си пъдпъдъче, което трепва и се свива при най-малкия шум.
bookSentenceEn: There were Nine Riders at the water’s edge below, and Frodo’s spirit **quailed** before the threat of their uplifted faces.

definition: Raised up; elevated emotionally or spiritually.
explanationBg: Вдигнат нагоре; а за човек — изпълнен с радост и надежда, сякаш духът ти литва.
explanationEn: Raised up high, or made to feel happier and more hopeful.
exampleEn: I always feel uplifted after listening to my favourite playlist.
mnemonicBg: „Ъп“ значи „нагоре“, а „лифт“ е асансьор — настроението ти се качва с асансьора чак до покрива.
bookSentenceEn: There were Nine Riders at the water’s edge below, and Frodo’s spirit quailed before the threat of their **uplifted** faces.

definition: Mounted soldiers wearing helmets decorated with plumes (feathers).
explanationBg: Конници, чиито шлемове са украсени с развяващи се пера — тържествена гледка като от парад или исторически филм.
explanationEn: Soldiers on horseback wearing helmets decorated with feathers.
exampleEn: Actors dressed as plumed cavalry rode through the square at the history festival.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „плюмаж“ — перата на петела: конница с горди пера, веещи се от шлемовете на парад.
bookSentenceEn: Dimly Frodo saw the river below him rise, and down along its course there came a **plumed cavalry** of waves.

definition: (Of a natural force) swept over and surrounded so as to cover completely.
explanationBg: Изцяло залят и обгърнат от нещо мощно — като бряг, погълнат от огромна вълна, или поле, обхванато от пожар.
explanationEn: Completely covered or swallowed by something powerful like water or fire.
exampleEn: The beach was engulfed by the rising tide before we could grab our towels.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „гълф“ като „гълтам“ — огромната вълна те ГЪЛта целия, от глава до пети.

definition: The physical destruction or disintegration of something; a remnant of a destroyed structure.
explanationBg: Пълното разрушаване на нещо; също и самите останки от срутена сграда — стени, оцелели след векове.
explanationEn: The destruction of something, or the remains of a destroyed building.
exampleEn: On the school trip we explored the ruins of an old fortress above the town.
mnemonicBg: Лесна е — и на български казваме „руина“: стара срутена сграда, останала без покрив.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I was delayed,’ said Gandalf, ‘and that nearly proved our **ruin**.

definition: Forbidding or uninviting; very serious or gloomy.
explanationBg: Мрачен, суров и неприветлив — лице без капка усмивка или място, от което те побиват тръпки.
explanationEn: Very serious, dark, and unfriendly in look or mood.
exampleEn: The coach's grim expression told us we had lost before he said a word.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „грим“ — представи си злодей с тъмен грим и каменно, мрачно лице.
bookSentenceEn: I mean he is dear to me; though he is strange, and **grim** at times.

definition: To establish by calculation; to consider or believe.
explanationBg: Да пресметнеш нещо или просто да смяташ и вярваш, че е така — „мисля, че ще успеем“ е точно това.
explanationEn: To calculate something, or to think that something is true.
exampleEn: I reckon we need at least two more players for a proper match.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „рекох“ — „Рекох си: ще стане!“ — точно когато казваш какво смяташ.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I have been **reckoning**,’ he said, ‘and I can’t bring the total up to October the twenty-fourth.

definition: Having a V-shaped cut or indentation.
explanationBg: С малки резки или врязвания по ръба — както старо острие е нащърбено от дълга употреба.
explanationEn: Having small V-shaped cuts in the edge or surface.
exampleEn: My hockey stick is notched from all the matches it has survived.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за стар НОЖ — notch звучи като „нож“: острие с резки, нащърбено от употреба.
bookSentenceEn: Frodo shuddered, remembering the cruel knife with **notched** blade that had vanished in Strider’s hands.

definition: In an unwilling and hesitant way.
explanationBg: Без желание и с бавене — правиш нещо, защото се налага, а не защото ти се иска.
explanationEn: In a slow, unwilling way, because you do not really want to do it.
exampleEn: He reluctantly handed over the controller when his turn was up.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „лък“ по средата — ре-ЛЪК-тънт-ли: дърпаш се назад като опъната тетива, хич не ти се отива.
bookSentenceEn: And it seems that Hobbits fade very **reluctantly**.

definition: A ghost or ghostlike image, especially of a person seen shortly before death.
explanationBg: Призрак или бледо привидение — прозрачна сянка на човек, която се мярка за миг и изчезва.
explanationEn: A ghost or a pale, shadowy image of a person.
exampleEn: In the horror game, a wraith floats through the walls and follows the players.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „рей“ — призракът се РЕЕ из тъмния коридор като бледа мъгла.
bookSentenceEn: You were in gravest peril while you wore the Ring, for then you were half in the **wraith**-world yourself, and they might have seized you.

definition: A narrow miss or escape; or a close cut of hair.
explanationBg: Бръснене или съвсем късо подстригване; а изразът „клоуз шейв“ значи разминаване на косъм с нещо лошо.
explanationEn: A close cutting of hair; a 'close shave' also means a narrow escape.
exampleEn: Missing that ball by a centimetre was a close shave — it nearly hit my face.
mnemonicBg: Бръсначът минава на милиметър от кожата — затова разминаването на косъм с беда е „клоуз шейв“.
bookSentenceEn: But it was a terribly narrow **shave**, so to speak.

definition: (Literary) to see or observe (someone or something).
explanationBg: Старинна и тържествена дума за „виждам“ или „погледни“ — среща се в приказки, легенди и стари книги.
explanationEn: A literary word that means to see or look at something.
exampleEn: We climbed the hill at sunrise to behold the whole city glowing below us.
mnemonicBg: „Би-ХОУЛД“ крие „задръж“ (хоулд) — задръж погледа си и се полюбувай на гледката.
bookSentenceEn: ‘They were terrible to **behold**!

definition: Personal possessions (apart from land or buildings).
explanationBg: Личните ти вещи и притежания — всичко, което може да се мести, за разлика от земя и сгради.
explanationEn: A person's movable belongings, not land or buildings.
exampleEn: When we moved to the new flat, all our chattels fitted into one van.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „чанти“ — при местене всичките ти вещи се озовават в чанти: чат-ълс.
bookSentenceEn: Not all his servants and **chattels**

definition: Great evil wolves used as mounts by orcs (Tolkien).
explanationBg: Грамадни зли вълци от фентъзи историите — толкова едри, че злите създания ги яздят като коне.
explanationEn: Huge evil wolves in fantasy stories, often ridden like horses.
exampleEn: In the video game, a pack of wargs chased our characters across the snowy map.
mnemonicBg: „Уорг“ звучи като „враг“ — вълк-ВРАГ: грамаден, зъл и страшен.
bookSentenceEn: There are orcs and trolls, there are **wargs** and werewolves; and there have been and still are many Men, warriors and kings, that walk alive under the Sun, and yet are under his sway.

definition: To move slowly or rhythmically backwards and forwards or side to side.
explanationBg: Да се полюшваш бавно насам-натам или настрани — както дърво на вятъра или тълпа в ритъма на бавна песен.
explanationEn: To move slowly from side to side, like a tree in the wind.
exampleEn: The whole crowd swayed together as the band played their slow hit.
mnemonicBg: Кажи провлачено „су-еееей“ и се полюшни наляво-надясно — самата дума се люлее.
bookSentenceEn: There are orcs and trolls, there are wargs and werewolves; and there have been and still are many Men, warriors and kings, that walk alive under the Sun, and yet are under his **sway**.

definition: The condition of being transparent; the state of being clear or see-through.
explanationBg: Свойството на нещо да е прозрачно — светлината минава през него и виждаш ясно какво има отзад, като през чисто стъкло.
explanationEn: The quality of being clear and easy to see through, like glass.
exampleEn: The transparency of the lake water let us see fish swimming near the bottom.
mnemonicBg: „Транс-“ значи „през“ — прозрачното пуска погледа ти да мине ПРЕЗ него като през чисто стъкло.
bookSentenceEn: But to the wizard’s eye there was a faint change, just a hint as it were of **transparency**, about him, and especially about the left hand that lay outside upon the coverlet.

definition: A bedspread.
explanationBg: Лека завивка или покривало, което се мята най-отгоре върху леглото — и за красота, и за топлинка.
explanationEn: A decorative cover spread over the top of a bed.
exampleEn: Grandma knitted me a blue coverlet that makes my bed look cosy.
mnemonicBg: Музикалният „кавър“ покрива песен, а coverlet покрива леглото — мъничко „кавърче“ за завивка.
bookSentenceEn: But to the wizard’s eye there was a faint change, just a hint as it were of transparency, about him, and especially about the left hand that lay outside upon the **coverlet**.

definition: (Past of spring) jumped up or moved suddenly.
explanationBg: Скочи или се стрелна внезапно — миналото време на „скачам“: котката чу шум и хоп — изхвърча нагоре.
explanationEn: Jumped up or moved suddenly; the past form of 'spring'.
exampleEn: My dog sprang off the sofa the second he heard the doorbell.
mnemonicBg: „Спраннг!“ — звукът на отпусната пружина: котката излита нагоре за един миг.
bookSentenceEn: Your friends **sprang** aside, off the road, or they would have been ridden down.

definition: Set on fire; lit (a fire); aroused (a feeling).
explanationBg: Запален — за огън, който е разпален; а преносно — за чувство, което пламва у теб, например ново любопитство.
explanationEn: Lit or set on fire; also made a feeling begin to grow.
exampleEn: That one science video kindled my interest in astronomy.
mnemonicBg: Четецът „Киндъл“ (Kindle) носи точно това име — да „разпали“ любовта към книгите: kindled = запален.
bookSentenceEn: There they hastily **kindled** ﬁre; for Glorﬁndel knew that a ﬂood would come down, if the Riders tried to cross, and then he would have to deal with any that were left on his side of the river.

definition: Large rocks rubbing harshly against one another.
explanationBg: Огромни скални блокове, които се търкат и стържат един в друг с тежък, смразяващ тътен.
explanationEn: Huge rocks scraping and rubbing loudly against each other.
exampleEn: During the landslide we heard grinding boulders tumbling down the slope.
mnemonicBg: В игрите „гриндиш“ дълго и тежко — представи си камъни-гиганти, които „гриндят“ един в друг със стържещ тътен.
bookSentenceEn: If I may say so, I added a few touches of my own: you may not have noticed, but some of the waves took the form of great white horses with shining white riders; and there were many rolling and **grinding boulders**.

definition: Very great in amount, scale, or intensity.
explanationBg: Огромен, невероятно голям или мощен — толкова, че чак дъхът ти секва.
explanationEn: Extremely big, strong, or impressive.
exampleEn: The final goal was met with a tremendous roar from the fans.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „треперя“ в началото („тре-“) — нещо толкова грамадно, че земята трепери под него.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Yes, it all comes back to me now,’ said Frodo: ‘the **tremendous** roaring.

definition: Accorded a great deal of respect, especially because of age, wisdom, or character.
explanationBg: Дълбоко уважаван заради възрастта, мъдростта или достойния си живот — човек, пред когото всички притихват с почит.
explanationEn: Deeply respected because of age, wisdom, or character.
exampleEn: Our venerable chess coach has trained champions for forty years.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „венец“ — на най-мъдрия старейшина слагат лавров ВЕНЕЦ от уважение.
bookSentenceEn: **Venerable** he seemed as a king crowned with many winters, and yet hale as a tried warrior in the fulness of his strength.

definition: (Especially of an old person) strong and healthy.
explanationBg: Бодър, здрав и пълен със сили — казва се най-вече за възрастен човек, когото годините не са прегънали.
explanationEn: Strong and healthy, especially for an old person.
exampleEn: At eighty, my grandpa is still hale enough to beat me at table tennis.
mnemonicBg: Звучи почти като „хелт“ (здраве) — дядо в желязно здраве, който бодро вика „Хей!“ и те бие на тенис на маса.
bookSentenceEn: Venerable he seemed as a king crowned with many winters, and yet **hale** as a tried warrior in the fulness of his strength.

definition: A cloth covering hung or held over a person or thing as a shelter.
explanationBg: Платнен покрив или навес, опънат над някого или нещо за защита — като сенник над сергия или балдахин над легло.
explanationEn: A cloth roof or cover hung over something for shelter.
exampleEn: We strung up a canopy over the picnic table in case it rained.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „канапе“ — представи си канапе в градината с опънат отгоре платнен покрив-шатра.
bookSentenceEn: In the middle of the table, against the woven cloths upon the wall, there was a chair under a **canopy**, and there sat a lady fair to look upon, and so like was she in form of womanhood to Elrond that Frodo guessed that she was one of his

definition: One’s family and relations; sharing a similar nature or background.
explanationBg: Родът и роднините ти; казва се и за хора, които са ти близки по дух — „сродни души“.
explanationEn: Your family and relatives; also people very similar to you.
exampleEn: We both love the same indie bands — she's a kindred spirit.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „Киндер“ — на семейния празник цялата РОДА си разменя яйца „Киндер“.
bookSentenceEn: 296 the fellowship of the ring close **kindred**.

definition: A deposit of small white ice crystals formed on the ground in cold weather.
explanationBg: Тънък бял слой ледени кристалчета, който покрива земята и тревата в мразовитите утрини.
explanationEn: A thin white layer of ice crystals that forms in cold weather.
exampleEn: The grass on the football pitch was white with frost this morning.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за Джак Фрост от анимациите — духчето на студа, което поръсва тревата с бял скреж.
bookSentenceEn: The braids of her dark hair were touched by no **frost**; her white arms and clear face were ﬂawless and smooth, and the light of stars was in her bright eyes, grey as a cloudless night; yet queenly she looked, and thought and knowledge were in her glance, as of one who has known many things that the years bring.

definition: (Archaic) clothing; attire.
explanationBg: Старинна, приказна дума за дрехи или одежди — ще я срещнеш в легенди и стари книги, не в магазина.
explanationEn: An old-fashioned word for clothes.
exampleEn: For the school play she wore golden raiment like a queen from a legend.
mnemonicBg: Римува се с „пеймънт“ (плащане) — кралско плащане за кралски одежди.
bookSentenceEn: Above her brow her head was covered with a cap of silver lace netted with small gems, glittering white; but her soft grey **raiment** had no ornament save a girdle of leaves wrought in silver.

definition: The conduct or pursuits of a knight errant; wandering in search of adventure.
explanationBg: Странстване като рицарите от легендите — да обикаляш света в търсене на приключения и подвизи.
explanationEn: Travelling around looking for adventures, like a knight in old tales.
exampleEn: He calls his solo hiking trips his summer errantry, like a knight on a quest.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „ера“ в началото — ерата на странстващите рицари, тръгнали по света за подвизи.
bookSentenceEn: But her brothers, Elladan and Elrohir, were out upon **errantry**; for they rode often far aﬁeld with the Rangers of the North, forgetting never their mother’s torment in the dens of the orcs.

definition: Severe physical or mental suffering.
explanationBg: Силно страдание — болка, която мъчи тялото, или мисли, които не ти дават миг покой.
explanationEn: Very great pain or suffering of body or mind.
exampleEn: Waiting a whole week for the exam results was pure torment.
mnemonicBg: Почти като „тормоз“ — мъчение, което не те оставя на мира нито денем, нито нощем.
bookSentenceEn: But her brothers, Elladan and Elrohir, were out upon errantry; for they rode often far aﬁeld with the Rangers of the North, forgetting never their mother’s **torment** in the dens of the orcs.

definition: Wild animals’ lairs; also, places frequented by people for secret purposes.
explanationBg: Скривалищата на дивите животни — бърлоги, дупки и леговища; така наричат и тайно място, където се събират хора.
explanationEn: The hidden homes of wild animals; also secret meeting places.
exampleEn: The foxes dug their dens under the old shed behind our garden.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „денс“ — представи си лисичета, които си пускат музика и правят денс парти в бърлогата.
bookSentenceEn: But her brothers, Elladan and Elrohir, were out upon errantry; for they rode often far aﬁeld with the Rangers of the North, forgetting never their mother’s torment in the **dens** of the orcs.

definition: Embarrassed, disconcerted, or ashamed.
explanationBg: Смутен и позасрамен — става ти неловко, изчервяваш се и не знаеш къде да гледаш.
explanationEn: Feeling embarrassed or a little ashamed.
exampleEn: He looked abashed when the teacher read his joke note out loud.
mnemonicBg: Хващат те БАШ в момента на белята — а-БАШ-т: и ушите ти пламват от срам.
bookSentenceEn: Such loveliness in living thing Frodo had never seen before nor imagined in his mind; and he was both surprised and **abashed** to ﬁnd that he had a seat at Elrond’s table among all these folk so high and fair.

definition: Situated above another; higher in position or status.
explanationBg: Който е разположен отгоре или по-нависоко — горната койка, горният етаж; също и по-висш по ранг.
explanationEn: Placed above something else; higher in position or rank.
exampleEn: Our seats were on the upper floor of the stadium, right under the roof.
mnemonicBg: Всичко „ъп“ върви нагоре — ъпгрейд, ъп ниво: upper е това, което стои отгоре.
bookSentenceEn: Frodo could see him now, sitting with Pippin and Merry at the **upper** end of one of the side-tables close to the dais.

definition: A small, dispersed amount of something; the act of dispersing.
explanationBg: Разпръскване на неща в различни посоки; също и малко количество, пръснато тук-там — шепа къщи из полето.
explanationEn: A small amount of something spread here and there; the act of spreading things around.
exampleEn: A scattering of popcorn covered the floor after movie night.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „СКАТ-ър!“ — котката скача през масата и моливите се разпиляват с трясък по целия под.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Frodo Baggins at your service and your family’s,’ said Frodo correctly, rising in surprise and **scattering** his cushions.

definition: In a polite, respectful manner.
explanationBg: По възпитан, любезен и почтителен начин — с „моля“, „благодаря“ и уважение към отсрещния.
explanationEn: In a polite and respectful way.
exampleEn: The receptionist courteously showed us where the changing rooms were.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „корт“ — кралският двор: дръж се като пред краля, с поклон и любезни думи.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Quite right,’ answered the dwarf, gathering up the cushions and **courteously** assisting Frodo back into his seat.

definition: Known or talked about by many people; famous.
explanationBg: Известен и прочут — име, което много хора знаят и изговарят с възхищение.
explanationEn: Famous and known by many people.
exampleEn: The city is renowned for its street food festivals.
mnemonicBg: И на български го имаме — „реноме“: прочутият човек има голямо реноме.
bookSentenceEn: ‘And I do not ask, for I have already been told that you are the kinsman and adopted heir of our friend Bilbo the **renowned**.

definition: Inclined or willing to do something; arranged in a particular way.
explanationBg: Склонен или в настроение да направиш нещо; може да значи и „подреден по определен начин“.
explanationEn: Willing or likely to do something; also arranged in a certain way.
exampleEn: After losing the game, he wasn't disposed to talk to anyone.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „поза“ — дис-ПОУЗ-д: в каква „поза“ си днес, разположен ли си за разходка, или не?
bookSentenceEn: But perhaps I should not inquire too closely, since Elrond and Gandalf do not seem **disposed** to talk of this?’

definition: Strongly and solidly built or made; healthy and robust.
explanationBg: Здрав, стабилен и солидно направен — издържа на удари и тежест, без да поддаде.
explanationEn: Strongly built and hard to break.
exampleEn: You'll need sturdy boots for the mountain hike this weekend.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „стар дъб“ — маса от стар дъб: яка, стабилна, не помръдва.
bookSentenceEn: Frodo learned that Grimbeorn the Old, son of Beorn, was now the lord of many **sturdy** men,

definition: Possessing or showing courage or determination.
explanationBg: Смел и решителен — хвърля се в трудното без колебание, дори когато е наистина страшно.
explanationEn: Very brave and determined.
exampleEn: The goalkeeper made a valiant effort to stop the penalty.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като името Вальо + „гигант“ — храбрият Вальо излиза пръв срещу гиганта.
bookSentenceEn: They are **valiant** men and keep open the High Pass and the Ford of Carrock.

definition: Feeling or showing tiredness, especially as a result of excessive exertion.
explanationBg: Капнал от умора — изтощен след дълго усилие, когато едва си влачиш краката.
explanationEn: Very tired, especially after long effort.
exampleEn: We were weary after the three-hour rehearsal, but happy with the show.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „умори“ — „уиъри“ звучи почти като „умори се“: капна човекът след дългия ден.
bookSentenceEn: But stop me when you are **weary**!

definition: The product of someone’s work, especially something skilfully made by hand.
explanationBg: Нещо, излязло изпод нечии ръце — изделие или дело, по което личи умение и старание.
explanationEn: Something a person has made or done, especially skilfully by hand.
exampleEn: The bracelet was her own handiwork, made from beads and wire.
mnemonicBg: „Хенд“ е ръка, „уърк“ е работа — буквално „ръчна работа“: дело на твоите ръце.
bookSentenceEn: Dwarves’ tongues run on when speaking of their **handiwork**, they say.’

definition: Pieces of hard work or tasks performed; toil.
explanationBg: Тежък труд и вложени усилия — задачите, в които си излял пот и старание.
explanationEn: Hard work or difficult tasks that someone has done.
exampleEn: After weeks of hard training, our labours finally paid off with a gold medal.
mnemonicBg: „Лаборатория“ идва от същия корен — „място за труд“: чуй „лейбър“ вътре в думата.
bookSentenceEn: Glo´in began then to talk of the works of his people, telling Frodo about their great **labours** in Dale and under the Mountain.

definition: Paved with flat stones.
explanationBg: Настлан с плоски камъни — като старите улички с калдъръм, по които стъпките тракат.
explanationEn: Covered with flat stones, like an old street or square.
exampleEn: We cycled carefully over the stone paved square in the old town.
mnemonicBg: „Пейвд“ и „павета“ са роднини — улица, настлана с каменни павета.

definition: Like a cavern in size or atmosphere; vast and dark.
explanationBg: Огромен, тъмен и кънтящ като пещера — пространство, в което гласът ти отеква надалече.
explanationEn: Huge, dark, and echoing like a cave.
exampleEn: Our footsteps echoed in the cavernous sports hall before the crowd arrived.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „каверна“ — пещерна кухина: зала, огромна, тъмна и кънтяща като пещера.
bookSentenceEn: And the halls and **cavernous** streets under the earth with arches carved like trees; and the terraces and towers upon the Mountain’s sides!

definition: Proper or appropriate sequence or arrangement.
explanationBg: Правилният, подобаващ ред — всичко да върви така, както си му е редът, стъпка по стъпка.
explanationEn: The proper, correct order in which things should happen.
exampleEn: The coach made us do the warm-up drills in due order, with no skipping.
mnemonicBg: „Дю“ звучи като „дължа“ — редът, който се дължи: всяко нещо на мястото си, стъпка по стъпка.
bookSentenceEn: Elrond and Arwen rose and went down the hall, and the company followed them in **due order**.

definition: (Archaic past participle of carve) carved.
explanationBg: Старинна дума за „издялан“ или „изваян“ — фигура, изрязана от дърво или камък от майсторска ръка.
explanationEn: An old word that means carved or cut into shape.
exampleEn: The museum door had carven figures of lions and eagles.
mnemonicBg: Сещаш се за „карвинг“ — дялкането на фигури от плодове и лед: carven е старинното „издялан“.
bookSentenceEn: In it were no tables, but a bright ﬁre was burning in a great hearth between the **carven** pillars upon either side.

definition: Medieval singers or musicians, especially ones who sang or recited poetry.
explanationBg: Средновековни певци и музиканти, които обикаляли дворци и площади и пеели песни и стихове за герои.
explanationEn: Medieval singers and musicians who performed songs and poems.
exampleEn: At the medieval festival, minstrels played lutes and sang funny songs about the knights.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „мини стрели“ — менестрелите изстрелват мини стрели от песни право в сърцата на публиката.
bookSentenceEn: 300 the fellowship of the ring As Elrond entered and went towards the seat prepared for him, Elvish **minstrels** began to make sweet music.

definition: The activity of celebrating or having fun, especially loudly.
explanationBg: Шумна веселба — когато хората празнуват заедно, смеят се, пеят и се забавляват от сърце.
explanationEn: Noisy fun and celebration with other people.
exampleEn: The merrymaking after our team won the cup went on until midnight.
mnemonicBg: Merry (весел) + making (правене) = „правене на веселба“ — представи си Мери, която организира купон за целия квартал.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Then you two shall go into a corner and ﬁnish your task, and we will hear it and judge it before we end our **merrymaking**.’

definition: Not aware of or not concerned about what is happening around one.
explanationBg: Който изобщо не забелязва какво става около него — потънал е в своя свят и нищо наоколо не го вълнува.
explanationEn: Not noticing or caring about what is happening around you.
exampleEn: With his headphones on, he was completely oblivious to the teacher calling his name.
mnemonicBg: Започва като „облак“ — obliv-: ходи с глава в ОБЛАците и нищичко не забелязва.
bookSentenceEn: They talked together in soft voices, **oblivious** of the mirth and music in the hall about them.

definition: The interruption of a settled state; a commotion.
explanationBg: Нещо, което нарушава спокойствието и реда — внезапен шум, суматоха или прекъсване.
explanationEn: Something that breaks the calm, like noise or trouble.
exampleEn: The fire alarm caused a huge disturbance in the middle of our maths test.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за табелката на хотелската врата „Do not disturb“ — не вдигай шум, не създавай disturbance.
bookSentenceEn: Fancy that ring of mine causing such a **disturbance**!

definition: A mixture of currants, raisins, sugar, apples, and spices used in pies.
explanationBg: Сладка смес от стафиди, ябълки, захар и подправки, с която се пълнят пайове — въпреки името, в нея обикновено няма месо.
explanationEn: A sweet mix of dried fruit, apple, sugar and spices used to fill pies.
exampleEn: Grandma let us taste the mincemeat before she spooned it into the little pies.
mnemonicBg: „Минс-МИЙТ“ звучи като „месо“, но е капан — вътре има стафиди и ябълки: запомни го като „сладкия измамник“.
bookSentenceEn: They seemed to think that the Enemy was looking high and low for me, and would make **mincemeat** of me, if he caught me tottering about in the Wild.

definition: Moving in a feeble or unsteady way; on the verge of collapse.
explanationBg: Който се клатушка и едва се крепи — движи се толкова несигурно, че всеки момент може да падне.
explanationEn: Moving in a weak, shaky way, as if about to fall.
exampleEn: After the spinning ride at the funfair, we came out tottering like penguins.
mnemonicBg: Представи си Тоторо, който се клатушка тежко при всяка крачка — тот-тот-tottering.
bookSentenceEn: They seemed to think that the Enemy was looking high and low for me, and would make mincemeat of me, if he caught me **tottering** about in the Wild.

definition: Unwillingness or disinclination to do something.
explanationBg: Чувството, когато никак не ти се прави нещо — дърпаш се, бавиш се и го отлагаш.
explanationEn: The feeling of not wanting to do something.
exampleEn: With great reluctance, she handed her phone to her mum for the night.
mnemonicBg: Ре-ЛЪК-тънс — чуваш „лък“: дърпаш се назад като опъната тетива, само и само да не го направиш.
