bookSentenceEn: ‘Yes, I’ve got it,’ answered Frodo, feeling a strange **reluctance**.

definition: Extreme anxiety, sorrow, or pain.
explanationBg: Силна мъка, тревога или болка — когато на човек наистина му е тежко.
explanationEn: Very strong worry, sadness or pain.
exampleEn: You could hear the distress in his voice when his dog went missing.
mnemonicBg: Ди-СТРЕС = двоен стрес — когато стресът се удвои, вече е истинска мъка.
bookSentenceEn: To his **distress** and amazement he found that he was no longer looking at Bilbo; a shadow seemed to have fallen between them, and through it he found himself eyeing a little wrinkled creature with a hungry face and bony groping hands.

definition: In a serious or solemn manner; seriously.
explanationBg: По сериозен и мрачен начин — без следа от усмивка, сякаш става дума за нещо много важно.
explanationEn: In a very serious way.
exampleEn: The coach spoke gravely about what would happen if we skipped practice again.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие grave (гроб) — който говори gravely, е сериозен като гробна тишина, никакви шеги.
bookSentenceEn: Strider looked down at Bilbo **gravely**.

definition: Not expected or anticipated.
explanationBg: Който идва изневиделица — никой не го е очаквал и никой не е бил готов за него.
explanationEn: Not expected at all; a complete surprise.
exampleEn: Her unlooked-for victory in the chess tournament shocked even her own team.
mnemonicBg: Буквално „не-гледан-за“ — никой не е гледал за него, а то изскача като котка от кашон, който не си отварял.
bookSentenceEn: Elladan and Elrohir have returned out of the Wild **unlooked-for**, and they had tidings that I wished to hear at once.’

definition: Pitifully sad and abandoned or lonely.
explanationBg: Тъжен, самотен и сякаш изоставен от всички — гледка, която ти къса сърцето.
explanationEn: Very sad and lonely, as if everyone has left you.
exampleEn: The forlorn umbrella sat in the lost-and-found box all term.
mnemonicBg: Фор-ЛООРН — като провлачения вой на изоставено кученце под дъжда: „лооорн…“
bookSentenceEn: He was alone and felt rather **forlorn**, although all about him the folk of Rivendell were gathered.

definition: Woven or interlinked together; very closely connected.
explanationBg: Преплетен като нишки в плат — нещата са така свързани едно с друго, че не можеш да ги разделиш.
explanationEn: Joined together very closely, like threads in one fabric.
exampleEn: Our class group chat is so interwoven with my daily life that I check it without thinking.
mnemonicBg: Като плитка — три кичура, вплетени един в друг: inter (между) + woven (изтъкан).
bookSentenceEn: At ﬁrst the beauty of the melodies and of the **interwoven** words in elven-tongues, even though he understood them little, held him in a spell, as soon as he began to attend to them.

definition: Lit by the light of a fire.
explanationBg: Осветен от пламъците на огън — например стая, в която свети само камината.
explanationEn: Lit up by the light of a fire.
exampleEn: We told scary stories in the firelit tent until someone screamed.
mnemonicBg: Fire (огън) + lit (запален) — лагерният огън е „лит“ и прави всички лица наоколо оранжеви: firelit.

definition: The edges or borders of a surface or area.
explanationBg: Краищата или ръбовете на нещо — частите най-отстрани, далеч от средата.
explanationEn: The outer edges or borders of an area.
exampleEn: We pitched our tent at the margins of the forest, where the fields begin.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за полетата на тетрадката — те са margins, крайчетата на листа, където драскаш котенца в час.
bookSentenceEn: Almost it seemed that the words took shape, and visions of far lands and bright things that he had never yet imagined opened out before him; and the ﬁrelit hall became like a golden mist above seas of foam that sighed upon the **margins** of the world.

definition: The feeling of being enchanted; a magical spell.

definition: Grasped mentally; understood.

definition: To stay longer than intended; to delay leaving a place.

definition: A complete or impressive collection of things; a full suit of armour.

definition: A type of quartz, often translucent, used as a gemstone.

bookSentenceEn: Frodo and Bilbo followed the wizard quickly along the winding path back to the house; behind them, uninvited and for the moment forgotten, **trotted** Sam.

definition: The channel or bottom of a river.

definition: (Past participle of shear) cut off, especially of hair or wool.

explanationEn: Someone or something dangerous that could cause harm; a threat.

definition: The action or practice of deceiving someone by concealing or misrepresenting the truth.
explanationBg: Когато някой нарочно крие или изкривява истината, за да подведе другите — това е измама.

exampleEn: Their friendship ended over a small deceit that grew into a huge lie.
mnemonicBg: „ди-СИЙТ“ звучи като „seat“ (стол): някой ти дръпва стола точно когато сядаш — подла измама!
bookSentenceEn: We needed not the fell voice of the messenger to warn us that his words held both menace and **deceit**; for we knew already that the power that has re-entered Mordor has not changed, and ever it betrayed us of old.

definition: To regard or consider in a specified way.
explanationBg: Да приемаш или преценяваш нещо по определен начин — например да смяташ един план за добър или един отговор за верен.
explanationEn: To consider or judge something in a particular way.
exampleEn: The jury deemed her science project the most creative in the whole school.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „дим“: видиш ли ДИМ, веднага смяташ (deem), че някъде гори!
bookSentenceEn: That is the doom that we must **deem**.

definition: Caught in or as in a trap.

mnemonicBg: „ин-СНЕЪД“ — стъпваш в дълбок СНЯг, затъваш до коляно и не мърдаш — уловен в капан!
bookSentenceEn: A part of his tale was known to some there, but the full tale to none, and many eyes were turned to Elrond in fear and wonder as he told of the Elven-smiths of Eregion and their friendship with Moria, and their eagerness for knowledge, by which Sauron **ensnared** them.

definition: A body of traditions and knowledge on a subject or held by a particular group.
explanationBg: Сборът от предания, истории и знания, които една общност пази и предава нататък — от стари легенди до тайните на занаята.
explanationEn: The traditional stories and knowledge shared by a group of people.

mnemonicBg: Крие се във „фолкЛОР“ — фолклорът е точно това: преданията и знанието на народа.
bookSentenceEn: 316 the fellowship of the ring Elrond himself set it down in his books of **lore**, it is not here recalled.

definition: (Formal address) used to address a king; also: the male parent of an animal.
explanationBg: Старинно обръщение към крал — „господарю“; освен това така се нарича и бащата на животно, например на жребче.
explanationEn: An old word used to address a king; also the father of an animal.

mnemonicBg: Представи си паж, който поднася на краля СИРене: „Заповядайте, sire!“
bookSentenceEn: Ea ¨rendil was my **sire**, who was born in Gondolin before its fall; and my mother was Elwing, daughter of Dior, son of Lu ´thien of Doriath.

definition: An official messenger bringing news; a sign that something is about to happen.
explanationBg: Официален вестоносец, който носи важни новини; казва се и за знак, че нещо скоро ще се случи.

mnemonicBg: Представи си викинга ХаРАЛД, който тича по улиците и вика новините — той е вестителят.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I was the **herald** of Gil-galad and marched with his host.

definition: (Past of behold) saw or observed.
explanationBg: Минало време на „behold“ — видя, съзря нещо, обикновено величествено или изумително.
explanationEn: Saw or looked at something, often something amazing (past of 'behold').

mnemonicBg: Вътре е „held“ (държан): гледката те хваща и ДЪРЖИ погледа — съзрял си нещо незабравимо.
bookSentenceEn: I **beheld** the last combat on the slopes of Orodruin, where Gil-galad died, and Elendil fell, and Narsil broke beneath him; but Sauron himself was overthrown, and Isildur

definition: A broken piece of a sword that still includes the hilt.
explanationBg: Отломък от счупен меч, на който още стои дръжката — частта, за която се хваща ръката.
explanationEn: A broken piece of a sword that still has its handle.
exampleEn: Behind the museum glass lay a rusty hilt-shard from some forgotten battle.
mnemonicBg: hilt = дръжка, shard = парче: счупваш меча и ти остава само дръжка с отломък — като чадър, оцелял след буря.
bookSentenceEn: the council of elrond 317 cut the Ring from his hand with the **hilt-shard** of his father’s sword, and took it for his own.’

definition: Fragments taken as weregild (man-price paid in compensation for killing).
explanationBg: Отломки, дадени като „веоргилд“ — старинен откуп: цената, която убиецът плащал на рода на убития вместо мъст.
explanationEn: Broken pieces given as payment to a victim's family for a killing.
exampleEn: In history class we read how silver weregild shards could settle a feud between two clans.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „вер-ГИЛД“ като „гилдия + gold“: плащаш злато на парчета, за да изкупиш вина.

definition: A young nobleman who acted as an attendant to a knight before becoming a knight himself.
explanationBg: Млад благородник, който служел на рицар — носел му щита и оръжието и се учел, докато един ден сам стане рицар.
explanationEn: A young nobleman who served a knight while training to become one.
exampleEn: In the new RPG you begin as a humble esquire polishing armour before your first quest.
mnemonicBg: „и-СКУАЙ-ъ“ — младежът ЕСКОРТира рицаря навсякъде: носи меча, държи коня, учи занаята.
bookSentenceEn: One of these was Ohtar, the **esquire** of Isildur, who bore the shards of the sword of Elendil; and he brought them to Valandil, the heir of Isildur, who being but a child had remained here in Rivendell.

definition: Caused (a fire or light) to cease to burn or shine.
explanationBg: Угасен — някой е спрял огъня или светлината да горят и да светят.

mnemonicBg: Сети се за „extinguisher“ — пожарогасител: пшшшт! — и пламъкът е угасен.
bookSentenceEn: But Narsil was broken and its light **extinguished**, and it has not yet been forged again.

definition: Made or became less; reduced.
explanationBg: Намалял или направен по-малък — по размер, сила или значение.
explanationEn: Became smaller or weaker; was reduced.
exampleEn: Her fear of speaking on stage diminished after every rehearsal.
mnemonicBg: „ди-МИНИ-шт“ — чуваш „МИНИ“: голямото се свива до мини размер, намаляло е.
bookSentenceEn: Sauron was **diminished**, but not destroyed.

definition: Destroyed or undone; not made.
explanationBg: Развален, разтурен или унищожен — все едно никога не е бил направен.

mnemonicBg: „made“ (направен) с „un-“ отпред: пусни строежа на rewind и той се разтуря до нищо.
bookSentenceEn: His Ring was lost but not **unmade**.

definition: The lowest load-bearing parts of a building or wall; the basis of something.
explanationBg: Най-долната носеща част на сграда или стена; в преносен смисъл — основата, върху която стъпва всичко останало.

mnemonicBg: Лесна връзка: foundations ≈ ФУНДАмент — основите, върху които стои всичко.
bookSentenceEn: The Dark Tower was broken, but its **foundations** were not removed; for they were made with the power of the Ring, and while it remains they will endure.

definition: To make or become less; to reduce.
explanationBg: Да направиш нещо по-малко или по-слабо, или то само да намалее — например болка, шум или страх.
explanationEn: To make something smaller or weaker, or to become less.
exampleEn: Stretching after practice helps lessen the soreness the next day.
mnemonicBg: Звучи точно като „lesson“ (урок): с всеки урок страхът от изпита намалява.
bookSentenceEn: And ever since that day the race of Nu ´menor has decayed, and the span of their years has **lessened**.

definition: (Of a place) deserted and barren; (of a person) feeling utterly alone and unhappy.
explanationBg: За място — пусто, голо и без живот; за човек — съсипан от самота и мъка.

mnemonicBg: Чуй „ДЕ-СА-ЛЪТ“ като „де са летовниците?“ — няма ги: плажът е пуст и тъжен.

definition: The dominion or authority of a lord; a title for a lord.

definition: Rounded masses projecting above a surface; small hills.

mnemonicBg: Помисли за „mountain“ (планина), но в джобен формат: mound е мини-планинка, купчинка-могилка.
bookSentenceEn: For the folk of Arnor dwindled, and their foes devoured them, and their lordship passed, leaving only green **mounds** in the grassy hills.

definition: Smaller in size, amount, or importance.
explanationBg: По-малкият или по-маловажният от две неща — отстъпва по размер, количество или значение.

mnemonicBg: „less“ + „-er“: от двете парчета пица едното винаги е lesser — по-малкото, което никой не взима пръв.
bookSentenceEn: ‘But in the wearing of the swift years of Middle-earth the line of Meneldil son of Ana´rion failed, and the Tree withered, and the blood of the Nu´meno´reans became mingled with that of **lesser** men.

definition: (Archaic) truly; certainly.
explanationBg: Старинна дума за „наистина, без съмнение“ — с нея тържествено са потвърждавали казаното.

mnemonicBg: Чуй „ВЕРи-ли“ като „вярно ли?“ — а отговорът е: вярно, наистина!

definition: Actions performed deliberately or consciously; legal documents.
explanationBg: Делата и постъпките на човек — нещата, които прави съзнателно, добри или лоши.

definition: A defensive wall; a person or thing that defends.

definition: A small remaining quantity or part of something.

mnemonicBg: Звучи като „РЕМонт-нант“: след всеки ремонт остава по едно парче плочка — остатъкът.

definition: Surrounded by; in the middle of.
explanationBg: Сред, посред нещо — заобиколен от него отвсякъде.

mnemonicBg: Звучи като „мида“: мидата лежи СРЕД пясъка — amid the sand!

definition: Undoing twisted, knitted, or woven threads; investigating and solving.

definition: Valuable objects that have belonged to a family for several generations.

definition: A thing that is helpful or beneficial; a blessing.

definition: Loyal, reliable, and hard-working; sturdily built.

mnemonicBg: Чуй „СТОуЛ-уърт“ като „СТОмана“: приятел със стоманена вярност — як и непоклатим.
bookSentenceEn: ‘If Gondor, Boromir, has been a **stalwart** tower, we have played another part.

definition: Without ceasing; continuously.
explanationBg: Без да спре нито за миг — непрекъснато, ден и нощ.

bookSentenceEn: ‘‘Strider’’ I am to one fat man who lives within a day’s march of foes that would freeze his heart, or lay his little town in ruin, if he were not guarded **ceaselessly**.

definition: Feeling or showing annoyance and displeasure.
explanationBg: Недоволен и подразнен — нещо не ти е по вкуса и това ясно си личи.

mnemonicBg: „pleased“ (доволен) с „dis-“ отпред — все едно слагаш ДИСлайк на настроението си.
bookSentenceEn: To some there Bilbo’s tale was wholly new, and they listened with amazement while the old hobbit, actually not at all **displeased**, recounted his adventure with Gollum, at full length.

definition: Is enough or adequate.
explanationBg: Достатъчно е — стига толкова, върши работа и не е нужно нищо повече.

mnemonicBg: Представи си малко СУФлЕ: дребно е, но ти стига — suffices!

definition: Places of safety or refuge; in Tolkien, the Grey Havens, port of departure for Elves.
explanationBg: Сигурни места за подслон и спокойствие — убежища или закътани пристанища; в книгата така се наричат Сивите пристани, откъдето отплават елфите.
explanationEn: Safe places where people can find shelter or rest.

mnemonicBg: Едно „а“ го дели от „heaven“ (рай): убежището е твоето малко райско кътче.

definition: The treasure or hoard kept by a halfling (hobbit).
explanationBg: Съкровището, което си пази един полуръст — дребно приказно човече; „trove“ е скътано богатство, сбирка от ценности.

definition: To persuade (someone) not to take a particular course of action.

definition: Pretended; simulated; not real.

mnemonicBg: Запомни през „ФЕЙк“: feigned = изфейкано чувство — усмивка само за пред камерата.
bookSentenceEn: Then he gave way before us, but only **feigned** to ﬂee, and soon after came to the Dark Tower and openly declared himself.

definition: The action or state of keeping careful watch for possible danger.

mnemonicBg: Започва като „ВИЖ!“: бдителният ВИЖда всичко — очи на четири!
bookSentenceEn: ‘We were all at fault,’ said Elrond, ‘and but for your **vigilance** the Darkness, maybe, would already be upon us.

definition: (Archaic or formal) from what place or source.

definition: Happening or done at an unsuitable time; premature.

definition: Work, especially hard physical work; effort.
explanationBg: Труд, особено тежка физическа работа — усилие, което иска пот и постоянство.

definition: With sincere and intense conviction; seriously.

mnemonicBg: Звучи близо до „honest“ (честен): говориш честно, искрено и на сериозно.

definition: Paid only partial attention to.
explanationBg: Чут или забелязан само наполовина — обърнал си му внимание едва-едва, между другото.
explanationEn: Given only half of your attention.
exampleEn: Mum's umbrella advice was half-heeded — I took a jacket and still got soaked.
mnemonicBg: „half“ = наполовина, „heed“ = внимавам: слушаш с една слушалка в ухото — чуваш половината.
bookSentenceEn: 328 the fellowship of the ring Saruman, **half-heeded** at the time.

definition: Not adorned or decorated; plain.
explanationBg: Без никаква украса — семпъл и чист, такъв, какъвто си е.
explanationEn: Plain and simple, with no decoration.
exampleEn: She keeps her phone case unadorned — no stickers, no charms, just plain black.
mnemonicBg: Вътре е „adorn“ (украсявам) с „un-“: смъкваш орнаментите — гола стена без нито един постер.
bookSentenceEn: It was round and **unadorned**, as it were one of the lesser rings; but its maker set marks upon it that the skilled, maybe, could still see and read.’’

definition: A roll of parchment or paper for writing on.
explanationBg: Лист пергамент или хартия, навит на руло, върху който се пише — древната „книга“.
explanationEn: A rolled-up sheet of paper or parchment for writing.
exampleEn: For history class we stained paper with tea and rolled it into an ancient-looking scroll.
mnemonicBg: Същата дума като „скролвам“ в телефона: пръстът ти развива безкраен дигитален свитък.
bookSentenceEn: Less welcome did the Lord Denethor show me then than of old, and grudgingly he permitted me to search among his hoarded **scrolls** and books.

definition: (Formal) in that place, document, or respect.
explanationBg: Официална дума за „в това“ — вътре в споменатото място, документ или нещо.
explanationEn: A formal word meaning 'in that place or thing'.
exampleEn: The settings menu has a hidden tab, and therein lies the switch that turns off ads.
mnemonicBg: Просто „there“ + „in“: посочваш кутията и казваш „там вътре“ — therein!
bookSentenceEn: And what was said **therein** was already known.

definition: (Archaic) a glowing coal or live ember.
explanationBg: Старинна дума за тлеещ въглен — парченце жар, което още свети в огнището.
explanationEn: An old word for a glowing coal in a fire.
exampleEn: We toasted the last marshmallow over a single glede left from the campfire.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „ГЛЕДай“: гледаш в огнището, а едно въгленче ти намига с червено око.
bookSentenceEn: It was hot when I ﬁrst took it, hot as a **glede**, and my hand was scorched, so that I doubt if ever again I shall be free of the pain of it.

definition: (Archaic) loses.
explanationBg: Старинна форма на „loses“ — означава просто „губи“, както се е говорело в много стар английски.
explanationEn: An old form of the word 'loses'.
exampleEn: 'He who loseth his password loseth his account,' my brother announced in a fake medieval voice.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за „лузър“: loseth е пра-прадядото на думата — „губи“, но казано с рицарски глас.
bookSentenceEn: Yet even as I write it is cooled, and it seemeth to shrink, though it **loseth** neither its beauty nor its shape.

definition: (Archaic) fades; becomes dim or weak.
explanationBg: Старинна форма на „fades“ — гасне, избледнява, бавно отслабва като светлина привечер.
explanationEn: An old form of 'fades' — slowly becomes dim or weak.
exampleEn: 'Summer fadeth away,' she sighed dramatically as we packed up the beach towels.
mnemonicBg: Знаеш „fade out“ от видеата — кадърът гасне; добави старинното „-eth“ и звучи по рицарски.
bookSentenceEn: Already the writing upon it, which at ﬁrst was as clear as red ﬂame, **fadeth** and is now only barely to be read.

definition: Handwriting as distinct from print; a writing system.
explanationBg: Начинът, по който са изписани буквите — ръкописен почерк или цяла писмена система като кирилицата.
explanationEn: Handwriting, or a system of written letters.
exampleEn: Her notes are written in such neat purple script that the whole class borrows them.
mnemonicBg: Като „скрипт“ във филмите и игрите — всичко идва от „пиша“: script = написаното.
bookSentenceEn: It is fashioned in an elven-**script** of Eregion, for they have no letters in Mordor for such subtle work; but the language is unknown to me.

definition: Lost or was without all hope.
explanationBg: Изгубил всяка надежда — отчаял се, че нещо изобщо ще се нареди.
explanationEn: Lost all hope that something would work out.
exampleEn: I almost despaired of beating that level, but on the twentieth try it finally happened.
mnemonicBg: „ди-СПЕЪД“ — геймър без нито един spare (резервен) живот: последният отива и идва отчаянието.
bookSentenceEn: I, too, **despaired** at last, and I began my homeward journey.

definition: A rope or strap placed around the head of a horse, used to lead or fasten it.
explanationBg: Въжето или ремъкът, който се слага около главата на кон, за да можеш да го водиш или да го вържеш някъде.
explanationEn: A rope or strap you put around a horse's head to lead it or tie it up.
exampleEn: The stable girl slipped a halter over the pony's head before leading it out to the paddock.
mnemonicBg: „ХОЛ-тъ“ — представи си, че водиш кон с въжето право в хола на баба: с halter се води кон.
bookSentenceEn: I deemed it the worst part of all my journey, the road back, watching him day and night, making him walk before me with a **halter** on his neck, gagged, until he was tamed by lack of drink and food, driving him ever towards Mirkwood.

definition: A financial gain; an advantage or benefit obtained from something.
explanationBg: Парите, които ти остават като печалба, след като извадиш разходите — или по-общо: ползата, която получаваш от нещо.
explanationEn: Money you gain, or any benefit you get from something.
exampleEn: We sold lemonade at the school fair and split the profit three ways.
mnemonicBg: Профитерол! Продаваш профитероли на панаира и трупаш profit — печалбата е сладка.

definition: Surprisingly impressive or notable.
explanationBg: Толкова впечатляващ и изненадващ, че те оставя с отворена уста.
explanationEn: So impressive or surprising that it amazes you.
exampleEn: Her free-throw streak was astounding — twenty in a row without a single miss.
mnemonicBg: ъ-СТАУН-динг — чуваш „стон“ по средата: толкова е поразително, че издаваш дълъг стон „оооо!“.
bookSentenceEn: The change in the wizard’s voice was **astounding**.

definition: (Of conduct or an event) giving rise to regret; undesirable.
explanationBg: За постъпка или събитие, което е жалко и буди съжаление — щеше да е по-добре изобщо да не се беше случвало.
explanationEn: Something bad that makes you feel sorry it happened.
exampleEn: Forgetting my best friend's birthday was regrettable, and I'm still making up for it.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие „Грета“ — горката Грета изпусна сладоледа си на тротоара: колко жалко, какво съжаление!
bookSentenceEn: That was a **regrettable** misunderstanding, long set right.

definition: Real or imagined causes for complaint.
explanationBg: Неща, от които хората се оплакват — истински или въображаеми причини за недоволство.
explanationEn: Reasons, real or imagined, that people have for complaining.
exampleEn: The students listed their grievances about the cafeteria food in a letter to the principal.
mnemonicBg: ГРИЙВ-ънсис ~ „грижи“ — тефтерче, в което записваш всичките си грижи и оплаквания, за да ги изредиш после.
bookSentenceEn: If all the **grievances** that stand between Elves and

definition: Without warning; unexpectedly.
explanationBg: Изневиделица, без никакво предупреждение — когато нещо те сварва неподготвен.
explanationEn: Without any warning, when you are not prepared.
exampleEn: The surprise math quiz caught the whole class unawares.
mnemonicBg: Ън-ъ-УЕЪЗ — чуваш стреснато „уеър?!“ (къде?!): въртиш се объркан, защото те хванаха изневиделица.
bookSentenceEn: ‘It was that very night of summer, yet moonless and starless, that Orcs came on us at **unawares**.

definition: Deliberately created or arranged rather than arising naturally.
explanationBg: Нагласено и измислено нарочно, а не станало от само себе си — личи си, че е изкуствено подредено.
explanationEn: Planned and arranged on purpose instead of happening naturally.
exampleEn: The influencer's 'spontaneous' reaction looked totally contrived, like she had rehearsed it ten times.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „try“ по средата — някой толкова се е „трай-вал“ да изглежда естествено, че всичко стои нагласено.
bookSentenceEn: How that was **contrived** we cannot guess; but Gollum is cunning, and the spies of the Enemy are many.

definition: A colour or shade.
explanationBg: Цвят или оттенък на цвят — фината разлика например между небесносиньо и тюркоазено.
explanationEn: A colour or a shade of a colour.
exampleEn: She edited the photo until the sky turned a soft pink hue.
mnemonicBg: Hue звучи като началото на „хубав“ — хубавата снимка се познава по точно уцеления оттенък.
bookSentenceEn: Radagast is, of course, a worthy Wizard, a master of shapes and changes of **hue**; and he has much lore of herbs and beasts, and birds are especially his friends.

definition: To prevent or obstruct (something anticipated) by taking action in advance.
explanationBg: Да попречиш на нещо, което очакваш да се случи, като действаш преди него — изпреварваш го и така го осуетяваш.
explanationEn: To stop something before it happens by acting first.
exampleEn: I charged my phone the night before the trip to forestall any drama on the bus.
mnemonicBg: ФОР-СТОЛ — слагаш СТОЛ пред вратата ПРЕДИ крадецът да влезе: спрял си го предварително.
bookSentenceEn: But Saruman has long studied the arts of the Enemy himself, and thus we have often been able to **forestall** him.

definition: A house, flat, or other place of residence.
explanationBg: Място, където живее човек — къща, апартамент или какъвто и да е дом.
explanationEn: A house or any place where someone lives.
exampleEn: Their new dwelling was a tiny flat above the bakery, and it always smelled like fresh bread.
mnemonicBg: ДУЕЛ-инг — двама рицари излизат на дуел за най-хубавото жилище в селото.
bookSentenceEn: 336 the fellowship of the ring and I came at long last to the **dwelling** of Saruman.

definition: The hills lying at the northern base of a mountain range.
explanationBg: Ниските хълмове в самото северно подножие на планина — там, където планината „започва“ откъм север.
explanationEn: The hills at the northern bottom edge of a mountain range.
exampleEn: Our summer camp was tucked into the northmost foothills, where the air stayed cool even in July.
mnemonicBg: Планината има „крака“ (foot) — най-северните ѝ стъпалца са northmost foothills.
bookSentenceEn: And Boromir will tell you that that is a great open vale that lies between the Misty Mountains and the **northmost foothills** of Ered Nimrais, the White Mountains of his home.

definition: To surround or close off on all sides.
explanationBg: Да обградиш нещо от всички страни — да го затвориш вътре, както ограда затваря двор.
explanationEn: To surround something or close it in on every side.
exampleEn: A tall hedge encloses the school garden so the wind can't ruin the tomatoes.
mnemonicBg: in + close — „затваряш вътре“: кокошките в кошарата са оградени отвсякъде.
bookSentenceEn: But Isengard is a circle of sheer rocks that **enclose** a valley as with a wall, and in the midst of that valley is a tower of stone called Orthanc.

definition: The significance or importance of something.
explanationBg: Значението или важността на нещо — каква тежест носи то. Внимавай: тук думата не значи „внос“, а смисъл.
explanationEn: The importance or deeper meaning of something.
exampleEn: I didn't understand the full import of the coach's warning until we lost the next game.
mnemonicBg: Думата „внася“ (import) смисъл в изречението — каквото внася, това ѝ е значението.
bookSentenceEn: How long, I wonder, have you concealed from me, the head of the Council, a matter of greatest **import**?

definition: A place where someone or something hides waiting in ambush.
explanationBg: Скрито място, от което някой дебне и чака да изненада — скривалище за засада.
explanationEn: A hidden spot where someone waits secretly to attack or surprise.
exampleEn: Behind the old gym was the perfect lurking-place for our hide-and-seek champion.
mnemonicBg: Като lurker в чата — седи скрит и само наблюдава; lurking-place е ъгълът, от който дебне.
bookSentenceEn: the council of elrond 337 What brings you now from your **lurking-place** in the Shire?’’

definition: A feeling and expression of contempt or disdain.
explanationBg: Презрение — чувството, че гледаш на някого отвисоко, сякаш не заслужава уважение, и открито го показваш.
explanationEn: A strong feeling that someone or something deserves no respect.
exampleEn: He looked at my secondhand sneakers with scorn, which honestly said more about him than about me.
mnemonicBg: С-КОРН ~ скорпион — гледа те отвисоко, с вдигната опашка и крива усмивка: чисто презрение.
bookSentenceEn: ‘ ‘‘Radagast the Brown!’’ laughed Saruman, and he no longer concealed his **scorn**.

definition: Use or benefit; usefulness ("to no avail").
explanationBg: Полза, файда, резултат от усилието — често в израза „без никаква полза“: мъчиш се, а нищо не излиза.
explanationEn: Use or benefit; if something is 'to no avail', it brings no result.
exampleEn: I begged my parents for a later curfew, but to no avail.
mnemonicBg: ъ-ВЕЙЛ звучи почти като „файда“ — to no avail = „без никаква файда“.
bookSentenceEn: Against it the old allies and policies will not **avail** us at all.

definition: People sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representative.
explanationBg: Пратеници — хора, изпратени със специална задача, обикновено да представляват някого, като дипломати.
explanationEn: People sent on a special mission to speak for someone, like diplomats.
exampleEn: The two rival schools sent emissaries to plan the joint charity concert.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие „мисия“ — е-МИСИЯ-ри са хората, изпратени на специална мисия.
bookSentenceEn: ‘ ‘‘Saruman,’’ I said, ‘‘I have heard speeches of this kind before, but only in the mouths of **emissaries** sent from Mordor to deceive the ignorant.

definition: To praise formally or officially; to entrust to someone.
explanationBg: Да похвалиш някого официално или да го препоръчаш — а понякога и да повериш нещо ценно в нечии ръце.
explanationEn: To praise someone officially, or to trust someone with something.
exampleEn: The principal commended the volunteers for cleaning up the river bank.
mnemonicBg: ко-МЕНД ~ комент — оставяш хвалебствен комент под клипа на приятел: похвала пред всички.
bookSentenceEn: ‘‘Well, I see that this wise course does not **commend** itself to you,’’ he said.

definition: Workshops with furnaces where metal is shaped by heating and hammering.
explanationBg: Ковачници — работилници с огнище, където металът се нагрява до червено и се кове с чук, за да получи форма.
explanationEn: Workshops where metal is heated in a fire and hammered into shape.
exampleEn: On the museum trip we watched blacksmiths working at real forges, sparks flying everywhere.
mnemonicBg: Като Forge в Minecraft — огън + наковалня + чук = мечове: това е ковачницата.
bookSentenceEn: I looked on it and saw that, whereas it had once been green and fair, it was now ﬁlled with pits and **forges**.

definition: Gathering or assembling, especially troops; collecting strength or courage.
explanationBg: Събиране на хора на едно място, най-вече войници — или събиране на смелост и сили за нещо трудно.
explanationEn: Gathering people, especially soldiers, or collecting your courage.
exampleEn: After mustering all her courage, Mia finally sang in front of the whole school.
mnemonicBg: МЪСТЪ-ринг ~ мустак — генерал с огромни мустаци надува свирката и събира войската на плаца.
bookSentenceEn: Wolves and orcs were housed in Isengard, for Saruman was **mustering** a great force on his own account, in rivalry of Sauron and not in his service, yet.

definition: Guilty of or involving betrayal; dangerously unstable.
explanationBg: Коварен — който предава доверието ти; казва се и за опасни места, които изглеждат безобидни, например хлъзгава пътека.
explanationEn: Ready to betray you, or dangerous while seeming safe.
exampleEn: The hiking trail gets treacherous after rain, so we waited a day before climbing.
mnemonicBg: ТРЕ-ЧЕРИ-ъс — череша, сладка отвън, с червейче вътре: изглежда чудесно, а те предава.
bookSentenceEn: Gandalf the Grey caught like a ﬂy in a spider’s **treacherous** web!

definition: (Archaic) to or toward that place.
explanationBg: Старинна дума за „натам“, към онова място — днес никой не я ползва в разговор, но я срещаш в стари книги.
explanationEn: An old word meaning 'to that place'.
exampleEn: The old map in the library said 'go thither' instead of simply 'go there'.
mnemonicBg: Дядо сочи с бастуна: „Върви натам, чедо!“ — thither е прашасалото, старинно „натам“.
bookSentenceEn: And the Eagles of the Mountains went far and wide, and they saw many things: the gathering of wolves and the mustering of Orcs; and the Nine Riders going hither and **thither** in the lands; and they heard news of the escape of Gollum.

definition: Decreased in vigour, power, or extent; became smaller (especially of the moon).
explanationBg: Намаля, отслабна — за сила, светлина или интерес; за луната значи, че се е смалявала нощ след нощ.
explanationEn: Became smaller or weaker (often said about the moon).
exampleEn: My excitement about the series waned after the third boring episode.
mnemonicBg: УЕЙНД ~ Брус Уейн — без баткостюма силата на Уейн намаля и отслабна.
bookSentenceEn: ‘So it was that when summer **waned**, there came a night of moon, and Gwaihir the Windlord, swiftest of the Great

definition: (Literary) a horse, especially a riding horse.
explanationBg: Книжна, поетична дума за кон — особено кон за яздене, какъвто язди герой или рицар.
explanationEn: A literary word for a horse, especially one you ride.
exampleEn: In the fantasy game you can upgrade your steed so it gallops twice as fast.
mnemonicBg: Смени една буква и става speed — steed е „спортната кола“ на рицаря.
bookSentenceEn: ‘ ‘‘Then I must have a **steed** on land,’’ I said, ‘‘and a steed surpassingly swift, for I have never had such need of haste before.’’

definition: Bodies of men enlisted for military service, especially compulsorily.
explanationBg: Войници, свикани на служба — обикновени хора, събрани (често задължително) да се бият, когато се наложи.
explanationEn: Groups of people called up to serve as soldiers.
exampleEn: In history class we read how medieval kings raised levies from every village before a war.
mnemonicBg: ЛЕВИС ~ Levi's — цял полк новобранци, строени в еднакви дънки: свикани войници.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Then he must be a noble beast indeed,’ said Aragorn; ‘and it grieves me more than many tidings that might seem worse to learn that Sauron **levies** such tribute.

definition: To compete eagerly with someone in order to do or achieve something.
explanationBg: Да се състезаваш разгорещено с някого — да се надпреварвате кой ще постигне нещо пръв или по-добре.
explanationEn: To compete eagerly with someone for the same goal.
exampleEn: The two best players vie for the captain's armband every single season.
mnemonicBg: „Вай, вай!“ — въздиша публиката, докато двама се скъсват да се надпреварват за първото място.
bookSentenceEn: The horses of the Nine cannot **vie** with him; tireless, swift as the ﬂowing wind.

definition: A horse of Rohan, lord of the Mearas, ridden by Gandalf (Tolkien).
explanationBg: Сенкогрив — приказно бързият кон на магьосника Гандалф, господар на конете Меарас от земята Рохан.
explanationEn: The great horse of Rohan, lord of the Mearas, that Gandalf rides in Tolkien's story.
exampleEn: My cousin named his racing bike Shadowfax because nothing in the neighbourhood can keep up with it.
mnemonicBg: Shadow (сянка) + fax — кон, който „се изпраща“ бързо като факс и лети безшумно като сянка.
bookSentenceEn: **Shadowfax** they called him.

definition: The sound of a footstep.
explanationBg: Звукът от стъпка — тихото тупване, когато нечий крак докосне земята.
explanationEn: The sound that a footstep makes.
exampleEn: The library was so silent that every footfall echoed down the corridor.
mnemonicBg: foot (крак) + fall (пада) — кракът „пада“ на пода: туп!… туп!… — звукът от стъпки.
bookSentenceEn: Light is his **footfall**!

definition: Faults or failures to meet a standard.
explanationBg: Недостатъци, слабости — нещата, в които някой или нещо не достига до очакваното ниво.
explanationEn: Weak points or faults; ways of not being good enough.
exampleEn: Forgetting names is one of my biggest shortcomings, so I write everyone's birthday in my phone.
mnemonicBg: short + coming — скачаш към летвата, но „идваш късо“: все нещо мъничко не ти достига.
bookSentenceEn: He had much to say about the **shortcomings** of the new owners of Bag End.

definition: To accept or act in accordance with; to tolerate.
explanationBg: Да изтърпиш или понесеш нещо, което не ти харесва; а когато е за правило — да го приемеш и спазваш.
explanationEn: To accept or put up with something; to follow a rule.
exampleEn: I can abide loud music, but I can't stand people talking during a movie.
mnemonicBg: ъ-БАЙД ~ „а, байде…“ — въздъхваш дълбоко и търпиш; а abide by the rules = спазвам правилата.
bookSentenceEn: ‘ ‘‘I can’t **abide** changes,’’ said he, ‘‘not at my time of life, and least of all changes for the worst.’’

definition: A loud and impassioned noise or disturbance.
explanationBg: Силна врява и възмущение — когато много хора едновременно шумят, викат и протестират.
explanationEn: A loud noisy protest or disturbance from many people.
exampleEn: There was an uproar in the gym when the referee cancelled the winning goal.
mnemonicBg: up + roar — рев, който се вдига нагоре: зала, пълна с ревящи лъвове = врява до тавана.
bookSentenceEn: I came to Buckland and found it in **uproar**, as busy as a hive of ants that has been stirred with a stick.

definition: A structure in which bees live; a place full of busy activity.
explanationBg: Кошер — къщичката, в която живеят пчелите; преносно: място, което жужи от оживление и работа.
explanationEn: A home for bees, or any place full of busy activity.
exampleEn: On Monday mornings the school hallway is a hive of slamming lockers and last-minute homework.
mnemonicBg: ХАЙВ ~ „хайде!“ — хиляди пчели хвърчат едновременно с викове „хайде, хайде!“: жужащ кошер.
bookSentenceEn: I came to Buckland and found it in uproar, as busy as **a hive** of ants that has been stirred with a stick.

definition: Having or showing a stubborn and determined intention to do as one wants.
explanationBg: Своенравен и твърдоглав — прави каквото си е наумил и не слуша никого.
explanationEn: Stubborn and determined to do exactly what you want.
exampleEn: My wilful little sister refuses to wear a jacket even when it's freezing.
mnemonicBg: will (воля) + full (пълен) — препълнен с „искам!“: инат до козирката.
bookSentenceEn: They behaved very queer all the time they were here: **wilful**, you might say.’’

definition: Extreme anger.
explanationBg: Огромен, изпепеляващ гняв — не просто ядосване, а истинска ярост.
explanationEn: Very great anger; fury.
exampleEn: Mum's wrath was terrifying when she found the kitchen covered in flour.
mnemonicBg: Помисли за Кратос от God of War — той е ходеща wrath: ярост, от която земята трепери.
bookSentenceEn: The Captain then sent some eastward straight across country, and he himself with the rest rode along the Road in great **wrath**.

definition: A very strong wind.
explanationBg: Много силен вятър, почти буря — от онези, които огъват дървета и отнасят чадъри.
explanationEn: A very strong wind.
exampleEn: The gale knocked over our tent, so we spent half the night chasing it across the field.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „галя“, но прави точно обратното — не те гали, а ти отнася чадъра и шапката.
bookSentenceEn: ‘I galloped to Weathertop like a **gale**, and I reached it before sundown on my second day from Bree – and they were there before me.

definition: Surrounded by armed forces in order to capture; harassed persistently.
explanationBg: Обсаден — обкръжен от вражески сили, които искат да те превземат; преносно: затрупан отвсякъде с въпроси или молби.
explanationEn: Surrounded by enemies, or constantly attacked with demands.
exampleEn: After posting the trick-shot video, he was besieged by friends asking how he did it.
mnemonicBg: Като в Rainbow Six Siege — врагове от всички страни, а ти си затворен вътре: обсаден.
bookSentenceEn: But they closed round at night, and I was **besieged** on the hill-top, in the old ring of Amon Suˆl.

definition: Fires lit on hilltops to give warning of war or summon help.
explanationBg: Огньове, палени на върховете на хълмове, за да предупредят отдалеч, че идва война, или да повикат помощ.
explanationEn: Fires lit on hilltops to warn of war or call for help.
exampleEn: In the strategy game we lit war-beacons on the hills to call our allies into battle.
mnemonicBg: beacon ~ „бекон“ — огънят на хълма не пече бекон, а праща сигнал: „Война! Помощ!“.
bookSentenceEn: I was hard put to it indeed: such light and ﬂame cannot have been seen on Weathertop since the **war-beacons** of old.

definition: Foolishness; a lack of good sense.
explanationBg: Глупост, безразсъдство — постъпка, която показва пълна липса на здрав разум.
explanationEn: A foolish act or a lack of good sense.
exampleEn: Riding a skateboard down the steepest street in town was pure folly.
mnemonicBg: ФОЛИ ~ фолио — да си направиш шапка от фолио срещу дъжда е чиста folly: пълна глупост.
bookSentenceEn: It was impossible to ﬁnd you, Frodo, in the wilderness, and it would have been **folly** to try with all the Nine at my heels.

definition: To get, acquire, or secure something.
explanationBg: Да получиш или да се сдобиеш с нещо — да си го осигуриш, често с известно усилие.
explanationEn: To get or gain something, often with some effort.
exampleEn: You have to obtain a signed permission slip before joining the climbing trip.
mnemonicBg: об-ТЕЙН ~ „обтегни се“ — поразтегни се, протегни ръка и ще се сдобиеш с каквото искаш: нищо не идва даром.
bookSentenceEn: 346 the fellowship of the ring ‘Could we not still send messages to him and **obtain** his help?’ asked Erestor.

definition: Not guessed or suspected.
explanationBg: Неподозиран — нещо, което никой не е познал и не е очаквал, че съществува или ще се случи.
explanationEn: Not guessed or expected by anyone.
exampleEn: The plot twist was completely unguessed — nobody in our book club saw it coming.
mnemonicBg: un + guess — нещо, което и най-добрият гадател с кристално кълбо не успя да познае.
bookSentenceEn: We could not now take it back to him, **unguessed**, unmarked by any spy.

definition: A short period of rest or relief from something difficult.
explanationBg: Кратка почивка или отсрочка — миг на облекчение насред нещо тежко.
explanationEn: A short rest or break from something hard.
exampleEn: The rain gave us a short respite from the brutal afternoon training.
mnemonicBg: РЕС-пайт ~ respawn — кратка пауза, в която „се съживяваш“ преди следващия рунд.
bookSentenceEn: The Nine have been unhorsed indeed, but that is but a **respite**, ere they ﬁnd new steeds and swifter.

definition: (Of the moon) showing a decreasing area of brightness; diminishing.
explanationBg: Намаляващ, отслабващ — за луната: когато светлата ѝ част се смалява нощ след нощ.
explanationEn: Getting smaller or weaker, like the moon when its bright part shrinks.
exampleEn: We watched the waning moon get thinner every night during the camping week.
mnemonicBg: Луната е на диета — waning значи, че „отслабва“ по малко всяка нощ.
bookSentenceEn: Only the **waning** might of Gondor stands now between him and a march in power along the coasts into the North; and if he comes, assailing the White Towers and the Havens, hereafter the Elves may have no escape from the lengthening shadows of Middleearth.’

definition: Making a concerted or violent attack on.
explanationBg: Нападащ, атакуващ — нахвърлящ се срещу някого или нещо с пълна сила.
explanationEn: Attacking someone or something with force.
exampleEn: Two defenders kept assailing our striker, but she still scored.
mnemonicBg: ъ-СЕЙЛ ~ SALE — тълпата в първата секунда на разпродажбата: щурмува, напада, помита щандовете.
bookSentenceEn: Only the waning might of Gondor stands now between him and a march in power along the coasts into the North; and if he comes, **assailing** the White Towers and the Havens, hereafter the Elves may have no escape from the lengthening shadows of Middleearth.’

definition: Decreases in vigour or extent; (of the moon) appears smaller.
explanationBg: Намалява, губи сила — за интерес, светлина или мощ; за луната: изглежда все по-малка.
explanationEn: Becomes smaller or weaker, like the moon late in the month.
exampleEn: My phone battery wanes so fast that I carry a power bank everywhere.
mnemonicBg: WANE звучи като „вехне“ — ентусиазмът вехне и се смалява като цвете без вода.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Gondor **wanes**, you say.

definition: A subtle distinction or detail; a fine point.
explanationBg: Тънкост, фин детайл — малка, едва доловима разлика, която забелязват само познавачите.
explanationEn: A small fine detail or subtle difference.
exampleEn: Chess looks simple until you discover every nicety of the opening moves.
mnemonicBg: Вътре се крие nice — малкият фин детайл, който прави нещата наистина nice.
bookSentenceEn: For he is very wise, and weighs all things to a **nicety** in the scales of his malice.

definition: In a way that does not result in the desired outcome; in vain.
explanationBg: Напразно, без успех — колкото и да опитваш, желаният резултат така и не идва.
explanationEn: Without success; with no useful result.
exampleEn: I searched vainly for my earphones all morning — they were in my pocket the whole time.
mnemonicBg: ВЕЙН ~ веене на вятър — усилието отива „на вятъра“: духаш срещу бурята напразно.
bookSentenceEn: A great dread fell on him, as if he was awaiting the pronouncement of some doom that he had long foreseen and **vainly** hoped might after all never be spoken.

definition: Very great in amount; very strong; defeating completely.
explanationBg: Толкова огромен или силен, че те залива целия и не можеш да му устоиш или да се справиш с него.
explanationEn: So strong or so big that you cannot resist or handle it.
exampleEn: The support from the whole school was overwhelming after our team reached the final.
mnemonicBg: WHELM звучи като „вълна“ — огромна вълна те залива презглава: непосилно много.
bookSentenceEn: An **overwhelming** longing to rest and remain at peace by Bilbo’s side in Rivendell ﬁlled all his heart.

definition: Sharpness or quickness, especially of mind or senses; eagerness.
explanationBg: Острота на ума или сетивата — а също и жар, ентусиазъм, силно желание да правиш нещо.
explanationEn: Sharpness of mind or senses, or strong enthusiasm.
exampleEn: Her keenness for astronomy is so contagious that half the class joined the stargazing club.
mnemonicBg: КИЙН ~ кинжал — ум, остър като кинжал, плюс хъс да го използваш веднага.
bookSentenceEn: the council of elrond 353 Elrond raised his eyes and looked at him, and Frodo felt his heart pierced by the sudden **keenness** of the glance.

definition: (Past of creep) moved slowly and quietly, especially with stealth.
explanationBg: Промъкна се — движеше се бавно, тихо и незабелязано (минало време на „промъквам се, пълзя“).
explanationEn: Moved slowly and quietly so nobody would notice (past of creep).
exampleEn: I crept past my parents' bedroom at midnight to grab a snack from the kitchen.
mnemonicBg: КРЕПТ ~ креп — промъкваш се на пръсти към кухнята за последната палачинка-креп, без да изскърца подът.
bookSentenceEn: Merry and Pippin were indignant when they heard that Sam had **crept** into the Council, and had been chosen as Frodo’s companion.

definition: Impertinent behaviour or talk; boldness or audacity.
explanationBg: Дързост и нахалство — когато някой си позволява нагли приказки или държание без капка срам. В този смисъл не означава „буза“.
explanationEn: Rude boldness; talking or acting without respect but with confidence.
exampleEn: He had the cheek to ask for my notes after skipping class all week.
mnemonicBg: На български имаме „дебели очи“, на английски — cheek („буза“): нахалство с дебели бузи.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Instead of throwing him out, and clapping him in chains, Elrond goes and rewards him for his **cheek**!’

definition: Expressed strong disapproval of; sentenced to a punishment.
explanationBg: Остро порицан — всички ясно са казали, че постъпката е лоша и непростима. В съда пък значи, че на някого е наложено наказание.
explanationEn: Strongly criticized as wrong, or officially given a punishment.
exampleEn: The school condemned the cheating scandal and cancelled the test results.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „кондензирано“ — представи си съдия, който тропва с чукчето и осъжда крадеца на кондензирано мляко: condemned!
bookSentenceEn: You are not thinking what you are saying: **condemned** to go on this hopeless journey, a reward?

definition: Not easily bent or changed in shape; rigid.
explanationBg: Твърд и труден за огъване — не се извива лесно, като дъска или като схванат след тренировка мускул.
explanationEn: Hard and not easy to bend.
exampleEn: My legs were so stiff after the football match that I could barely climb the stairs.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „щифт“ — металният щифт е твърд и не се огъва, точно като схванат врат след тренировка.
bookSentenceEn: We have come a long way with you and been through some **stiff** times.

definition: Soldiers or other persons sent ahead to gather information.
explanationBg: Хора, изпратени напред преди останалите, за да огледат пътя и да съберат сведения какво ги чака.
explanationEn: People sent ahead of a group to look around and collect information.
exampleEn: Before the hike, two scouts went ahead to check if the trail was safe.
mnemonicBg: Същата дума като нашите „скаути“ — децата с шалчетата, които първи тръгват напред да разузнаят терена.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Some of the **scouts** have been sent out already.

definition: To search thoroughly through a place or thing for something.
explanationBg: Да претърсиш нещо много старателно, ъгълче по ъгълче, докато намериш каквото търсиш.
explanationEn: To search a place very carefully and completely.
exampleEn: I scoured my whole room looking for my earbuds before school.
mnemonicBg: Запомни двойката: scout-ът тръгва да scour-ва — разузнавачът претърсва всичко педя по педя.
bookSentenceEn: We shall have to **scour** the lands all round for many long leagues before any move is made.

definition: The ledge or sill forming the bottom part of a window.
explanationBg: Долната хоризонтална дъска или плоча на прозореца — мястото, където слагаш саксия или където котката обича да седи.
explanationEn: The flat shelf at the bottom of a window.
exampleEn: Our cat spends every afternoon sleeping on the window-sill in the sun.
mnemonicBg: Sill звучи като „сила“ — первазът има сила да удържи и саксиите, и котката отгоре.
bookSentenceEn: So great was Frodo’s delight at this announcement that Gandalf left the **window-sill**, where he had been sitting, and took off his hat and bowed.

definition: (Of the moon) increased in apparent size; grew larger or stronger.
explanationBg: Нарасна и засия по-силно — казва се най-вече за луната, която от тънък сърп всяка нощ става все по-пълна.
explanationEn: Grew bigger or stronger, especially the moon becoming fuller.
exampleEn: The moon waxed all week until it hung huge and bright over the campsite.
mnemonicBg: Wax значи и „восък“ — представи си, че луната е восъчна свещ, която някой долива всяка нощ, и тя расте ли, расте.
bookSentenceEn: The Hunter’s Moon **waxed** round in the night sky, and put to ﬂight all the lesser stars.

definition: Strips or small pieces, especially ones torn or cut from something larger.
explanationBg: Малки откъснати или отрязани ивици и парченца от нещо по-голямо — като лист, накъсан на тънки лентички.
explanationEn: Small thin pieces torn or cut from something bigger.
exampleEn: After the dog got to my homework, all I found were shreds of paper under the table.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „шредер“ — машината в офиса, която нарязва листовете на тънки лентички.
bookSentenceEn: The hobbits had been nearly two months in the house of Elrond, and November had gone by with the last **shreds** of autumn, and December was passing, when the scouts began to return.

definition: Old and torn; in poor condition.
explanationBg: Стар и целият скъсан — дреха или знаме, което виси на парцали от дълга употреба.
explanationEn: Old and badly torn.
exampleEn: He refuses to throw away his tattered hoodie because it is his lucky one.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „тъй дърт“ в tattered — толкова дърт и износен, че виси на парцали.
bookSentenceEn: On the rocks of the rapids below it searchers discovered the bodies of ﬁve more, and also a long black cloak, slashed and **tattered**.

definition: Lacking a definite or attractive shape.
explanationBg: Без ясна или красива форма — нещо размъкнато, по което не личи каква форма изобщо е трябвало да има.
explanationEn: Without a clear or nice shape.
exampleEn: She hid her new dress under a shapeless old sweatshirt.
mnemonicBg: Shape (форма) + less (без) = без форма — като огромния суичър, в който се губиш цялата.
bookSentenceEn: ‘It is rash to be too sure, yet I think that we may hope now that the Ringwraiths were scattered, and have been obliged to return as best they could to their Master in Mordor, empty and **shapeless**.

definition: To create or bring about, especially with skill and effort.
explanationBg: Да измислиш и нагласиш нещо хитро, с умение и усилие — да скроиш план как да се случи.
explanationEn: To cleverly plan and manage to make something happen.
exampleEn: We contrived a plan to throw a surprise party without our friend noticing anything.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „try“ вътре в contrive — опитваш, нагласяваш, пак опитваш, докато хитрият план се получи.
bookSentenceEn: I will send out messages, such as I can **contrive**, to those whom I know in the wide world; but so perilous are the lands now become that some may well miscarry, or come no quicker than you yourself.

definition: (Of a plan or action) to fail; to be unsuccessful.
explanationBg: Когато план или начинание се проваля — нещата не се получават така, както са били замислени.
explanationEn: To fail; to not work out as planned.
exampleEn: Our plan to sneak snacks into the cinema miscarried when the bag ripped open.
mnemonicBg: Mis (грешно) + carry (нося) — носиш тортата за партито накриво, изпускаш я и целият план се проваля.
bookSentenceEn: I will send out messages, such as I can contrive, to those whom I know in the wide world; but so perilous are the lands now become that some may well **miscarry**, or come no quicker than you yourself.

definition: Forged again before (a certain time); remade beforehand.
explanationBg: Старинен израз: reforged значи „изкован наново“ (за метал или меч), а ere е древна думичка за „преди“ — тоест прекован преди определен момент.
explanationEn: Made again in the forge before a certain time ('ere' is an old word for 'before').
exampleEn: In the video game, the broken sword must be reforged ere the final boss appears.
mnemonicBg: Re- значи „пак“, forge — „кова“, а ere звучи като „еее, рано е!“ — значи „преди“: прековано преди срока.

definition: Marked with or emitting rays of light.
explanationBg: Който излъчва лъчи или е украсен с лъчи — като нарисувано слънце с чертички около него.
explanationEn: Shining with rays, or decorated with lines like sun rays.
exampleEn: She drew a rayed sun in the corner of every page of her notebook.
mnemonicBg: Сети се за X-ray (рентгена): ray е лъч, а rayed значи „целият в лъчи“ — като слънчице в тетрадка.
bookSentenceEn: The Sword of Elendil was forged anew by Elvish smiths, and on its blade was traced a device of seven stars set between the crescent Moon and the **rayed** Sun, and about them was written many runes; for Aragorn son of Arathorn was going to war upon the marches of Mordor.

definition: In poor condition through long use or lack of care.
explanationBg: Износен и занемарен от дълга употреба — изглежда стар, проскубан и недогледан.
explanationEn: Looking old and worn because of long use or little care.
exampleEn: The youth club looks shabby from outside, but inside it has the best music gear in town.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „шал на баба“ в shabby — старият бабин шал: овехтял, оръфан, но любим.
bookSentenceEn: He took from the box a small sword in an old **shabby** leathern scabbard.

definition: An object or collection wrapped in paper for carrying or sending by post.
explanationBg: Пратка — нещо, опаковано в хартия или кутия, което носиш или изпращаш по пощата.
explanationEn: A wrapped package that you carry or send by post.
exampleEn: A parcel with my new sneakers finally arrived after two weeks of waiting.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „парцел“ — представи си, че получаваш по пощата цял парцел земя, опакован с панделка: пакет!
bookSentenceEn: ‘Also there is this!’ said Bilbo, bringing out **a parcel** which seemed to be rather heavy for its size.

definition: Undone after being wound; relaxed after stress.
explanationBg: Размотан — нещо навито (прежда, кабел) е развито обратно. Казва се и за човек, който се е отпуснал след напрежение.
explanationEn: Unrolled or untwisted; also relaxed after stress.
exampleEn: After the tournament, we unwound at home with pizza and video games.
mnemonicBg: Un- (раз-) + wound (навит): котката е размотала кълбото прежда из стаята — и ти така се „размотаваш“ след стрес.
bookSentenceEn: He **unwound** several folds of old cloth, and held up a small shirt of mail.

definition: A feeling of unease or embarrassment; awkwardness.
explanationBg: Чувство на неудобство и леко срамуване — когато ти става тъпо и не знаеш къде да се денеш.
explanationEn: A feeling of embarrassment and awkward unease.
exampleEn: To her discomfiture, the teacher read her note aloud to the whole class.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „комфи“ (comfy — удобно) с „дис“ отпред — хич не ти е комфи: неудобно и срамно ти е.

definition: Equipment, especially that used for a particular activity.
explanationBg: Всичките неща и принадлежности, които ти трябват за дадено занимание — за спорт, поход или музика.
explanationEn: The equipment you need for a particular activity.
exampleEn: Do not forget your goalkeeper gear for Saturday's match.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „гира“ — гирите във фитнеса са част от спортната ти екипировка.
bookSentenceEn: The Company took little **gear** of war, for their hope was in secrecy not in battle.

definition: A line of descent; lineage.
explanationBg: Родовата линия на човек — веригата от предци, от които произхожда: родители, баби, дядовци и така назад във времето.
explanationEn: The line of family ancestors a person comes from.
exampleEn: She traced her family's linage back to a small mountain village.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „line“ (линия) вътре — родът ти е една дълга линия от хора, която стига чак до теб.

definition: A horn blown to give signals in war or to rally troops.
explanationBg: Рог, който се надува по време на битка — със звука му се дават сигнали и се събират войниците.
explanationEn: A horn blown in battle to send signals to soldiers.
exampleEn: Our team captain blew a plastic war-horn from the stands every time we scored.
mnemonicBg: War (война) + horn (рог) — представи си вувузела на стадиона, само че за битка: боен рог.
bookSentenceEn: Boromir had a long sword, in fashion like Andu´ril but of less lineage, and he bore also a shield and his **war-horn**.

definition: Extremely serious or urgent; deplorable; ominous.
explanationBg: Изключително сериозен и страшен — положение, което е тежко и изисква спешни действия.
explanationEn: Very serious, urgent, or terrible.
exampleEn: The team was in dire need of a goal in the last five minutes.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „die“ (умирам) в dire — толкова сериозно е, че звучи на живот и смърт.
bookSentenceEn: 364 the fellowship of the ring said Elrond, ‘until you stand once more on the borders of your land, and **dire** need is on you.’

definition: Having a wide blade.
explanationBg: С широко острие — нож, меч или сечиво, чиято режеща част е широка.
explanationEn: Having a wide cutting blade.
exampleEn: Grandpa uses a broad-bladed knife to slice the watermelon in one cut.
mnemonicBg: Broad (широк) + blade (острие) — нож с острие, широко като лопата за сняг.
bookSentenceEn: Gimli the dwarf alone wore openly a short shirt of steelrings, for dwarves make light of burdens; and in his belt was a **broad-bladed** axe.

definition: An archer’s portable case for arrows.
explanationBg: Калъф, който стрелецът носи на гърба или на кръста си и в който държи стрелите си.
explanationEn: A case an archer uses to carry arrows.
exampleEn: At archery practice she pulled the last arrow from her quiver and hit the bullseye.
mnemonicBg: Звучи близко до „куфар“ — мини-куфарче за стрели, метнато на гърба на стрелеца.
bookSentenceEn: Legolas had a bow and **a quiver**, and at his belt a long white knife.

definition: Armour made of interlinked metal rings.
explanationBg: Броня от хиляди малки метални халкички, вплетени една в друга — като метален пуловер, който пази от удари.
explanationEn: Armour made of many small metal rings linked together.
exampleEn: In the museum we tried lifting a real mail-coat, and it was heavier than my school bag.
mnemonicBg: Представи си, че пощата (mail) ти доставя палто (coat) от метални халкички — ризница с куриер до вратата.
bookSentenceEn: The younger hobbits wore the swords that they had taken from the barrow; but Frodo took only Sting; and his **mail-coat**, as Bilbo wished, remained hidden.

definition: (Archaic) past of gird; encircled or bound.
explanationBg: Старинна дума: опасан, стегнат с колан или ремък — например с меч, препасан на кръста.
explanationEn: An old word meaning tied or fastened around, like with a belt.
exampleEn: The karate master stood girt with his black belt, ready to begin the lesson.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „гердан“ — както герданът опасва шията, така girt значи опасан, препасан.
bookSentenceEn: Gandalf bore his staff, but **girt** at his side was the elven-sword Glamdring, the mate of Orcrist that lay now upon the breast of Thorin under the Lonely Mountain.

definition: In a cold or unfeeling manner, like stone.
explanationBg: Студено и без никакво чувство — с каменно изражение, все едно нищо не може да те трогне.
explanationEn: In a cold way that shows no feeling, like stone.
exampleEn: When I asked to borrow her charger again, she just stared at me stonily.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „stone“ (камък) вътре — гледаш някого с лице като камък: студено и без капка емоция.
bookSentenceEn: Sam was standing by the pony, sucking his teeth, and staring moodily into the gloom where the river roared **stonily** below; his desire for adventure was at its lowest ebb.

definition: The movement of the tide out to sea; a decline.
explanationBg: Отливът — когато морето се отдръпва от брега. Преносно: когато нещо постепенно намалява и отслабва.
explanationEn: The flow of the sea away from the shore; a slow decline.
exampleEn: We waited for the ebb so we could hunt for crabs on the wet sand.
mnemonicBg: Морето си играе на гоненица: flow — идва към теб, ebb — отдръпва се назад; каквото е „на ebb“, спада.
bookSentenceEn: Sam was standing by the pony, sucking his teeth, and staring moodily into the gloom where the river roared stonily below; his desire for adventure was at its lowest **ebb**.

definition: Grass that has been cut and dried for use as fodder.
explanationBg: Окосена и изсушена трева, с която се хранят животните през зимата — сеното на село.
explanationEn: Dried cut grass used as food for farm animals.
exampleEn: We spent the afternoon jumping off hay bales at my uncle's farm.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „Хей!“ — викаш „Хей!“ от върха на купа сено на село.
bookSentenceEn: You could have stayed here and et the best **hay** till the new grass comes.’

definition: In a sullen or gloomy manner.
explanationBg: Мрачно и намусено — когато правиш нещо с такова кисело настроение, че всички го забелязват.
explanationEn: In a gloomy, bad-tempered way.
exampleEn: He sat moodily at the back of the bus after losing the game.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „mood“ — когато си в лош муд, правиш всичко moodily: мрачно и навъсено.
bookSentenceEn: Sam was standing by the pony, sucking his teeth, and staring **moodily** into the gloom where the river roared stonily below; his desire for adventure was at its lowest ebb.

definition: Packed or stored away neatly.
explanationBg: Прибран и подреден на мястото му — багаж или вещи, грижливо натъкмени за съхранение или за път.
explanationEn: Packed and put away neatly.
exampleEn: She stowed her snowboard in the attic until next winter.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „сто“ — прибираш сто неща в куфара, всяко на мястото му: stowed.
bookSentenceEn: Sam eased the pack on his shoulders, and went over anxiously in his mind all the things that he had **stowed** in it, wondering if he had forgotten anything: his chief treasure, his cooking gear; and the little box of salt that he always carried and reﬁlled when he could; a good supply…

definition: Justification or authority; a written authorisation.
explanationBg: Основание или официално право да направиш нещо; също документ, който дава такова право — например полицейска заповед за обиск.
explanationEn: A good reason or official permission to do something.
exampleEn: In the detective game, the police cannot search the mansion without a warrant.
mnemonicBg: Представи си портиер на име Уорън, който те пуска само с документ — warrant е разрешителното на Уорън.
bookSentenceEn: …anything: his chief treasure, his cooking gear; and the little box of salt that he always carried and reﬁlled when he could; a good supply of pipe-weed (but not near enough, I’ll **warrant**); ﬂint and tinder; woollen hose; linen; various small belongings of his master’s that Frodo had forgotten and Sam had stowed to bring them out in triumph when they were called…

definition: Dry, easily flammable material used to start a fire.
explanationBg: Сухи тревички, кора или мъх, които пламват и от една искра — с тях се подпалва огънят.
explanationEn: Dry material that catches fire easily, used for starting a fire.
exampleEn: We collected dry leaves and bark as tinder for the campfire.
mnemonicBg: Сещаш се за приложението Tinder? Кръстено е точно на това — сухите съчки, в които една искра пали огън.
bookSentenceEn: …treasure, his cooking gear; and the little box of salt that he always carried and reﬁlled when he could; a good supply of pipe-weed (but not near enough, I’ll warrant); ﬂint and **tinder**; woollen hose; linen; various small belongings of his master’s that Frodo had forgotten and Sam had stowed to bring them out in triumph when they were called for.

definition: Split or divided in two; (of a hoof) divided into parts.
explanationBg: Разцепен на две части — както копитото на козата е разделено на две половинки.
explanationEn: Split into two parts, like a goat's hoof.
exampleEn: The old oak stood cloven in two after the lightning storm.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „клон“ в cloven — мълнията удря клона и го разцепва точно на две.
bookSentenceEn: They crossed the bridge and wound slowly up the long steep paths that led out of the **cloven** vale of Rivendell; and they came at length to the high moor where the wind hissed through the heather.

definition: The soldiers at the rear of a body of troops, especially protecting against attack.
explanationBg: Бойците в самия край на колоната, които пазят гърба на всички останали от нападение.
explanationEn: The soldiers at the back of a group who protect it from behind.
exampleEn: In paintball our team always leaves two players as a rearguard near the base.
mnemonicBg: Rear (отзад) + guard (пазач) — приятелят, който върви последен и вика: „Спокойно, аз пазя тила!“
bookSentenceEn: The others were in ﬁle behind, and Legolas whose eyes were keen was the **rearguard**.

definition: Caused to stop sleeping; awoken; provoked into action.
explanationBg: Събуден от сън или раздвижен за действие — някой те е вдигнал на крака.
explanationEn: Woken up from sleep, or pushed into action.
exampleEn: The smell of pancakes roused me faster than any alarm.
mnemonicBg: Звучи почти като „раздрусан“ — баба те раздрусва рано сутрин: „Ставай!“ — и ето те roused.
bookSentenceEn: In the late afternoon they were **roused** by the watch, and took their chief meal: cold and cheerless as a rule, for they could seldom risk the lighting of a ﬁre.

definition: Changed direction suddenly.
explanationBg: Рязко смени посоката — както колело, което внезапно свива встрани, за да избегне дупка.
explanationEn: Changed direction suddenly.
exampleEn: The cyclist veered left to avoid a puddle and splashed us anyway.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „вираж“ във veered — колата прави рязък вираж и сменя посоката за секунда.
bookSentenceEn: The wind suddenly fell and then **veered** round to the south.

definition: A very steep rock face or cliff, typically a tall one.
explanationBg: Висока, почти отвесна скала — стоиш на ръба, а под краката ти зейва пропаст.
explanationEn: A very steep and high cliff.
exampleEn: We took photos near the precipice but kept well back from the edge.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „пред сипей“ в precipice — заставаш пред стръмния сипей и стомахът ти се свива.
bookSentenceEn: 368 the fellowship of the ring snow; its great, bare, northern **precipice** was still largely in the shadow, but where the sunlight slanted upon it, it glowed red.

definition: Fell or shone at an angle upon it.
explanationBg: Падна или огря нещо под ъгъл — например светлина, която не пада право отгоре, а косо, отстрани.
explanationEn: Fell or shone on something at an angle, not straight down.
exampleEn: When I opened my laptop by the window, the sunlight slanted upon it and washed out the screen.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „склон“ в slant — каквото е по склона, е под наклон: светлината пада косо.
bookSentenceEn: 368 the fellowship of the ring snow; its great, bare, northern precipice was still largely in the shadow, but where the sunlight **slanted upon it**, it glowed red.

definition: Less harsh or severe than before; gentler.
explanationBg: По-мек и по-нежен от преди — за време, вкус или характер, който вече не е толкова суров.
explanationEn: Softer or less severe than before.
exampleEn: The weather turned milder, so we finally moved football practice outside.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „мил“ в milder — колкото по-мил, толкова по-мек и по-благ.
bookSentenceEn: The land and the weather will be **milder** now, but perhaps all the more dangerous.’

definition: Place-name (Dimrill Dale): a valley at the foot of the Misty Mountains.
explanationBg: Име на място от книгата — дол (долина) в подножието на Мъгливите планини. Буквално значи „сумрачно поточе“: dim — сумрачен, rill — поточе.
explanationEn: The name of a valley at the foot of the mountains; it means 'shadowy little stream'.
exampleEn: We named the shady little stream behind our campsite Dimrill, and the name stuck all summer.
mnemonicBg: Dim (сумрак) + rill (поточе) — представи си ручейче в сянката на планината привечер: сумрачно поточе.
bookSentenceEn: ‘If we climb the pass that is called the Redhorn Gate, under the far side of Caradhras, we shall come down by the **Dimrill** Stair into the deep vale of the Dwarves.

definition: A still, deep lake in the Dimrill Dale, sacred to the Dwarves (Tolkien).
explanationBg: Име на езеро от книгата — дълбоко и съвсем неподвижно, свещено за джуджетата. Водата му отразява всичко като огледало, оттам и името.
explanationEn: The name of a deep, still lake that reflects everything like a mirror.
exampleEn: We named the calm lake by our cabin Mirrormere because it reflected every cloud perfectly.
mnemonicBg: Mirror (огледало) + mere (езеро) — езеро-огледало: поглеждаш в него и виждаш небето като в селфи камера.
bookSentenceEn: There lies the **Mirrormere**, and there the River Silverlode rises in its icy springs.’

definition: Springs of very cold water issuing from the ground.
explanationBg: Извори с ледено студена вода, която блика направо от земята — толкова студена, че ръцете ти изтръпват.
explanationEn: Places where very cold water comes out of the ground.
exampleEn: On the mountain hike we refilled our bottles from icy springs.
mnemonicBg: Icy = леден (като „айс“), springs = извори — изворче, по-студено и от айскафе, преляло с лед.
bookSentenceEn: There lies the Mirrormere, and there the River Silverlode rises in its **icy springs**.’

definition: A passionate expression of grief or sorrow.
explanationBg: Силен израз на мъка и скръб — тъжна песен, плач или думи, с които оплакваш нещо изгубено.
explanationEn: A strong expression of grief, often a sad song or cry.
exampleEn: Her new song is a lament for a friendship that ended over the summer.
mnemonicBg: Чуй го като „ла-мент“ — тъжна балада, в която проточваш: „лааа… каква мъка!“
bookSentenceEn: Only I hear the stones **lament** them: deep they delved us, fair they wrought us, high they builded us; but they are gone.

definition: Covered or enveloped so as to hide from view.
explanationBg: Обвит и закрит така, че да не се вижда — като планина, скрита в гъста мъгла.
explanationEn: Covered or wrapped so that it cannot be seen.
exampleEn: The football pitch was shrouded in morning fog, so we could not even see the goals.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „шал“ в shrouded — мъглата е увила планината с огромен сив шал и нищо не се вижда.
bookSentenceEn: That morning they lit a ﬁre in a deep hollow **shrouded** by great bushes of holly, and their supper-breakfast was merrier than it had been since they set out.

definition: Shrubs of the holly plant, which has prickly leaves and red berries.
explanationBg: Храсти от джел — вечнозеленото растение с бодливи лъскави листа и червени топчета, познато от коледната украса.
explanationEn: Bushes of a plant with prickly shiny leaves and red berries.
exampleEn: We decorated the bushes of holly in our yard with fairy lights for Christmas.
mnemonicBg: Запомни: ХОЛИ-вуд буквално значи „гора от джел“ — бодливите коледни храстчета с червените топчета.
bookSentenceEn: That morning they lit a ﬁre in a deep hollow shrouded by great **bushes of holly**, and their supper-breakfast was merrier than it had been since they set out.

definition: In a firm or steady manner; without faltering.
explanationBg: Равномерно и стабилно, без спиране и без колебание — с едно и също сигурно темпо.
explanationEn: In a firm, even way, without stopping or shaking.
exampleEn: Her grades improved steadily once she started studying twenty minutes a day.
mnemonicBg: Като в „Ready, steady, go!“ — стабилно и равно темпо, без засечки чак до финала.
bookSentenceEn: Flocks of birds, ﬂying at great speed, were wheeling and circling, and traversing all the land as if they were searching for something; and they were **steadily** drawing nearer.

definition: A large permanent unit of an army.
explanationBg: Голяма постоянна войскова част — стотици войници, които служат и действат заедно под общо командване.
explanationEn: A large permanent unit of soldiers in an army.
exampleEn: My great-grandfather's old photos show his whole regiment lined up in uniform.
mnemonicBg: Чуй „режим“ в regiment — цял полк живее по строг режим: ставане, строй, марш!
bookSentenceEn: ‘**Regiments** of black crows are ﬂying over all the land between the Mountains and the Greyﬂood,’ he said, ‘and they have passed over Hollin.

definition: A large, densely packed crowd of people.
explanationBg: Огромна, гъста тълпа — толкова много хора на едно място, че едва се разминават.
explanationEn: A very large, tightly packed crowd of people.
exampleEn: A throng of fans waited outside the arena hours before the concert.
mnemonicBg: Звучи като „трон“ — гъста тълпа се блъска около трона, всички искат да зърнат краля.
bookSentenceEn: As they passed overhead, in so dense **a throng** that their shadow followed them darkly over the ground below, one harsh croak was heard.

definition: A person, thing, or circumstance causing inconvenience or annoyance.
explanationBg: Нещо или някой, който ти лази по нервите и ти пречи — дразнеща неприятност, без да е истинска беда.
explanationEn: Something or someone that annoys you and causes small problems.
exampleEn: The pop-up ads in that free game are a real nuisance.
mnemonicBg: Представи си комар на име Нюсънс, който бръмчи в ухото ти точно когато заспиваш — жива досада.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Well if that isn’t a plague and **a nuisance**!’ said Pippin.

definition: Large, evil crows of Fangorn and Dunland, used as spies (Tolkien).
explanationBg: Измислена дума от книгата: големи зли врани, които летят на ята и шпионират за господаря си.
explanationEn: A made-up name for big evil crows that work as spies.
exampleEn: In our fantasy board game, flocks of crebain circle the map and spy on the players' hideouts.
mnemonicBg: Започва като „крякане“ — ято черни врани кряка над теб и докладва всичко, което види.
bookSentenceEn: ‘Luckily our ﬁre made little smoke, and had burned low before the **crebain** came,’ said Aragorn.

definition: Disastrous or destructive; in ruins.
explanationBg: Който носи разруха и тежки загуби — толкова вреден, че може да съсипе планове, сгради или джоба ти; казва се и за нещо, което вече е в развалини.
explanationEn: Causing terrible damage or destruction; also describing something fallen into ruins.
exampleEn: Buying game skins every week proved ruinous for my pocket money.
mnemonicBg: В ruinous се крие думата „руини“ — нещо толкова съсипващо, че оставя след себе си само руини.
bookSentenceEn: Many of them looked to have been worked by hands, though now they lay tumbled and **ruinous** in a bleak, barren land.

definition: Becomes more intense or profound; becomes deeper.
explanationBg: Става все по-дълбок — или все по-силен и наситен, когато говорим за чувство, цвят или криза.
explanationEn: Becomes deeper, stronger, or more intense.
exampleEn: Our friendship deepens every summer we spend at the same volleyball camp.
mnemonicBg: Deep значи „дълбок“ — представи си басейн, чието дъно потъва все по-надолу: deepens!
bookSentenceEn: ‘Winter **deepens** behind us,’ he said quietly to Aragorn.

definition: Intercepted on the way, especially in order to attack or rob.
explanationBg: Когато някой те е дебнал по пътя и изненадващо те е пресрещнал — често със зла умисъл, например да те нападне или ограби.
explanationEn: Stopped by someone who was waiting on your way, often to attack or rob you.
exampleEn: On my way to the canteen I was waylaid by classmates who wanted to copy my homework.
